cna.title: MISP CSS Injection via Remote Tag Colour in Event Preview

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [sync] Only use a valid colour for remote tags in the

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [sync] Only use a valid colour for remote tags in the
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix introduces strict validation of the tag colour value before it is rendered into a CSS style attribute. Only values matching a valid six-digit hexadecimal colour pattern (e.g. #aabbcc) are accepted; any other value is replaced with a safe default (#ffffff). This prevents arbitrary CSS from being injected through the colour field, aligning the remote tag handling with the validation already applied to local tags.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48, 27 commits after fix); the exact first affected version is not stated in the patch.
PR:L assumes that creating or modifying a tag on a linked MISP server requires only low-level user privileges; the exact permission model was not verified from the patch.
SC:L assumes CSS injection could enable limited client-side information disclosure (e.g., via CSS selectors or layout manipulation); full XSS or data exfiltration is not evidenced.
CAPEC-66 is the closest available mapping; no CAPEC specifically models CSS injection via trusted inter-instance data, so this mapping carries uncertainty.
The commit message states the issue was found during internal review and not externally reported; no external finder or reporter is credited.
The Co-Authored-By line references an AI tool (Claude Opus 5.5); it is credited as a tool rather than a human remediation developer.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/View/Servers/preview_event.ctp, a regex check (preg_match against /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i) is added before the tag colour is used. If the colour does not match the hex pattern, it defaults to #ffffff. The validated $colour variable replaces the raw $tag['colour'] in both the background-color style property and the getTextColour() call, eliminating the untrusted value from the CSS context.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N – the attack originates from a remote linked MISP server over the network. AC:L – no race conditions or special timing; simply setting a tag colour suffices. AT:N – no manipulation of the attack target is required. PR:L – the attacker needs low-privilege access (tag creation) on the linked server. UI:A – the victim must actively navigate to the event preview page. VC:N – no direct confidentiality loss on the vulnerable system. VI:N – no integrity impact on the vulnerable system's data. VA:N – no availability impact. SC:L – CSS injection may allow limited information disclosure on the client (e.g., reading page structure via CSS selectors or side channels). SI:L – the attacker can modify the visual presentation of the preview page (UI manipulation, overlay, spoofing). SA:N – no security authority impact.

capecRationale.rationale: The attack exploits the inherent trust between linked MISP instances. The local instance accepts and renders data (tag colours) from a remote linked server without sufficient validation, assuming the data is well-formed. The attacker leverages this trusted relationship to inject CSS. This is the closest CAPEC; no CAPEC specifically models CSS injection via trusted data sources, so CAPEC-66 is the best available match.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The tag colour value is not neutralized for the CSS context in which it is placed. HTML entity encoding (h()) does not sanitize CSS metacharacters such as semicolons, colons, or function calls, allowing CSS injection. CWE-74 is the most precise parent weakness covering injection into a downstream component (CSS) without a more specific child CWE for CSS injection.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a CSS injection vulnerability in the remote event preview feature. When a user previews an event from a linked MISP server, the colour value associated with each remote tag is written directly into an inline CSS style attribute without sufficient validation. Although HTML entity encoding is applied, the value is interpreted as CSS within the style attribute, allowing a malicious or compromised linked server to inject arbitrary CSS declarations.

An attacker with the ability to create or modify tags on a linked MISP instance can craft a tag colour value containing CSS injection payloads. When a user on the local instance views the event preview, the injected CSS is rendered, potentially allowing UI manipulation, visual spoofing, or limited information disclosure through CSS-based techniques.

Preconditions:

- A linked MISP server relationship exists between the victim instance and the attacker-controlled instance.

- The attacker can create or modify tags on the linked server.

- A victim user views the remote event preview page.

Affected: <2.5.48.

cna.title: Ghostscript: reintroduction of .charkeys -dsafer bypass in rhel 8

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Nicholas Pettas for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-10-20) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to eliminate privileged .forceput operations in the .charkeys procedure to enforce -dSAFER sandbox boundaries: upgrade to the fixed Ghostscript builds, which replace .forceput invocations with standard put operations in the /.charkeys procedure in Resource/Init/gs_ttf.ps, closing all 2 injection vectors (crafted PostScript document, malicious TrueType font processing). Until patched, this is a concern on Ghostscript on Linux (RHEL 8) processing untrusted input, such as print or document-conversion services, so Restrict or halt processing of untrusted PostScript documents and TrueType font inputs across document-conversion and printing services that invoke Ghostscript. As a compensating measure, Use auditd to log unauthorized file access attempts and unexpected execve syscalls spawned by the Ghostscript process, Run SELinux in enforcing mode to confine the Ghostscript process to a restricted domain, Use Linux mount and PID namespaces to restrict filesystem and process visibility for Ghostscript execution, Deploy an EDR agent to detect and terminate unexpected shell or child process spawns from Ghostscript, and Use Falco or eBPF runtime security to detect anomalous child process execution and unauthorized file reads. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying privileged .forceput sandbox bypass — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1002 Audit Subsystem (auditd) (medium)

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Ghostscript as shipped with Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8. The correction for CVE-2019-14869 was omitted during the rebase from version 9.25 to 9.27, leaving privileged .forceput operations in the .charkeys procedure insufficiently protected. Processing a specially crafted PostScript file may allow an attacker to bypass -dSAFER restrictions and access files outside the permitted paths or execute commands with the permissions of the Ghostscript process.

·         Delete BRAIN2 installation log files after successful installation.

·         Restrict administrative access to affected systems.

·         Ensure temporary directories containing installation artifacts are adequately protected.

descriptions.value:
A vulnerability has been identified in
BRAIN2 versions up to and including version 3.09. Under specific installation
conditions, the password of a Windows service account may be written in
cleartext to a setup log file. The issue occurs when Microsoft SQL Server
access is configured using Integrated Security and the Windows account intended
to run the BRAIN2 MainService is specified during execution of the BRAIN2
installation wizard. The setup log file is stored in the
temporary directory of the Windows administrator performing the installation.
This directory is not accessible to standard Windows users and can generally
only be accessed by users with administrative privileges. Successful exploitation could result in the
disclosure of credentials belonging to the configured BRAIN2 service account.

cna.title: Gitea Actions task token private repository enumeration

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #40115

descriptions.value: Gitea Actions task tokens authenticate to the REST API as a shared system user with a negative ID, which repository, organization, project and key filters treated as having no owner restriction, and the token carried no API scope to restrict user-scoped routes. A user who can run a workflow could use the job's token with `GET /api/v1/user/repos` to list every repository on the instance, including private repositories of other users and organizations, with their metadata. Repository contents remained protected by per-repository permission checks. System users now own nothing, and `/api/v1/user` routes other than `GET /api/v1/user` accept only individual and bot accounts.

descriptions.description: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

cna.title: Pillow: Infinite loop in PdfParser.rewrite_pages on page tree Parent cycle

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.1.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow can enter an infinite loop while rewriting PDF pages. PdfParser.rewrite_pages() follows Parent relationships without detecting a cycle in the page tree. An attacker can supply a cyclic PDF to an application that appends an image to that PDF. This can hold the worker at full CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Pillow: Quadratic-time DoS in PDF save_all (PdfParser.next_object_id)

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.1.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow takes quadratic time to reserve PDF object identifiers when saving many frames with save_all enabled. PdfParser.next_object_id() repeatedly rebuilds and scans all previously reserved identifiers for every object. An attacker can supply a multi-frame image, including a small APNG with a large declared frame count, to an application that converts it to a multipage PDF. This can consume excessive CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: login-failure upsert trusts mysql/mariadb affected-row count

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Semih Doğan for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the login-failure storage component of Keycloak, the identity and access management solution. This issue specifically affects deployments using MySQL or MariaDB databases in a multi-node configuration. When multiple failed login attempts occur simultaneously for the same account, a synchronization error can cause the system to enter a repetitive loop that locks the user's record in the database. This results in legitimate login attempts for that user being blocked and failing with an error. Furthermore, because some failures are not correctly recorded during this loop, the system's brute-force protection may not accurately count all failed attempts.

descriptions.description: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization

cna.title: Apache Texera: Missing authentication on the Python virtual environment endpoints in non-Kubernetes deployments

descriptions.description: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function

descriptions.value:
Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating).



The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated by the application itself. In the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments, which place no authenticating gateway in front of the services, these endpoints are reachable without credentials. The Kubernetes deployment gates them at the gateway, so only the Kubernetes deployment provides the full security model described in SECURITY.md.



This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to use the Kubernetes deployment, which enforces the full security model, and to upgrade to 1.3.0-incubating, which documents that the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

cna.title: filelock: On Windows an oplock on a soft lock's marker holds SoftFileLock.acquire() past its timeout and blocks the stale break

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.22.0 until 4.2.1, soft lock classes on Windows read an existing marker with _read_lock_file and remove a stale marker through break_lock_file using pathname operations that wait for an oplock break. Another local account with read access to an unheld marker can keep a Level 1 or batch oplock unanswered, causing SoftFileLock.acquire and related async or fallback locks to wait beyond timeout, blocking=False, and cancel_check. A stale marker under the oplock cannot be broken, but mutual exclusion remains intact and no file other than the marker is accessed. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

This issue is fixed in iOS 26.7.2 and iPadOS 26.7.2, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, macOS Sequoia 15.8.2, macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, tvOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2. cna.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in OpenKM Community Edition

solutions.value:
Update OpenKM CE 7.0.3 to 7.0.4, which has already been released. According to the manufacturer, the entity resolver has been fixed, and general and parameter external entities have been disabled by enabling FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING. For versions 6.3.3 through 6.3.13, the fix will be included in 6.3.14, which is pending release; HTTP requests for non-local DTDs have also been removed.


As a temporary measure to restrict access to the workflow, the vendor recommends blocking non-administrator users from accessing /OpenKM/services/rest/workflow/* and /OpenKM/services/OKMWorkflow on the reverse proxy or firewall. If the web services are not in use, block the entire /OpenKM/services/* directory.



The manufacturer recommends migrating to OpenKM CE 7.0.4. Before migrating from 6.3.x, please note that 7.x does not include the jBPM workflow engine.

descriptions.value: Vulnerability due to inadequate restriction of references to external XML entities in OpenKM Community Edition. cna.title: Kirki WordPress Plugin < 6.4.1 Broken Object-Level Access Control via Page API

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Kirki WordPress Plugin < 6.4.1 Broken Object-Level Access Control via Page API

descriptions.value: Kirki plugin for WordPress before 6.4.1 contains a broken object-level access control vulnerability in its page REST API, where the PUT /wp-json/kirki/v1/pages/{page_id} route and the save_page_data, duplicate, and delete handlers in PageController.php rely only on a coarse role-to-access middleware check without performing a per-object WordPress capability check. A user with Kirki edit access, granted to the Editor role by default, can exploit this flaw to modify the title, slug, and publication status of any non-trashed post of any post type, including custom post types and WooCommerce products they do not own, exposing private or draft content or removing published content by manipulating the unrestricted post_status field.

cna.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information on the UOC Virtual Campus

solutions.value: No solution has been reported at this time.

supportingMedia.value: No solution has been reported at this time.

descriptions.value: Vulnerability involving the exposure of sensitive information in the URLs of the UOC Virtual Campus’s document upload feature. After completing a document upload, the application includes identifiers related to the active session—such as `apjsessionid`—and other internal parameters associated with requests and users in the HTTP GET request parameters. This data may be stored in the browser history and in server or proxy logs, or transmitted via the HTTP Referer header, depending on the configuration and browsing flow. Its inclusion in the URL could allow for the unauthorized disclosure of information to third parties with access to those logs or recipients.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-88 OS Command Injection

A command injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated site administrator to execute arbitrary commands as the host git user on peer Git server nodes outside the pre-receive hook sandbox by supplying a crafted pre-receive environment download URL. Exploitation required a clustered deployment using custom pre-receive hook environments and at least one peer Git server node. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, 3.20.12, and 3.19.16. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix enforces the distribution level constraint in the sharing group access check, requiring distribution level 4 (All communities) for the sharing group test to apply. Additionally, the owning organisation is now explicitly granted access to proposals on its own attributes regardless of distribution level, correcting the over-restrictive behavior.
assumptions: The CAPEC mapping (CAPEC-2, Parameter Tampering) is the closest available match but is uncertain; the vulnerability is more accurately a missing authorization check (incomplete ACL evaluation) rather than active parameter manipulation by the attacker.
The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag v2.5.48 and the commit position (35 commits after the fix); exact version boundaries are not explicitly stated in the patch metadata.

The second aspect of the vulnerability (owner organisation denied access to its own proposals) is primarily a functional/availability defect rather than a security vulnerability, but is included as part of the same fix and the same root cause (incomplete ACL logic).
CVSS PR:L assumes the attacker must be an authenticated MISP user with membership in a relevant sharing group; no evidence supports unauthenticated access.
The Co-Authored-By line credits an AI assistant (Claude Opus 5.5) as a remediation developer; this is recorded as-is from the commit metadata.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In the shadow attribute model's condition builder, the sharing group check for both objects and attributes now includes an AND condition requiring distribution = 4 alongside the sharing_group_id IN check. The attribute distribution condition was changed from a simple sharing_group_id IN clause to a compound AND condition with distribution = 4. A new OR condition (Event.org_id matching the user's org_id) was added to grant the owning organisation access to proposals on its own attributes.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: MISP is a network-accessible web application. AC:L: The user only needs to be a member of a sharing group; no special conditions or race conditions are required. AT:N: No active attack requirements beyond normal API usage. PR:L: The attacker must be an authenticated user with membership in a relevant sharing group. UI:N: No user interaction is required; the check is server-side. VC:H: The user can view proposals (proposed attribute changes) that should be restricted by distribution level, disclosing sensitive information about proposed changes. VI:N: No integrity impact; the user cannot modify proposals. VA:N: No availability impact. SC/SI/SA:N: No impact on subsequent components.

capecRationale.rationale: The user's sharing group membership (a parameter of their identity/session) was leveraged by the flawed authorization logic to grant access to proposals without the required distribution level check. This is the closest available CAPEC pattern; the user is not actively tampering with parameters, but the system improperly treats group membership as a sufficient access parameter without enforcing the additional distribution constraint. The mapping is uncertain because the vulnerability is more accurately a missing authorization check than active parameter manipulation.

MISP contains an access control flaw in the proposal (shadow attribute) visibility logic. The authorization check accepted any attribute or object carrying one of the user's sharing groups without verifying the distribution level, and denied the owning organisation access to proposals on its own organisation-only attributes.

cna.title: Pillow: NULL dereference in ImagingExpand via rank filters on zero-size images

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's rank-based filters can dereference invalid image storage for a zero-size image. ImagingExpand() allocates a non-empty output and then faults while replicating edges by reading the first pixel from empty input storage; ImagingRankFilter is never reached. An attacker can supply or cause creation of a zero-size image to an application that applies a rank, median, minimum, or maximum filter. This causes a native process crash. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The event deletion routine was extended to cascade-remove all associated child records that were previously left behind. Specifically, the fix ensures that event report tags, event graph rows, shadow attribute correlation rows (on both event_id and 1_event_id foreign keys), fuzzy ssdeep chunks, and attachment scan results are all purged within the same transaction as the parent event deletion, eliminating the orphaned-data condition.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48 with 33 commits after fix); the exact fixed release version is not specified in the patch.

The CAPEC-126 mapping is the closest available match; the vulnerability is fundamentally an incomplete cleanup defect rather than a classic state-transition exploit, so the mapping carries uncertainty.

The confidentiality impact is assessed as None because the patch does not demonstrate that orphaned records are accessible to unauthorized users; the primary concern is data integrity and retention policy.
The commit message states the issue was 'found during the internal review, not externally reported,' so no external finder or reporter is credited.
The CVSS assumes the orphaned data is not directly queryable by other users through existing MISP endpoints; if such access paths exist, the confidentiality impact could be higher.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Event.php, the quickDelete method was modified to: (1) add event_graph and shadow_attribute_correlations (both event_id and 1_event_id) to the relations array used for raw DELETE statements; (2) before executing the raw deletes, query for the IDs of event reports and for attribute/shadow-attribute IDs of type 'attachment' or 'malware-sample'; (3) delete EventReportTag rows matching those report IDs; (4) delete AttachmentScan rows matching those attribute IDs; (5) invoke FuzzyCorrelateSsdeep::purge() to remove ssdeep chunks for the event. All operations occur within the existing database transaction.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: The vulnerability is in a web-based application (AV:N) and requires a straightforward authenticated action (AC:L, AT:N). Deleting events requires elevated privileges (PR:H). No user interaction is needed (UI:N). The primary impact is on the integrity of the vulnerable system's data store: orphaned records persist that should have been removed (VI:L). There is no direct confidentiality impact on the vulnerable system itself because the data was already accessible to the deleting user, and no evidence shows the orphans are exposed to other users (VC:N). No availability impact is demonstrated (VA:N). No impact on subsequent systems (SC:N, SI:N, SA:N).

capecRationale.rationale: The event object transitions to a 'deleted' state, but related child objects (report tags, correlations, scan results, ssdeep chunks) do not follow the expected state transition and remain in an active/persisted state. An attacker with delete privileges could exploit this by creating events with sensitive associated data, deleting the event, and then attempting to access the orphaned records through other application endpoints. This is the closest CAPEC to the observed incomplete state propagation; the mapping is uncertain because the primary issue is a maintenance/cleanup defect rather than a directly exploitable state machine flaw.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The event deletion logic failed to remove all associated child records (report tags, graphs, correlations, ssdeep chunks, scan results), leaving them as orphans in the database. This is a textbook incomplete cleanup of related resources when a parent object is destroyed.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a data integrity flaw in its event deletion logic. When a user deletes an event, several associated records are not removed from the database, leaving them as orphaned entries. The affected record types include event report tags, event graph entries, proposal (shadow attribute) correlations, fuzzy ssdeep correlation chunks, and attachment scan results.

These orphaned records may contain sensitive threat intelligence data such as correlation mappings, scan results, and report metadata that should have been removed along with the parent event. Their persistence beyond the intended deletion lifecycle creates a risk of unintended data retention and potential information exposure if the records are reachable through other application queries or administrative interfaces.

Preconditions:

- An authenticated user with sufficient privileges to delete events in MISP.

- The event must have associated reports, graphs, correlations, ssdeep chunks, or attachment scan results.

Impact:

- Residual sensitive data persists in the database after the parent event is deleted.

- Accumulation of orphaned records over time may contribute to storage bloat.

- Orphaned records may be inadvertently exposed through other data-access paths that do not validate the existence of the parent event.

Affected versions: <2.5.48

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix applies HTML output encoding (the h() helper) to the parameter name before it is used as a form label, ensuring that any HTML metacharacters in the value are neutralized and rendered as inert text rather than executable markup.
assumptions: The misp-modules service is assumed to be a component whose output can be influenced by a module developer or a compromised service endpoint; the exact attack vector for injecting a malicious parameter name is not detailed in the patch.
MISP requires authentication to access the workflow module page; PR:L is assumed based on MISP's standard access model.
The affected version boundary (< 2.5.48) is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48, 25 commits after fix); the exact first affected version is not specified.
CAPEC-1 (Reflected XSS) is the closest match; the data source is a backend service rather than a direct request parameter, but the unencoded reflection into HTML is the defining characteristic.
The h() function is assumed to be CakePHP's HTML-encoding helper (equivalent to htmlspecialchars), based on the framework context of the MISP codebase.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/WorkflowModules/Module_misp_module.php, the translateParams method was modified: the 'label' array element changed from Inflector::humanize($paramName) to h(Inflector::humanize($paramName)), wrapping the humanized parameter name in CakePHP's HTML-encoding function before it is assigned as a form label.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N – web-based, reachable over the network. AC:L – no race or special timing; the misp-modules service simply needs to return a crafted parameter name. AT:N – no manipulation of the target system required. PR:L – the victim must be an authenticated MISP user to view the workflow module page. UI:A – the victim must actively load the workflow module page for the script to execute. VC/VI/VA:N – the MISP server itself is not compromised. SC:L – the attacker can read cookies or session data in the victim's browser. SI:L – the attacker can modify the page or perform actions in the victim's session. SA:N – no elevation of security authority on the server.

capecRationale.rationale: The misp-modules service supplies parameter names that are reflected into the HTML of the workflow module page without encoding. The attacker-controlled data flows from an external source into the rendered output, matching the reflected XSS pattern. Uncertainty: the data originates from a backend service rather than a direct HTTP parameter, but the effect (untrusted data reflected into HTML without encoding) is functionally identical to reflected XSS.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The parameter name from an external service is inserted into HTML output (a form label) without HTML encoding, allowing injected markup or script to execute in the victim's browser. This is a textbook reflected XSS.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the workflow module interface. Parameter names returned by the misp-modules service are rendered as raw HTML form labels on the workflow module page without output encoding. An attacker who can influence the parameter names reported by the misp-modules service can inject arbitrary HTML or JavaScript that executes in the context of an authenticated MISP user's browser.

Preconditions:

- The attacker must be able to control or influence parameter names reported by the misp-modules service.

- A victim must be authenticated and view the affected workflow module page.

Impact:

- Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session.

- Potential theft of session tokens, manipulation of the MISP interface, or initiation of unauthorized actions on behalf of the victim.

Affected versions: <2.5.48.

descriptions.description: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
CWE-88: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.6.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow is vulnerable to argument injection when invoking Ghostscript for EPS input. EpsImagePlugin.Ghostscript passes a caller-controlled input filename after -f without converting it to a safe absolute path, so a name beginning with a hyphen can be interpreted as a Ghostscript option. An attacker who controls the filename can inject Ghostscript arguments. Arbitrary command execution specifically requires a leading @ argument-file filename and control of the referenced text file containing additional Ghostscript arguments; the reported chain reproduces with the default -dSAFER invocation. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Vite: Cross origin script execution through Vite custom middleware

descriptions.value: Vite is a frontend tooling framework for JavaScript. Prior to 6.4.4, 7.3.7, 8.1.6, 8.2.4, and 8.3.3, applications using custom middleware are vulnerable when they pass an unchanged browser request URL to server.transformIndexHtml. getHtmlFilename uses the query-bearing request URL to resolve an existing local file while preserving attacker-supplied leading slashes in the generated proxy module URL. If the transformed HTML contains an inline module script and a victim browser loads the crafted development-server page, the leading double slash makes the browser fetch and execute an attacker-controlled module in the Vite-served page. This execution can expose sensitive page data or permit critical actions available to the affected application. This issue is fixed in versions 6.4.4, 7.3.7, 8.1.6, 8.2.4, and 8.3.3.

cna.title: filelock: SoftFileLock stale-lock break removes a live lock file on a reused inode number and admits two holders

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.22.0 until 4.2.1, SoftFileLock can break a stale marker after an attacker frees its own marker following the stale read, an honest contender creates a live successor on the reused inode, and the successor's modification time is not newer than the saved observation, causing the live marker to be removed and two holders to be admitted. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

An authenticated user, or anyone holding that user's session token, can send POST requests to /sessions or /classes/_Session to create additional sessions for that user and add fields to _Session; these sessions are not revoked when the original session is logged out.

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 4.1.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow's MSP RLE decoder can expand a small file into an unbounded in-memory buffer. The decoder writes run-length output to BytesIO without limiting expansion to the declared image size. An attacker can supply a crafted MSP image to an application that loads its pixels. This can exhaust memory and deny service even when the declared pixel count passes the decompression-bomb check. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Vite: First 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting is exposed by `?vite-wasm-instance`

descriptions.value: Vite is a frontend tooling framework for JavaScript. From 8.2.0 until 8.2.4 and 8.3.3, the first 4 bytes of files outside of server.fs setting can be returned to the browser by a request containing ?vite-wasm-instance. Requests containing the ?vite-wasm-instance query are handled by the internal Wasm plugin's load hook. The hook removes the query and reads the resulting path directly from disk, but the server.fs checks were not applied. After reading the file, Vite attempts to parse it as WebAssembly. When that parse fails, Node and deno throws an error that contains the first 4 bytes of the file. This vulnerability is fixed in 8.2.4 and 8.3.3.

descriptions.value: launch-editor allows users to open files with line numbers in editor from Node.js. cna.title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: account takeover via stale sso_auth note in organization identity-first login

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank LHeiakim for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to ensure the SSO_AUTH re-authentication note is cleared from the authentication session whenever a flow transition strips the authenticated user: upgrade to Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.6.8 (or the fixed Rhbk/Keycloak Rhel/Keycloak Services builds), which clears the lingering SSO_AUTH re-authentication note from the authentication session during login flow transitions such as registration or credential reset, closing all 2 injection vectors (transition to credential reset flow, transition to registration flow). Until patched, this is a concern on Keycloak deployments with the Organization feature enabled and users holding credentials in multiple organizations, so Disable the Organization feature or ensure users cannot hold memberships across multiple organizations. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying stale authentication state flag defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Organization identity-first login flow of the Keycloak authentication server. Keycloak is an open-source identity and access management solution used to secure modern applications and services. The issue occurs when an attacker who belongs to multiple organizations initiates a login and then switches to a registration or password reset path. During this process, a flag indicating a successful login is not properly cleared when the user is removed from the session. An attacker can then provide a victim's username, and the system incorrectly treats the stale flag as proof of the victim's identity. This allows the attacker to bypass authentication and gain full access to the victim's account and connected applications.

cna.title: vault-java-driver: stored deeply nested JSON kills every thread that reads it

credits.value: Yuval Saggie and Mor Wienberger (powered by Echo Frontier)

descriptions.value: CAPEC-230 Serialized Data with Nested Payloads

solutions.value: Upgrade io.github.jopenlibs:vault-java-driver to 7.0.0 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade io.github.jopenlibs:vault-java-driver to 7.0.0 or later.

descriptions.value: vault-java-driver, a Java client for HashiCorp Vault, parses Vault's JSON responses with a vendored minimal-json parser that has no nesting depth limit. A deeply nested value raises a StackOverflowError, which escapes catch (Exception) handlers and kills the reading thread. A Vault token that can write but not read a KV v2 path can store such a value there, so every later read of that path through the driver fails. This requires Vault 1.19.x or earlier, because 1.20 and later reject values nested deeper than 298 levels. This issue affects io.github.jopenlibs:vault-java-driver 5.2.0 through 6.2.3 and is fixed in 7.0.0.

workarounds.value:

    systemctl stop rhc-canonical-facts.timer

cna.title: Pillow: TiffDecode returns uninitialized memory as pixels for short JPEG strips

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.3.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow can return uninitialized memory as pixels when libtiff performs a short decode of JPEG-compressed or Group 4 fax TIFF data. The _decodeStrip and _decodeTile buffers can be larger than the bytes written by libtiff, but Pillow converts the expected rows without clearing the unwritten tail. The tile path is affected from 5.3.0 and the strip path from 6.0.0. An attacker can supply a crafted TIFF to an application that loads and returns or re-encodes its pixels. This can disclose stale heap contents without memory corruption or a process crash. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

solutions.value:

As a temporary measure to restrict access to the workflow, the vendor recommends blocking non-administrator users from accessing /OpenKM/services/rest/workflow/* and /OpenKM/services/OKMWorkflow on the reverse proxy or firewall. If the web services are not in use, block the entire /OpenKM/services/* directory.



The manufacturer recommends migrating to OpenKM CE 7.0.4. Before migrating from 6.3.x, please note that 7.x does not include the jBPM workflow engine.

descriptions.value: Unauthorization vulnerability in the management of workflow definitions in OpenKM Community Edition. cna.title: Pillow: Quadratic GIF comment concatenation allows DoS in Image.open()

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 5.4.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow performs quadratic copying while parsing GIF comments. cna.title: Pillow: OOB read in TiffDecode.c tile and RGBA paths leaks heap memory into pixels

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 8.1.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow's TIFF tile and RGBA decode paths can read beyond row data produced by libtiff. In _decodeTile and the RGBA unpacker path, when Pillow and libtiff interpret duplicated PhotometricInterpretation or BitsPerSample tags differently, Pillow does not verify that the required input row fits inside the row libtiff produced, while the strip path has this validation. Loading pixels from such a crafted TIFF can expose adjacent heap data in output pixels or crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

descriptions.value: An IPv6 FlowSpec validation bypass in the CZ.NIC BIRD Internet Routing Daemon allows an established BGP peer to inject FlowSpec rules matching destinations outside the address space authorized by the unicast-route validation procedure. With validation enabled on the receiving flow6 channel, BIRD fails to reject a destination prefix component with a nonzero offset, contrary to RFC 8956 section 5. It validates a reconstructed prefix with zero-filled skipped bits, although the original FlowSpec component can match a broader set of IPv6 addresses. Given a suitable unicast route from the peer, the rule can pass validation and, where export policy permits, be propagated to downstream peers. Downstream enforcement may cause unauthorized traffic filtering or redirection.

descriptions.description: CWE-1284 Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input

configurations.value: An established BGP peer must be able to send IPv6 FlowSpec to a receiving flow6 channel configured with "validate yes". A suitable unicast route from that peer must be present in the base table. Propagation additionally requires an export policy permitting the rule. Data-plane impact depends on downstream support for, acceptance of, and enforcement of the FlowSpec match and action.

cna.title: Pillow tiled-TIFF decoder reads past tile buffer in copy4 (Unpack.c:1290)

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 8.2.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow's tiled-TIFF decoder can read past the tile buffer while copying four-byte pixels. In _decodeTile, libtiff can return a tile allocation smaller than the required row stride multiplied by the tile length, and Pillow's stride-and-copy loop walks beyond that allocation. An attacker can supply a crafted tiled TIFF to an application that loads it. This can expose adjacent heap data in pixels or crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

ImagingRawDecode calculates a packed-pixel row size, while the unpackers read separately padded bit planes. A caller can supply a buffer and image dimensions whose accepted size is smaller than the unpacker's actual footprint. This can disclose up to three adjacent heap bytes in output pixels or crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: filelock: ReadWriteLock on Windows acts on SQLite side files another local user places beside its database

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.20.4 until 4.2.1, ReadWriteLock and AsyncReadWriteLock on Windows use _connect to attach SQLite to the lock database by pathname, allowing another local account that can create adjacent names to place a database-wal or database-journal side file before acquisition. An undeletable WAL file makes each read or write acquisition fail immediately with sqlite3.OperationalError regardless of timeout. Separately, when the database contains at least one table, a hot journal that grants the lock account modify rights can cause SQLite recovery to delete a file named by that journal only when the lock account has permission to delete the target. The issue requires a directory writable by another account, such as a shared Windows temporary directory, and does not affect private directories. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's JPEG decoder can write a full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft scale. cna.title: @fastify/express vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via absolute-form request targets

descriptions.value: @fastify/express is a Fastify plugin that runs Express middleware inside Fastify. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.8, when Fastify runs with the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option enabled, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware against a URL whose duplicate-slash normalization has also collapsed the separator after an absolute-form request target's scheme, so Fastify's router resolves the request to the scoped path and runs the handler while the Express layer no longer sees that path. As a result, a request using an absolute-form target can reach a handler on a scoped route such as an admin path while the middleware for authentication, authorization, or rate limiting is skipped. An unauthenticated attacker needs only the non-default ignoreDuplicateSlashes option to be enabled. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.9, and users should upgrade to 4.0.9 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request, or leave ignoreDuplicateSlashes at its default.

cna.title: Vvveb: Path Traversal in nextRestore() and nextBackup()

descriptions.value: Vvveb is a powerful and easy to use CMS with page builder to build websites, blogs or ecommerce stores. In versions 1.0.8.6 and prior, the nextRestore() and nextBackup() functions in the backup controller accept a file GET parameter and concatenate it directly to DIR_BACKUP without calling sanitizeFileName(). This allows an authenticated administrator to read arbitrary files on the server (via nextRestore) and write SQL dump content to arbitrary locations (via nextBackup). This is inconsistent with the sibling functions restore(), delete(), and download() which all correctly call sanitizeFileName() first. This issue has been patched via commit aa29cb0.

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix extends the BLOCKED_RANGES list in is_safe_url() to include the previously missing IP address ranges: 0.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, ::/128, fc00::/7, and fe80::/10. The existing IPv4-mapped IPv6 normalisation logic ensures that mapped forms (e.g., ::ffff:0.0.0.0) are also blocked. Regression tests are added covering both literal IP addresses in URLs and hostnames that resolve to the newly blocked ranges.
assumptions: PR:L assumes that creating or modifying a MISP attribute to trigger the html_to_markdown expansion module requires authenticated access. MISP typically enforces authentication for attribute operations, but the patch does not explicitly state the authentication model.

SC:H assumes the MISP server can reach internal services (e.g., cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, internal admin panels, or CGNAT infrastructure) and that the responses are returned to the attacker via the Markdown conversion output. The actual impact depends on the server's network topology.
The exact affected version range is not specified in the patch. The nearest tag is v3.0.13 with 139 commits after the fix, but the precise release containing the fix is not identified.
CAPEC-12 is selected as the closest match; no alternative CAPEC more precisely describes an SSRF via incomplete IP-range validation in a URL-fetching module.

The patch does not indicate whether the module follows redirects to additional unblocked ranges; MAX_REDIRECTS is set to 10, and the redirect target validation is not shown in this patch. If redirect targets are not re-validated, the SSRF surface may be broader than what this patch addresses.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In misp_modules/modules/expansion/html_to_markdown.py, five new ipaddress.ip_network() entries are added to the BLOCKED_RANGES list: 0.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, ::/128, fc00::/7, and fe80::/10. In tests/test_html_to_markdown.py, two new test methods are added: test_blocks_unspecified_shared_ula_and_link_local_literals verifies that is_safe_url() returns False for literal URLs using each blocked range (including IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms), and test_blocks_hostnames_resolving_to_ula_addresses verifies that a hostname resolving to an fc00::/7 address is rejected.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The vulnerable URL is supplied via a MISP attribute over the network. AC:L: Crafting a URL with a blocked-range IP is straightforward; no race or special timing is needed. AT:N: No manipulation of the target service is required. PR:L: Creating or modifying a MISP attribute that triggers the expansion module requires authenticated access (assumed; MISP typically requires authentication for attribute operations). UI:N: No victim interaction beyond the initial attribute creation is needed. VC:N, VI:N, VA:N: The MISP server itself is not compromised; it is used as a proxy. SC:H: The SSRF allows reading responses from internal services (e.g., cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin panels), representing a high confidentiality impact on the target system. SI:N, SA:N: The module performs a GET-style fetch for HTML-to-Markdown conversion; no evidence of write or security-impact on the target.

capecRationale.rationale: The patch directly addresses an SSRF condition: the application fetches a URL on behalf of the user, and the validation logic failed to block requests to internal and restricted IP ranges. An attacker crafts a URL with a blocked-range IP (e.g., http://0.0.0.0/admin or http://[fe80::1]/) to cause the MISP server to issue a request to an internal service. This is the canonical CAPEC-12 pattern. No uncertainty in this mapping.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The html_to_markdown module fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The incomplete IP range allow/block list permitted requests to internal, link-local, and otherwise restricted network destinations, constituting a classic SSRF.

The is_safe_url() function's BLOCKED_RANGES list was incomplete, failing to validate against all non-routable and internally significant IP address ranges. This is the root-cause input validation deficiency enabling the SSRF.

descriptions.value:
The html_to_markdown expansion module in MISP Modules contains a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its is_safe_url() URL validation function. The BLOCKED_RANGES list used to reject unsafe destination addresses was incomplete, omitting several critical IP address ranges. Specifically, the following ranges were not blocked: 0.0.0.0/8 (unspecified, which routes to loopback on Linux), 100.64.0.0/10 (carrier-grade NAT per RFC 6598), ::/128 (IPv6 unspecified), fc00::/7 (IPv6 Unique Local Addresses), and fe80::/10 (IPv6 link-local). The existing list only covered IPv4 loopback (127.0.0.0/8), RFC 1918 private ranges, IPv4 link-local (169.254.0.0/16), and IPv6 loopback (::1/128).

An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify MISP attributes that trigger the html_to_markdown expansion module could supply URLs pointing to these unblocked internal address ranges. Because the module fetches the URL server-side to convert HTML content to Markdown, the request is made from the MISP server's network context. This allows an attacker to probe and read responses from internal services, carrier-grade NAT infrastructure, or link-local endpoints that would otherwise be unreachable from external networks. IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms (e.g., [::ffff:0.0.0.0]) also bypassed the existing checks.

The security impact is primarily confidentiality: an attacker can read data served by internal services reachable from the MISP server. The MISP instance itself is not compromised, but it is abused as a proxy to access otherwise restricted network resources.

This allows an attacker to probe and read responses from internal services, carrier-grade NAT infrastructure, or link-local endpoints that would otherwise be unreachable from external networks. IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms (e.g., [::ffff:0.0.0.0]) also bypassed the existing checks.

The security impact is primarily confidentiality: an attacker can read data served by internal services reachable from the MISP server. The MISP instance itself is not compromised, but it is abused as a proxy to access otherwise restricted network resources.

cna.title: webpack-dev-server vulnerable to cross-origin WebSocket access via proxied upgrades

descriptions.value: webpack-dev-server is a development server that provides live reloading for webpack projects. In versions before 5.2.7 and in version 6.0.0, when a proxy entry is configured to forward WebSockets, the server forwards non-HMR WebSocket upgrade requests to the proxy target without validating the Host or Origin headers, so the allowedHosts protection does not apply to those proxied upgrades. A malicious web page visited by a developer can open a cross-origin WebSocket through the dev server and read from and write to the proxied backend, even when the server is bound to loopback. The issue is fixed in webpack-dev-server 5.2.7 and 6.1.0, where proxied WebSocket upgrades pass the same Host and Origin validation as the HMR WebSocket, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, omit WebSocket forwarding from proxy entries that do not need it and scope the proxy to specific paths.

cna.title: Apache Kafka: Unauthorized principal can read arbitrary broker files via IncrementalAlterConfigs

credits.value: Arthur Chan <arthur.chan@adalogics.com>, Ada Logics and Anthropic Research
OpenAI Codex Security - Amy Burnett and Khai Tran

descriptions.value:
An authenticated Kafka principal with no authorization grants (not even ALTER_CONFIGS) can make a broker read a file or an environment variable from the broker host and return its contents. An IncrementalAlterConfigs (or AlterConfigs) request targeting a BROKER resource reaches the broker's configuration validation before any authorization check is applied to that path. Validation resolves configuration variables such as ${file:/path:key} or ${env:VAR} using a ConfigProvider named in the request, and this resolution bypasses the org.apache.kafka.automatic.config.providers allowlist that was added as the mitigation for CVE-2024-31141. An arbitrary ConfigProvider (for example FileConfigProvider or EnvVarConfigProvider) is therefore instantiated and the referenced file or environment variable is read, and a type-validation error returns the resolved content to the caller.


Impact:

On a cluster with an authorizer enabled, an authenticated principal with no authorization grants can read the contents of files accessible to the broker process, and the broker's environment variables, exposing credentials, keystores, or other secrets, defeating the CVE-2024-31141 allowlist. The read is bounded by the broker process's file permissions. The brokers and the cluster remain available; the issue is disclosure of file and environment- variable contents. Clusters with no authorizer configured are not affected in practice, because every principal already holds ALTER_CONFIGS there.


Mitigation:

Upgrade to Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0. As defense in depth, run brokers under a least-privileged operating-system account so that sensitive files are not readable by the broker process.


Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: broker configuration changes are authorized (ALTER_CONFIGS on the cluster) before the configuration is validated, and configuration- variable resolution enforces the config-providers allowlist.

cna.title: filelock: WindowsFileLock ignores mode: a 0o600 lock file and the ReadWriteLock database inherit the directory ACL

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.10.0 until 4.2.1, filelock on Windows ignores the mode argument for WindowsFileLock files and the ReadWriteLock SQLite database. A lock created with mode=0o600 receives the parent directory's inheritable ACL because _open_non_reparse_fd and _nt_open do not create an owner-only security descriptor. Another local account with inherited access can read holder metadata or the lock database, modify those files where the ACL permits writes, or take the byte-range lock after release and delay later acquisitions. UnixFileLock is not affected, and mutual exclusion between cooperating processes continues to hold. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [settings] Server setting lookups address one setting,

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [settings] Server setting lookups address one setting,
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The settings lookup function now validates that the resolved node is a leaf setting (has a 'level' property and is not an array representing a branch). If the resolved node is a branch or otherwise does not represent a single setting, the function returns false, indicating an invalid setting. This prevents the redaction check from being bypassed and stops the endpoints from returning entire configuration branches containing sensitive values.
assumptions: The exact privilege level required to access the server settings endpoints (admin vs. any authenticated user) is not stated in the patch; PR:L is assumed as the most conservative defensible value.

The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48 with 11 commits after fix); the exact last affected version and first fixed version are not explicitly confirmed.
CAPEC-124 (Parameter Tampering) is the closest available attack pattern; no CAPEC specifically models configuration-tree branch traversal, so the mapping is approximate.
The patch does not indicate whether unauthenticated access is possible; authentication is assumed based on the nature of server settings endpoints in MISP.
The Co-Authored-By line references an AI tool (Claude Opus 5); it is listed as a tool credit rather than a human remediation developer.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Server.php, the getSettingData() method previously checked only for the presence of a 'level' key before returning the setting. The patch adds a guard clause: if the resolved setting is an array (i.e., a branch/sub-tree) or lacks the 'level' key, the function immediately returns false. The existing logic for setting the name and resolving options is then applied only to confirmed leaf settings. This ensures callers that assumed a single-setting result never receive a multi-key branch.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: MISP is a network-accessible web application. AC:L: The attack requires only substituting a branch name for a leaf setting name in an existing API call; no race conditions or complex timing are needed. AT:N: No manipulation of the target environment is required. PR:L: The attacker needs an authenticated account with access to the server settings endpoints; the exact privilege level (admin vs. regular user) is not confirmed in the patch, so Low is assumed. UI:N: No victim interaction is required. VC:H: Sensitive secrets (security salt, Redis passwords, plugin API keys) are fully disclosed. VI:N, VA:N: No integrity or availability impact is evidenced. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N: No impact on subsequent components is indicated.

capecRationale.rationale: The attacker manipulates the setting name parameter supplied to the settings lookup endpoint, substituting a branch name (e.g., 'Security') for a leaf setting name. This causes the application to return a broader data set than intended. CAPEC-124 is the closest match because the core technique is altering a request parameter to change the application's response scope. The mapping is approximate because the parameter is not a traditional HTTP parameter but an application-level setting identifier; no CAPEC specifically covers configuration-tree traversal.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The settings endpoint returned sensitive configuration values (security salt, Redis passwords, plugin API keys) to a caller who requested a branch name, bypassing the intended redaction mechanism. The data was exposed to an actor who should not have had access to those specific values.

The redaction check, which serves as an authorization control for sensitive setting values, was effectively bypassed because branch nodes do not carry a redacted flag. The system failed to enforce the intended access restriction on sensitive configuration data.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a vulnerability in its server settings lookup mechanism that allows an authenticated user to retrieve sensitive configuration data that should have been redacted.

The settings lookup function resolves a dotted setting name to a node in the configuration tree. When a branch name (such as Security, MISP, or Plugin) is supplied instead of a specific leaf setting, the function returns the entire sub-tree. Because a branch node does not carry a redaction flag, the redaction check in the settings retrieval endpoint is bypassed, and the full branch contents are returned to the caller. This exposes sensitive values including the security salt, Redis connection passwords, and plugin API keys.

A second endpoint that edits server settings similarly reads the entire configuration store when a branch name is resolved, returning all settings to the caller.

The impact is disclosure of sensitive server configuration secrets to any user who can access the server settings endpoints.

Affected versions: <2.5.48.

references.name: VDB-421756 | radareorg radare2 HTTP Sandbox Policy rtr_http.inc.c r_core_cmd_str_pipe protection mechanism
Submit #1009600 | radareorg radare2 up to 6.2.2 OS Command Injection

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was detected in radareorg radare2 6.2.0/6.2.2. This issue affects the function r_core_cmd_str_pipe in the library libr/core/rtr_http.inc.c of the component HTTP Sandbox Policy Handler. Performing a manipulation results in protection mechanism failure. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The attack is considered to have high complexity. The exploitability is assessed as difficult. Upgrading to version 6.2.4 is capable of addressing this issue. The patch is named 18fd12efa98a7d1977de7bdd379d8a848777b90f. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The pre-requisite of the vulnerability is reflected by the CVSS vector. One of the project maintainers explains: "There is a real sandbox configuration issue here, but the report overstates it. The HTTP server defaults to http.sandbox=true, so commands received through /cmd temporarily enable cfg.sandbox. However, cfg.sandbox.grain defaults to all, which means all sandbox capabilities - including exec - remain allowed. Therefore enabling the HTTP sandbox alone does NOT prevent commands from spawning processes. This only matters when the HTTP command endpoint is reachable by someone you do not trust. It is not a remote vulnerability by default: the HTTP server must first be started and exposed to the attacker."

cna.title: MISP Event Synchronization Exposes Non-Exportable Tags on Remote Instances

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [sync] Filter the tags of every event report pushed to a

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [sync] Filter the tags of every event report pushed to a
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The non-exportable tag filtering is now invoked for each individual event report within the iteration loop, ensuring that restricted tags are removed from every report before it is transmitted to the remote MISP instance. This prevents the leakage of tags that were explicitly marked as non-exportable.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (v2.5.48 with 34 commits after fix), suggesting the fix is included in v2.5.48 and prior versions are affected. No explicit version range is stated in the patch.
PR:L assumes that a non-admin authenticated user with push-to-remote permissions can trigger the sync; if only administrators can initiate sync, PR should be raised to H.
The CAPEC-128 mapping is uncertain; no CAPEC pattern precisely describes a per-item filtering logic error causing data leakage during a legitimate operation.
The security impact is assessed as limited to tag disclosure; the actual sensitivity of 'non-exportable' tags depends on MISP deployment configuration and is not specified in the patch.
The availability impact (null report push causing remote save failure) is considered minor and not reflected in the CVSS vector as the primary concern is information disclosure.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Event.php, the call to __removeNonExportableTags was moved from a single post-loop invocation (which used the last $key value from the foreach) into the else branch of the loop body, so it executes for each non-empty report individually. The post-loop else block that applied the filter to a single report was removed, eliminating both the tag-leakage bug and the null-report push when the last report was empty.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The vulnerability is triggered over the network during MISP-to-MISP synchronization. AC:L: No special conditions are needed beyond a configured sync relationship and an event with multiple reports. AT:N: No attacker interaction is required; the bug triggers on any sync push. PR:L: An authenticated user with permission to push events to a remote server is required. UI:N: No user interaction beyond initiating the sync. VC:L: Non-exportable tags (restricted metadata) are disclosed to the remote instance; the core event data is not exposed. VI:N, VA:N: No integrity or availability impact on the local instance. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N: No impact on the remote instance's confidentiality, integrity, or availability beyond receiving the tags it should not have.

capecRationale.rationale: This is the closest available CAPEC pattern. The vulnerability arises from a code logic error that causes data (non-exportable tags) to be improperly exposed during a legitimate sync operation. The mapping is uncertain because the issue is a logic bug in data filtering rather than a deliberate attacker action; no CAPEC pattern precisely covers 'improper per-item filtering in a loop causing data leakage during a legitimate API operation.'

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: Tags explicitly marked as non-exportable were not filtered from event reports during synchronization, exposing restricted information to the remote MISP instance. The root cause is a logic error (filter applied once instead of per-item), but the security consequence is information disclosure.

descriptions.value:
In MISP, the event synchronization process contained a logic error in the preparation of event reports for remote push. The filtering of non-exportable tags was applied only once after the iteration over all reports, rather than to each individual report.

As a result:

- All reports except the last one in the set were pushed to the remote MISP instance with their non-exportable tags intact, effectively disclosing restricted tag information to the receiving instance.

- When the last report in the set was withheld (empty), a null report was pushed, causing the remote instance to fail saving the event.

This issue affects any MISP instance configured to push events with multiple reports to a remote server via synchronization.

Affected: <2.5.48.

cna.title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in _tiffWriteProc when saving TIFF to BytesIO

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.0.0 until 13.0.0, Pillow has a heap buffer overflow and stale-heap disclosure in _tiffWriteProc when saving compressed TIFF data through libtiff to a target without a usable fileno(), such as BytesIO. The callback sizes its allocation from the prior buffer size instead of the current write position, allowing an attacker-controlled out-of-line TIFF tag or retained ICC profile to be copied beyond the allocation after libtiff seeks forward. This overflow can crash the process and may allow code execution. Independently, unwritten alignment gaps in compressed TIFF output larger than 64 KiB can disclose stale heap bytes without a crafted tag. File paths and targets with real file descriptors are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: filelock: StrictSoftFileLock follows a symbolic link swapped in at <path>.filelock and creates claim files in a directory another local user chooses

descriptions.value: filelock is a platform-independent file lock for Python. From 3.30.0 until 4.2.1, On POSIX platforms, StrictSoftFileLock and AsyncStrictSoftFileLock validate the coordination directory in _ensure_protocol_directory but later reach the claims directory through _open_directory by pathname, allowing a local account that can rename the coordination name to swap in a symbolic link between check and use during acquisition. That race can create and leave claim files in another writable directory or strand claims in a different strict lock so the second lock times out. Separately, the claims property and force_break follow a resting symbolic link without a race when the lock user inspects or recovers the lock. Claims inspection discloses a file name to the other account only if the resulting exception text or claim_name reaches that account through a shared log, CI output, or error report. A blind force_break recovery that removes live claims from another strict lock can allow two processes into that lock's critical section; this path reaches other strict locks, not arbitrary files. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.1.

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [settings] Module settings keep the flags the module
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix ensures that the redacted and cli_only flags declared by a module in its own setting definition are preserved when the server rebuilds the setting for API exposure. By carrying these flags through to the final setting object, the existing enforcement logic (which checks these flags before serving values or accepting edits) now correctly applies to module-supplied settings, preventing disclosure of redacted values and blocking API-based modification of CLI-only settings.
assumptions: The affected version boundary is inferred from the tag_version_boundary metadata (fix is 10 commits after v2.5.48); the exact fixed release version is not stated in the patch metadata.
PR:L assumes that reading server settings requires an authenticated MISP user with appropriate role permissions; the patch does not specify the exact permission level required.

The CAPEC-126 mapping is the closest available pattern for the information-disclosure aspect; the authorization-bypass aspect (cli_only) does not have a precise CAPEC match and is subsumed under the same mapping.
VC:L assumes the exposed data is limited to module-specific API keys rather than system-wide credentials; the actual sensitivity depends on which modules are installed.

The commit message references a separate issue (branch read) reported by Jeroen Pinoy; this vulnerability was discovered as a side effect of fixing that issue, so Jeroen Pinoy is not credited as a finder of this specific vulnerability.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In app/Model/Server.php, within the readModuleSettings() method, a loop was added after the setting fields are populated that iterates over the strings 'redacted' and 'cli_only'. For each flag, if the module's own result array contains a truthy value for that key, the flag is set to true on the rebuilt $setting object before it is stored in $serverSettings. This is a 6-line addition that preserves the module-declared guard flags that were previously discarded during the setting reconstruction.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: MISP is a web application accessible over the network. AC:L: No special race conditions or complex setup are needed; a standard API call to the settings endpoint triggers the issue. AT:N: No manipulation of the attack target is required. PR:L: The attacker needs an authenticated MISP account with permission to view server settings. UI:N: No user interaction is required. VC:L: Sensitive module API keys are exposed, but the scope is limited to settings of modules that declare the redacted flag. VI:N: No direct integrity impact on the vulnerable component's data beyond the VA impact. VA:L: CLI-only settings can be modified via the API, representing a limited integrity impact on the vulnerable component's configuration. SC/SI/SA:N: No evidence of impact on other components or systems.

capecRationale.rationale: The primary impact is that sensitive data (module API keys marked as redacted) is discoverable via standard API endpoints because the redaction flag was not enforced. An authenticated user querying server settings can obtain credentials that the module author intended to keep hidden. This is the closest CAPEC to the information-disclosure aspect of the vulnerability. The secondary aspect (CLI-only settings editable via API) is an authorization bypass that does not map cleanly to a single CAPEC; CAPEC-126 is selected as the best available match for the overall pattern of accessing data that should be restricted.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The redacted flag, which instructs the server to mask a setting's value (e.g., an API key), was dropped during setting reconstruction. This caused the sensitive value to be served in plaintext via API endpoints to any authenticated user, constituting an information exposure.

The cli_only flag, which restricts a setting to command-line modification only, was dropped during setting reconstruction. This allowed the setting to be modified via the web API without the intended authorization restriction, effectively bypassing the access control the module author specified.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains a vulnerability in the handling of module plugin settings. When the server rebuilds module-supplied settings for API consumption, it drops the redacted and cli_only flags that a module declares in its own configuration metadata.

As a result:

- A module that marks a setting (such as an API key) as redacted still has its value returned in full by the servers/getSetting and servers/serverSettingsEdit endpoints, exposing sensitive credentials to any authenticated user who can read server settings.

- A module that marks a setting as cli_only (intended to be editable only via the command-line interface) can still be modified through the web API, bypassing the intended access restriction.

An authenticated user with access to server settings can therefore read sensitive module credentials and modify settings that the module author intended to restrict to CLI-only access.

Affected: <2.5.48

descriptions.value:
Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in hackney_http_connect in benoitc hackney allows HTTP Request Splitting via the value a proxy_auth_fun callback returns. After a 407 response from an HTTP CONNECT proxy, hackney_http_connect:handle_proxy_auth/11 calls the caller's proxy_auth_fun with the status code and the response headers and writes the returned binary into the Proxy-Authorization line of the CONNECT retry without checking it. A CR, LF or NUL byte in that value adds header lines to the request sent to the proxy.

The value is attacker-influenced when the callback derives it from untrusted data, for example from the proxy's challenge headers. Other caller-supplied values on the CONNECT path, such as the target host and the request headers, were already checked for control bytes.

This issue affects hackney: from 2.0.0 before 4.9.0.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Challenge. hackney_http_connect:do_handshake_with_auth/9 in src/hackney_http_connect.erl sends the CONNECT request to the proxy. When the proxy answers 407 and the proxy_auth_fun option is set, it hands the status code and the parsed response headers to hackney_http_connect:handle_proxy_auth/11.

2. Callback result. handle_proxy_auth/11 calls the caller's proxy_auth_fun with those two values. On {ok, AuthHeader} it removes any existing Proxy-Authorization header and appends the binary <<"Proxy-Authorization: ", AuthHeader/binary>> to the header list, then retries the handshake with it.

3. Splitting. The header list is joined with CRLF into the CONNECT request. A CR, LF or NUL byte inside AuthHeader therefore ends the Proxy-Authorization line early and the rest is sent as further header lines. The target host and the request headers go through control-byte checks on this path; the callback result did not. The fix applies the same has_ctl_bytes/1 check to it and returns {error, {proxy_auth_error, invalid_header}}.
