cna.title: baserCMS: Encoded path traversal bypass in the theme file API

descriptions.value: baserCMS is a website development framework. In versions 5.2.3 before 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 before 5.4.2, the optional BcThemeFile plugin's Admin API validates a raw path in ThemeFilesService::update() and getFullpath(), but ThemeFileForm::_execute() subsequently applies rawurldecode() to fullpath before writing. Because normalizePath() resolves only literal dot segments, percent-encoded traversal can pass the containment checks and become a path outside the theme directory at the write sink. An authenticated administrator can write PHP files into writable locations such as webroot and execute them, exceeding the intended theme-template editing boundary. The source also identifies the same check-before-decode ordering in ThemeFilesService::copy(), although that path was not dynamically verified. Exploitation requires the non-default plugin, an administrator session, and a same-origin Origin header; USE_CORE_ADMIN_API=false does not block session-authenticated requests. The Admin web form is not affected by this encoded-path tampering because FormProtection protects fullpath. This is a third bypass of the protections associated with CVE-2026-30940, using encoded traversal decoded after validation. This issue has been patched in versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2.

descriptions.value: Sentry-Javascript is an official Sentry SDKs for JavaScript. From 9.36.0 until 9.47.2, 10.75.2, and 11.0.0-rc.1, the webpack integration for @sentry/nextjs skips application middleware for every request path under a configured tunnelRoute, while the tunnel rewrite serves only the exact tunnel path with valid o and p query parameters. descriptions.value:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in ash-project ash allows a client to read destination records unrelated to the source record through a through relationship.

When a has_many relationship declared with through: was loaded for a single record with a limit of 1, or an unsorted has_one through relationship was loaded with a limit of 1, lateral_join?/4 in lib/ash/actions/read/relationships.ex chose the path that reads the destination without any filter linking it to the source. The load returned the first destination record by sort, or any other record with an offset. The read still runs the destination's policies but carries the relationship as accessing_from, so a client paging such a field (for example teachers(limit: 1, offset: n) through AshGraphql) can enumerate destination records that policies allow only when reached through that relationship.

This issue affects ash: from 3.24.0 before 3.37.1.

cna.title: Missing Authorization in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, whose authorization gate refuses the create, update and delete role routes to a credential confined to named domains, while leaving the read of roles unchanged. Until then, on a multi-tenant server, do not issue a full-scope API key - or assign serveradmin - confined to named domains to a party not trusted with the whole server; keep the REST API off (RestApiPort=0, the default) where it is not needed; and review custom roles' permissions for changes a confined credential should not have made (after upgrading as well, since an upgrade does not undo a change already made).

descriptions.value: Missing authorization in the REST role-management routes of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 through 6.3.6 allows a remote authenticated user whose credential is confined to named domains to modify a custom role that accounts in other domains hold, and to create custom roles and delete any that no account holds. The routes that create, update and delete a custom role require the manage_roles permission, which only the serveradmin role holds; but a full-scope API key issued for named domains, and serveradmin assigned with a domain list, are serveradmin confined to those domains and hold manage_roles. The server's authorization gate did not refuse the three role routes to a confined credential and the route named no domain, so a credential issued to one tenant could raise or lower the permissions of a custom role assigned across other tenants - granting another domain's role every permission over its mailboxes and settings, or removing what it needs. A custom role may not hold administer_server, administer_domain or manage_roles, so the confined credential cannot make itself or another a server administrator by creating or rewriting a custom role.

cna.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, which refuses a credentialed state-changing REST request a browser reports as cross-site (by Sec-Fetch-Site, or an Origin whose host is not the server's own), covering HTTP Basic and bearer credentials as the cookie session was already covered. Until then, reach the REST API and the Deck from a dedicated browser or profile closed after use so no cached Basic credential is present while browsing other sites; keep the REST API off (RestApiPort=0, the default) or bound to the loopback where it is not needed; and prefer an API key (a Bearer token a cross-site page cannot set) over the Basic box for automated clients. An upgrade does not undo a request already forged: review API keys, accounts, domains and settings for changes nobody made, and revoke any key nobody issued.

descriptions.value: Cross-site request forgery in the REST API of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allows a remote attacker to make an authenticated user's browser perform a state-changing request. The REST API accepts HTTP Basic authentication and answers a browser with a Basic sign-in box; a browser caches the credential once the box is answered and sends it with later requests to that origin, including a top-level form post from another site, and the server reads a request body whatever its declared content type. The cross-site protection covered only the cookie session (a header a cross-site form cannot set, and a SameSite=Strict cookie); HTTP Basic was not held to it. A page under an attacker's control, visited by a user whose browser holds a cached Basic credential for the REST API - typically an administrator who signed in through the box - could therefore cause a state-changing request such as creating a domain, an account or an API key, or changing a setting, with the victim's credential. The attacker cannot read the cross-origin response, so the forgery is blind.

descriptions.value: toml-node is a TOML parser for Node.js and the browser. Prior to 5.0.1, toml.parse() repeatedly slices and rejoins every path prefix in lib/compiler.js while processing long dotted keys, table headers, array-of-tables headers, and inline-table keys in assign(), deepRef(), and setNestedKey(). The resulting quadratic work can block the Node.js event loop for several seconds, and sufficiently long paths can terminate the process through memory exhaustion. The maxDepth option does not limit key-segment count and therefore does not mitigate this path. This issue is fixed in version 5.0.1.

descriptions.value: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, automatic import of a repository's .codebase-memory/ artifact allocated a decompression buffer using the attacker-controlled 64-bit original_size value from artifact.json but truncated that value to int when passing the destination capacity to the Zstandard decompressor. A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

descriptions.value: Vyper 0.1.0b1 before 0.1.0b12, 0.1.0b14, and 0.4.1 through 0.5.0b1 mix character-based line offsets with Python's UTF-8 byte col_offset values in vyper/ast/parse.py, so multi-byte characters shift the source slices used to reconstruct later numeric literals. descriptions.value: A flaw was found in mod_qos. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by maintaining numerous concurrent low-rate connections to a target server. Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.20 and 1.7.x before 1.7.5 contains an object injection primitive in rcube_session::unserialize(). A session key prefixed with “!” was treated as having no value, and the reconstructed serialized string was emitted with a key but no corresponding value, desynchronizing the remainder of the input so that following session data was interpreted as a serialized value. This yields a PHP object injection primitive for an attacker able to influence stored session data. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix object injection primitive in rcube_session::unserialize() via “!”-prefixed session keys”, which rejects such keys.

cna.title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: uma protection api resourcetype field not validated — cross-owner resource access

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank 0xNayel (YesWeHack Bug Bounty Program) for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce ownership validation on the resourceType field within UserManagedPermissionService to prevent UMA policies from attaching to resources owned by other users: upgrade to Red Hat build of Keycloak 26.4.17, 26.6.8 (or the fixed Rhbk/Keycloak Rhel/Keycloak Services builds), which validates the resourceType field during policy creation in UserManagedPermissionService to prevent policies from matching resources across different owners during evaluation in DefaultPolicyEvaluator, closing crafted UMA policy creation specifying an arbitrary victim resourceType. Until patched, this is a concern on Keycloak deployments exposing the UMA Protection API where authenticated realm users have permission to create and manage resources, so Restrict authenticated users from creating and managing resources, limit exposure of sensitive resourceType identifiers, and monitor policy definitions created via the UMA Protection API. As a compensating measure, Capture audit records when authenticated users create or modify authorization policies via the UMA Protection API to detect unauthorized cross-owner policy creation. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying missing authorization defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1006 Privilege Change Audit Logging (medium)

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the UserManagedPermissionService of the Keycloak authorization server. The UMA Protection API, which manages user permissions, fails to validate the resourceType field when a user creates a new policy. This allows an attacker to create a policy that applies to resources owned by other users, potentially leading to unauthorized access or modification of sensitive data across the entire realm.

descriptions.value:
When dispatching SASL frames to authenticate the peer, Proton will also dispatch AMQP frames if they claim to be SASL frames. This allows authentication bypass. However there will be no user name set so the effects depend on how the application deals with this condition - which otherwise means that authentication has not completed yet.



This issue affects Apache Qpid Proton C: through 0.40.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.41.1, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: NoSQL command injection via mismatched raw BSON length prefix written verbatim to the wire

descriptions.value: A data-validation flaw exists in the BSON handling and binary serialization path of the MongoDB C# Driver. When an application constructs a raw or lazy BSON document object from externally supplied binary data, the driver does not verify that the size quantity declared inside that data matches the amount of data actually provided, and it copies the data onto the wire unchanged. An unauthenticated party who can supply binary content to such an application can thereby cause additional elements to be inserted into, or existing elements to be removed from, the database command the application issues, without needing any database credentials of their own. This can result in unauthorized modification of stored data and disclosure of data outside the intended scope of the application's request, bounded by the database privileges the application itself holds.

descriptions.value:
Eclipse Kura downloads deployment packages (DPs) from a remote URL without any limit on the size of the data it receives. A malicious or compromised HTTP(S) server, or an attacker able to tamper with a plain-HTTP download, can stream an arbitrarily large (or endless) response. Kura writes the response to local storage until the filesystem is full. On gateways the temporary directory is often a RAM-backed tmpfs, so this can also exhaust memory. The result is denial of service of the device: failed configuration persistence, failed logging and possible crashes of the framework or other services.



The same missing size limit is present in the REST upload endpoint `POST /deploy/v2/_upload`, which copies the request body to the temporary directory with no limit.



Workarounds: only install DPs from trusted HTTPS sources, restrict who can install packages (Web UI `kura.packages.admin` permission, REST `kura.permission.rest.deploy`, cloud DEPLOY-V2 access).

Prior to versions 42.11.3, 43.7.0, 44.3.0, and 45.0.0-alpha.5, requests to open external protocol URLs could be attributed to a document other than the one that initiated them, causing the requestingUrl passed to session.setPermissionRequestHandler to identify trusted content for a launch requested by untrusted content. cna.title: Missing Authorization in hMailServer

credits.value: Found in the hMailServer project's own security review (Progressive Robot Ltd)

solutions.value: Upgrade to hMailServer 6.3.7, which refuses the domain-alias create, the domain rename and an internal relay host to a credential that is confined to named domains, and the reaching rule actions (bind-to-address, send-using-route, script-function on an owned rule) to anyone but the server administrator, over both the REST and the COM APIs, while keeping the changes that stay inside the credential's domains. Until then, on a multi-tenant server, do not give a domain-administrator credential, a role that manages accounts in named domains, or a named-domain API key to a party not trusted with the whole server; keep the REST API off (RestApiPort=0, the default) where it is not needed; and review existing domain aliases, domain names, relay hosts and account/domain rule actions for entries a confined credential should not have made, and the accounts' own rules for these three actions, which withholding such credentials does not stop an account setting on its own rules over COM (do this after upgrading as well, since an upgrade does not undo a change already made).

descriptions.value: Missing authorization in the REST and COM administration APIs of Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0 through 6.3.6 allows a remote authenticated user whose credential is confined to named domains to change mail routing and domain configuration beyond those domains on a multi-tenant server. A domain administrator, an account or API key given another role that manages accounts in named domains, or a full-scope API key issued for named domains could create a domain alias for any name (so that other tenants' mail for that name is diverted to an address the attacker controls, or denied), rename a domain to any name the server does not host, set a rule's bind-to-address, send-using-route or script-function action to reach one of the server's own addresses, a configured route's stored credentials or a function of the server's event script, and set the domain's relay host - which delivery then connects to with no address rule - to an address on the server's own network; and over the COM API any account could set the three rule actions on its own rules, where the script-function action runs at delivery. The authorization gate did not refuse these routes to a confined credential and the handlers were not given the caller; over COM the domain-alias save performed no authorization check at all, the domain rename required only a domain administrator, and a rule save required at most that the caller could change the rule's owner.

cna.title: Authlib: is_secure_transport() loopback exemption can be bypassed with a userinfo component, allowing cleartext-HTTP URLs to non-loopback hosts

descriptions.value: Authlib is a Python library which builds OAuth and OpenID Connect servers. From 0.13 until 1.8.0, authlib.common.security.is_secure_transport() uses a textual prefix comparison for loopback HTTP exemptions, so a URL whose userinfo begins with a loopback host can be accepted even when its parsed host is an external non-loopback system. An external party able to supply a URL to OIDC RP-Initiated Logout registration, authorization-server metadata validation, or another call site can bypass the TLS-required guard and cause cleartext redirection or acceptance of cleartext endpoints. The issue does not bypass redirect URI exact matching and does not by itself forge tokens or authenticate users. The vulnerable authlib.common.security.is_secure_transport() implementation in authlib/common/security.py misinterprets the userinfo component before OIDC RP-Initiated Logout dynamic client registration and other consumers enforce transport security. This issue is fixed in version 1.8.0.

cna.title: Django REST framework: JSONParser applies an attacker-named codec to the request stream

descriptions.value: Django REST framework is a toolkit for building Web APIs. From 3.6.4 until 3.18.2, JSONParser.parse in rest_framework/parsers.py uses the client-supplied Content-Type charset value with codecs.getreader, which accepts byte-transform codecs such as bz2_codec rather than only text encodings. A remote unauthenticated client can therefore cause a compressed JSON request body to be expanded after Django has enforced DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE against only the wire bytes, allowing a very small request to consume substantial per-worker memory. The default parser set is sufficient, and any reachable endpoint that accepts a JSON body is affected. This issue is fixed in version 3.18.2.

cna.title: fpdf2: Exponential SVG '<use>' expansion causes CPU and memory exhaustion in 'FPDF.image()'

descriptions.value: fpdf2 is a PDF creation library for Python. From 2.5.0 until 2.8.8, fpdf2's SVGObject.build_xref() passes nested SVG <use> references to GraphicsContext.add_item(), whose default clone=True deep-copy behavior copies the complete referenced graphics tree during FPDF.image() processing. Repeating references at each nesting level makes the in-memory object count and processing work grow exponentially, allowing a small user-controlled SVG to consume excessive CPU and memory, raise MemoryError, fail PDF generation jobs, and reduce or exhaust worker capacity. ResourceAccessPolicy does not prevent the issue because the references are inline and require no external resource, XML entity, local file, or permissive network setting. This issue is fixed in version 2.8.8.

cna.title: NoMachine nxwebrunner Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

descriptions.value:
NoMachine nxwebrunner Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of NoMachine. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the web service, which listens on TCP port 4443 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-30685.

cna.title: Plaintext exposure of encrypted fields via ANSI code-page corruption of database name

descriptions.value: A flaw in the client-side encryption support of the MongoDB .NET/C# driver can cause data designated for client-side field-level encryption to be written without encryption. Under certain platform text-encoding configurations, an internal name conversion loses information, so the encryption layer fails to associate the operation with its configured encryption rules and the operation proceeds without an error being raised. An application user with the ability to write data through an affected application can therefore have sensitive fields persisted in plaintext, defeating the confidentiality guarantee that client-side encryption is intended to provide. No integrity or availability impact was observed.

The effect is limited to the document matched by the application's own filter, whose contents can be modified in ways the application did not intend.

cna.title: Flexible GraphRAG: Cypher/Graph Injection via broken string-escaping in FalkorDB adapter (_escape()) - full graph wipe from ingested-document content

descriptions.value: Flexible GraphRAG is a Python framework for building graph and retrieval-augmented generation applications across multiple graph, vector, and search backends. From 0.6.0 until 0.8.2, the _escape() helper in flexible-graphrag/langchain/graph/pg_store_adapters/falkordb_adapter.py escapes quotes before backslashes and then interpolates the result into Cypher assembled by FalkorDBAdapter.add_graph_documents, allowing an inserted escape to be doubled and a quote to terminate the string early. When GRAPH_BACKEND=langchain and GRAPH_DB=falkordb are configured, attacker-influenced ingested document content can cause the extraction model to produce malicious entity or relationship values that reach these queries, allowing injected Cypher clauses to modify or delete graph data and, when the calling code surfaces query results to the user or LLM, disclose graph data. Dynamic node and relationship type identifiers are also inserted into backtick-quoted query positions without safe parameterization. The LlamaIndex FalkorDB store is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.2.

cna.title: draw.io Desktop: Arbitrary local-file read via read-side IPC (no blessed-path gate)

descriptions.value: draw.io Desktop is the official Electron build of draw.io. Prior to 31.4.4, draw.io Desktop is vulnerable to arbitrary local-file disclosure through the Electron main process's read-side IPC handlers. The readFile, getFileDrafts, getBkpFile, fileStat, isFileWritable, checkFileExists, and watchFile actions operate on a renderer-chosen filesystem path with no blessed-path (assertWritablePath) authorization. The only gates are validateSender — a URL-prefix origin check — plus, for readFile alone, a content "sniff" and a lexical appBaseDir prefix block. The write-side handlers (saveFile, writeFile, saveDraft, deleteFile) are all protected by assertWritablePath; the read side is not. The result is a read/write authorization asymmetry: any frame executing in the app's file:// origin can read the contents of local files that the same origin is explicitly forbidden to write. This issue is fixed in version 31.4.4.

cna.title: baserCMS: SQL injection in the admin panel and admin API

descriptions.description: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

descriptions.value: baserCMS is a website development framework. In versions 5.0.0 before 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 before 5.4.2, list and detail actions in the Admin and Api/Admin prefixes pass request query parameters, including contain, conditions, fields, finder, and order, directly to the ORM as options. A user able to log into the admin panel can embed SQL fragments in those options to execute arbitrary SQL against the application's database, including reading password hashes from the users table. Public-page and public-API fixes released in 5.3.1 and 5.4.1 did not protect these administrative paths. Setting USE_CORE_ADMIN_API to false does not prevent access through an authenticated browser session. This issue has been patched in versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2.

cna.title: Mod_qos: query truncation during json body merging permits security-rule bypass

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Robin "drzobin" Larsson for reporting this issue.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in mod_qos. An off-by-one pointer calculation error occurs when merging request body parameters with an existing URL query, which truncates the query string during security evaluation while leaving the actual request unchanged. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted request that conceals prohibited values from inspection, resulting in a bypass of configured security rules.

descriptions.value: Roundcube Webmail 1.6.14 before 1.6.20 and 1.7.0 before 1.7.5 is affected by a server-side request forgery filter bypass. The network blocklist used by rcube_utils::is_local_url() omitted the RFC 6052 NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96, the RFC 8215 local-use NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 and the unspecified address ::/128, so URLs such as http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/ passed the filter and reached loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses. Upstream fixed this in the commit “Fix SSRF filter (is_local_url()) bypass via NAT64 64:ff9b::/96”.

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a higher privileged user accesses the affected administrative screens. This issue only affects sites with a large number of users.

descriptions.value: In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

flowintel contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrative users to access sensitive configuration data and logs intended for administrators only.

The notification page and alert API responses exposed sensitive fields, including webhook URLs, signing secrets, IMAP credentials, and delivery logs, in the initial data or JSON responses. Although the user interface hid the configuration form from non-admin users, the underlying data remained accessible via the page source or API endpoints. This exposure included historical webhook URLs that may contain active bearer tokens.

An attacker with a valid non-admin account could retrieve these credentials and logs, potentially leading to unauthorized access to notification services, impersonation of the application in webhook deliveries, or further lateral movement within the infrastructure.

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0
CAPEC-126 Accessing Functionality Not Properly Restricted by User Role

descriptions.description: CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

solutions.value: The vulnerability is remediated by enforcing role-based access control on data serialization and template rendering. Non-admin users are now restricted to receiving only public enable flags and do not have access to webhook URLs, secrets, or delivery logs. The shared alert serializer explicitly removes sensitive fields for non-admin users, ensuring that both the notification page and the alerts API preserve administrative diagnostics while protecting sensitive data from unauthorized access.

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

assumptions: The affected version is assumed to be all versions prior to 4.1.0 based on the fixed_version metadata.
The CAPEC mapping is based on the general pattern of accessing restricted functionality, as the specific attack vector is a standard HTTP request to an existing endpoint.

The CVSS vector assumes that the exposure of secrets leads to a high impact on integrity of the vulnerable component, as these secrets can be used to impersonate the application or access other services.

capecRationale.rationale: The attacker leveraged their authenticated non-admin role to access data (webhook secrets, logs) that was not properly restricted to the administrator role, despite the UI hiding the configuration form.

x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: Attack Vector is Network (AV:N) as the application is web-based. Attack Complexity is Low (AC:L) as it requires only standard HTTP requests. Attack Requirements are None (AT:N). Privileges Required are Low (PR:L) as any authenticated non-admin user can exploit this. User Interaction is None (UI:N). Vulnerable Component Impact is None (VC:N) as the server itself is not compromised. Vulnerable Component Integrity is High (VI:H) because sensitive secrets and logs are exposed, which can lead to further compromise. Vulnerable Component Availability is None (VA:N). Subsequent Component Impact is None (SC:N, SI:N, SA:N) as the direct impact is limited to information disclosure within the vulnerable component, though downstream impacts are possible but not directly measured by the base vector.
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The vulnerability is remediated by enforcing role-based access control on data serialization and template rendering. Non-admin users are now restricted to receiving only public enable flags and do not have access to webhook URLs, secrets, or delivery logs. The shared alert serializer explicitly removes sensitive fields for non-admin users, ensuring that both the notification page and the alerts API preserve administrative diagnostics while protecting sensitive data from unauthorized access.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: The patch modifies app/alerts/alerts_core.py and app/notification/notification.py. In alerts_core.py, the alerts_to_json function now checks if the user is an admin and removes the webhook_url field from the JSON response for non-admin users. In notification.py, the index route now checks the current user's admin status. For non-admins, it passes a restricted configuration object containing only public enable flags (CASE_CREATE_ALERT_ENABLED, WEBHOOK_ENABLED) instead of the full ConfigModule, and it passes an empty list for alert_logs instead of the actual log data. This ensures sensitive configuration and logs are not embedded in the template context for unauthorized users.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: HotGo 2.18.6 through 2.19.0 Missing Authorization via pullMessages Endpoint

descriptions.value: HotGo 2.18.6 through 2.19.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated backend users to read other administrators' private letters because the messageIds helper omits the receiver filter. Low-privilege users can call GET /admin/notice/pullMessages, which is exempt from role permission checks via exceptAuth, to retrieve titles, contents and senders of private letters.

FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass in its case serialization logic that allows an authenticated user to view metadata of private cases they do not have access to.

When a case is linked to another case, the JSON representation of the source case included the ID, title, and description of every linked case regardless of the requesting user's permissions. This affected multiple access paths:

- Browser views (case detail, case info, search, calendar)
- REST API endpoints (get case, list cases, search, title lookup, completed/not-completed lists)
- Internal tooling and connector module context building

An attacker with valid credentials and access to any case that contains a link to a private case could enumerate the private case's identifier, title, and description without holding a membership or role on that private case. The exposure occurred because the serialization method did not receive or evaluate the acting user's identity before including linked-case data in the response.

Security impact:
- Disclosure of private case identifiers, titles, and descriptions to unauthorized users
- Facilitation of further targeted attacks against the exposed private cases
- Bypass of the intended per-case access control model

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0
CAPEC-12 Application Metadata Discovery

descriptions.description: CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

solutions.value: The serialization method now accepts the acting user as a parameter and filters linked cases based on the user's authorization. When an authenticated user is provided, only linked cases the user is permitted to view are included. When no user is provided (internal or anonymous callers), the method fails closed by excluding all private linked cases. All call sites across browser views, API endpoints, calendar, search, tools, and internal core operations were updated to pass the resolved user identity, ensuring consistent enforcement regardless of the access path.

cna.title: UrlGenerator Lets Host Placeholder Values Send Generated URLs to Another Host

descriptions.value:
UrlGenerator puts the values of host placeholders into the generated URL without encoding them. Their default requirement, [^.]++, accepts /, @, #, ?, \, % and :. With the host {tenant}.example.com, the value evil%2Ecom# gives https://evil%2Ecom#.example.com/dashboard, which browsers send to evil.com. This works even when requirements are checked. Unicode full stops like 。 have the same effect, since IDNA maps them to ..

Applications are exposed when untrusted values reach host placeholders, for example when they pass the query string of the request to url(). A route that uses RedirectController::redirectAction() with keepQueryParams: true does the same, when the target route has a host placeholder that the redirecting route doesn't define.

UrlGenerator now rejects host placeholder values that contain a character that is forbidden in a host. These characters are C0 controls, space, #, %, /, :, <, >, ?, @, [, \, ], ^, | and DEL. Unicode full stops are rejected too. This check applies whatever strict_requirements is set to. When strict_requirements is false or null, the generator logs an error and returns an empty string instead of throwing. Host placeholder values can still be an IPv6 literal like [::1], but they can't contain a port anymore.

cna.title: Quadratic time unique_items list validation in Pydantic V1

descriptions.value:
Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate.

The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones. For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons.

The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()).

The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in quadratic time, as their items aren't guaranteed to be hashable: bound their size using the max_items constraint.

Pydantic V2 models are not affected.

supportingMedia.value:
Summary

Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate.

Details

The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones:

@classmethod
def unique_items_validator(cls, v: 'Optional[List[T]]') -> 'Optional[List[T]]':
    if v is None:
        return None

    for i, value in enumerate(v, start=1):
        if value in v[i:]:
            raise errors.ListUniqueItemsError()

    return v

For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons.

The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87.

If you are relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2, upgrade to V2.14.2 or later.

Impact

Denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()).

The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in quadratic time, as their items aren't guaranteed to be hashable: bound their size using the max_items constraint.

Pydantic V2 models are not affected.

descriptions.value:
flowintel contains multiple authorization bypass vulnerabilities in its Analyzer (MISP Modules) functionality, affecting both the web interface and the REST API.

- Saving analyzer results to a case or task accepted caller-supplied case and task identifiers without verifying that the authenticated user is a member of the target case or holds the required restricted-task permissions. An authenticated user could write notes, create tasks, and attach MISP objects or attributes into another organization's case.

- Stored analyzer results were retrievable by UUID by any authenticated user. Both the web endpoint and the API endpoint returned the full result payload without checking ownership, exposing another user's analysis output.

- The save handler did not validate the structure of the request, did not reject conflicting destination selections, and did not halt processing when a task-note operation failed, allowing partial or unintended writes.

Preconditions: the attacker must possess a valid authenticated session (or API token) in flowintel. No administrative role is required.

Security impact: unauthorized cross-tenant data disclosure (analyzer results) and unauthorized cross-tenant data modification (notes, tasks, MISP objects/attributes in another organization's case).

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
CAPEC-129 Parameter Tampering

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

solutions.value: The patch enforces authorization on both read and write paths for analyzer results. A new ownership/admin check gates result retrieval in both the web view and the API. Before any write operation, the target case is resolved and the caller's membership (or admin role) is verified; restricted-task permissions are additionally enforced. Input validation rejects malformed or conflicting destination selections, and task-note errors now abort the save. The front-end template was updated to surface 403 permission errors instead of silently treating them as generic failures.

cna.title: MISP Missing Authorization in Sync Proposal Endpoints Allows Cross-Event Data Access and Modification

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [security] Synced proposals reach only events the sender

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [security] Synced proposals reach only events the sender
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix enforces proper authorization scoping at two levels. First, pushProposals now resolves the event through fetchSimpleEvent (which applies ACL) and the pull path uses a new __eventSyncedWithServer helper that verifies the event is actually shared with the syncing server before accepting proposals. The stored event_id, event_uuid, and event_org_id are taken from the local event record, not from sender-supplied fields. Second, a new findTargetAttribute method requires all three of Attribute.id, Attribute.event_id, and Attribute.uuid to match simultaneously, ensuring an edit proposal can only affect an attribute within its own event. Acceptance paths now reject the proposal if the target attribute cannot be resolved within the correct event scope.
assumptions: The affected MISP version range is not specified in the patch; the fix is applied to the main development branch and the exact version boundary is unknown.

CVSS PR:L assumes the attacker needs only a standard sync-permission role; if the deployment requires additional administrative setup to enable sync, the effective privilege requirement may be higher.
CVSS VC:L assumes the attacker can observe event data in the API response; if the deployment suppresses event details in error responses, confidentiality impact may be lower.
CAPEC-126 is the closest available mapping; the exact pattern is an authorization-scoping gap rather than a classic privilege escalation, so the mapping is approximate.

The SSVC technical_impact of 'total' assumes the attacker can fully modify or delete target attributes; if the deployment has additional compensating controls (e.g., audit logging, backup restoration), the effective impact may be partial.

The patch does not specify whether the vulnerability is exploitable only during active server-to-server sync or also via direct API calls to pushProposals; both paths are fixed, suggesting both were vulnerable.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In EventsController::pushProposals, the raw Event::find by UUID was replaced with Event::fetchSimpleEvent (ACL-aware) and the inline proposal-saving loop was extracted into ShadowAttribute::capture which now receives the already-authorized event and overwrites event_id, event_uuid, and event_org_id from the local record. In ShadowAttributesController::__accept and ShadowAttribute::acceptProposal, the unscoped Attribute::find by UUID was replaced with ShadowAttribute::findTargetAttribute which matches id + event_id + uuid. A new private method __eventSyncedWithServer validates that a pulled proposal's event is shared with the remote server (via distribution level, sharing group, or orgc ownership) before capture. pullProposals now pre-resolves and caches the authorized event per UUID. Regression tests (ProposalSyncScope) verify hidden events return the same response as missing events, stored columns reflect local identity, cross-event edit proposals are rejected, and duplicate/newer-version handling is correct
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N - MISP is a network-accessible web application. AC:L - the attack requires crafting a standard API request with a known/guessed UUID; no race conditions or special timing needed. AT:N - no prior data tampering required; the attack payload is the request itself. PR:L - requires an authenticated user with perm_sync. UI:N - no victim interaction needed. VC:L - the sync user can retrieve event data (including attributes) from events they should not see. VI:H - the user can modify or delete attributes in events outside their authorization scope, and inject proposals onto restricted events. VA:N - no denial-of-service impact evidenced. SC/SI/SA:N - impact is confined to the vulnerable MISP instance's own data; no cross-system impact is demonstrated by the patch.

capecRationale.rationale: The sync user holds legitimate perm_sync privileges, but the application fails to correctly scope those privileges to the events and attributes the user is authorized to access. The attacker exploits the missing authorization boundary to perform actions (push proposals to restricted events, modify foreign attributes) that exceed the intended scope of their role. This is the closest CAPEC to the observed pattern of an authenticated user leveraging an authorization gap to reach resources outside their permitted set. Uncertainty: CAPEC-126 typically describes privilege escalation; here the user already has sync rights but the application's scoping is incorrect, making this a best-available match rather than an exact fit.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The pushProposals endpoint and the pullProposals capture path did not verify that the sync user had access to the target event before storing proposals. The event was located by a user-supplied UUID with no ACL enforcement, allowing proposals to be attached to events outside the user's permitted scope.

The edit-proposal acceptance path resolved the target attribute using only the user-controlled UUID field (Attribute.uuid) without scoping to the event, allowing an attacker to reference an attribute in a different event and have it modified or deleted. descriptions.value: CAPEC-126 Exploiting Incorrectly Adjusted Privileges

solutions.value: The fix enforces proper authorization scoping at two levels. First, pushProposals now resolves the event through fetchSimpleEvent (which applies ACL) and the pull path uses a new __eventSyncedWithServer helper that verifies the event is actually shared with the syncing server before accepting proposals. The stored event_id, event_uuid, and event_org_id are taken from the local event record, not from sender-supplied fields. Second, a new findTargetAttribute method requires all three of Attribute.id, Attribute.event_id, and Attribute.uuid to match simultaneously, ensuring an edit proposal can only affect an attribute within its own event. Acceptance paths now reject the proposal if the target attribute cannot be resolved within the correct event scope.

descriptions.value:
MISP contains an authorization bypass in its server-to-server proposal synchronization mechanism. Two related flaws were identified:

1. The events/pushProposals endpoint located the target event by UUID without enforcing any access-control check. A sync user with perm_sync could push shadow-attribute proposals to any event on the local instance, including events with restricted distribution (e.g., distribution level 0, visible only to the owning organisation). The stored proposal also carried the sender-supplied event_uuid and event_org_id rather than the local event's actual identity, corrupting the data model.

2. When accepting an edit proposal (old_id != 0), the code resolved the target live attribute by UUID alone (Attribute.uuid = shadow.uuid) without scoping the lookup to the proposal's own event. A malicious sync user could therefore craft a proposal whose uuid matched an attribute in a different event; upon acceptance, the wrong attribute would be modified or deleted. The same unscoped lookup existed in the ShadowAttribute::acceptProposal path.

Preconditions: an authenticated user with sync permission (perm_sync) on a MISP instance that participates in server-to-server synchronisation. The attacker must know or enumerate the UUID of a target event or attribute.

Security impact: unauthorised read access to restricted events, unauthorised insertion of proposals onto events the user cannot see, and unauthorised modification or deletion of attributes belonging to other events. This compromises the confidentiality and integrity of threat-intelligence data across organisational boundaries within a MISP deployment.

cna.title: Cross-user Data Disclosure in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow Responses

descriptions.value: A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests. An authenticated user with read access to an index who requests Arrow output containing an affected column type can receive data from indices they are not authorized to access. The attacker cannot select which concurrent data is disclosed.

cna.title: Org.keycloak:keycloak-services: post-logout redirect uri configuration of a disabled client is still honored, leading to open redirect

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Keycloak. The OpenID Connect (OIDC) logout endpoint continues to honor post-logout redirect rules for disabled clients rather than rejecting the requests. If a disabled client retains permissive redirect configurations, a remote attacker can exploit this issue by supplying an arbitrary redirection target in a logout request, leading to an open redirect that can be used in phishing attacks.

cna.x_redhatCweChain: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

workarounds.value:
Administrators can mitigate this flaw by removing permissive redirect configurations from inactive clients or deleting unused clients:

1. In the Keycloak Admin Console, navigate to the relevant realm and inspect the 'Clients' list.
2. For any client set to disabled, open its settings and clear or restrict the 'Valid Post Logout Redirect URIs' and 'Valid Redirect URIs' fields, ensuring wildcard characters ('*') are removed and only explicitly trusted absolute URLs remain.
3. Alternatively, permanently delete any disabled clients that are obsolete and no longer required.

Caveats: Deleting a client permanently removes its configuration, mappers, service account roles, and credentials. Changes made to client settings in the Admin Console apply immediately to the realm without requiring a Keycloak service restart.

cna.title: Without APP_RUNTIME_MODE, HTTP Workers Running Under the CLI SAPI Return Full Exception Dumps in Production

descriptions.value:
Since Symfony 7.4.0, FrameworkBundle chooses the error renderer from the runtime mode of the application, which comes from the APP_RUNTIME_MODE env var. When this variable isn't set, the cli, phpdbg and embed SAPIs default to the CLI mode, and errors are rendered with CliErrorRenderer. This renderer dumps the whole exception, and it did so even when debug was off.

HTTP workers that run under the CLI SAPI and don't set APP_RUNTIME_MODE then sent these dumps as error responses in production. They contain the messages, file paths and traces of the exceptions. Some exceptions reference the request, like the access denied errors of access_control rules. Their dump then contains the server parameters, with all the environment variables of the application.

This affects, for example, the RoadRunner, Swoole and ReactPHP runners of php-runtime, and baldinof/roadrunner-bundle before 3.2.4. The worker mode of FrankenPHP sets the variable and isn't affected.

The CLI renderer is now used only in debug mode.

cna.title: Harness `ToolOutputLimits` ANSI stripping can take quadratic time, blocking the event loop

descriptions.value:
### Summary ui

With `strip_ansi=True`, Pydantic AI Harness's `ToolOutputLimits` capability removes ANSI escape sequences from tool output with a pattern that takes time quadratic in the length of a line. A tool result of a few hundred kilobytes, crafted with many unterminated escape sequences, can occupy the event loop for tens of seconds to minutes, delaying every other request and agent run in the process.

### Details

This affects applications that set `strip_ansi=True` on `ToolOutputLimits` (named `OverflowingToolOutput` before 0.13.0) and run tools whose output an attacker can influence, such as shell commands, file reads, fetched pages or MCP servers. Stripping runs on the event loop before the capability reduces the output, so its own size limits do not bound it.

The assumed attacker can place text in content a tool returns.

### Mitigation

Upgrade `pydantic-ai-harness` to 0.70.0 or later. Until then, leave `strip_ansi` at its default, `False`.

On Pydantic AI v1, the harness cannot be upgraded past 0.4.0. Upgrade to Pydantic AI v2 and `pydantic-ai-harness` 0.70.0, or leave `strip_ansi` off.

Flowintel , contained a session management vulnerability in its browser authentication mechanism. The session identifier used a bare numeric user ID rather than a credential-bound token, resulting in several related weaknesses:

- Remembered logins (remember-me cookies) remained valid after a user changed their password, allowing an attacker holding a previously issued cookie to retain access indefinitely.
- Server-side session identifiers were not rotated upon login (local, SSO, or remembered), enabling session fixation.
- Self-service email and password changes did not require verification of the current password, permitting an attacker with an active session to modify account credentials without knowledge of the existing password.
- Administrator-initiated password resets did not revoke other browser sessions, invalidate remembered logins, or rotate the affected user's API key.

An attacker who obtained a valid session or remember-me cookie (e.g., through XSS, network interception, or cookie theft) could maintain unauthorized access even after the legitimate user changed their password. Additionally, an attacker with any valid session could change the account's email address or password without knowing the current credentials, effectively taking over the account.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
CAPEC-18 Session Prediction
CAPEC-60 Session Hijacking

solutions.value: The fix binds browser session identifiers to the account's current credentials using an HMAC-SHA256 token derived from the user ID, auth provider, creation date, and password hash. All login paths (local, SSO, remembered) now rotate the server-side session ID. Self-service email and password changes require the current password. A self-service password change refreshes the owner's session while revoking all other browser sessions and remembered logins. Administrator password resets additionally rotate the user's API key. Legacy bare-ID session identifiers are rejected by the user loader, and session housekeeping code is updated to parse the new format safely.

cna.title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via RegExp mount paths under parameterized prefixes

descriptions.value: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.7 through 4.0.9, the plugin does not rewrite regular-expression mount paths to account for a parameterized plugin prefix, so when middleware is mounted with a regular expression inside a plugin registered under a parameterized prefix, the Express matcher treats the prefix parameter as literal text and never matches the real request path. As a result, Express silently skips that middleware while Fastify still runs the route handler, so an application that relies on regular-expression mounted middleware for authentication or authorization inside a parameterized-prefix plugin exposes protected routes to unauthenticated clients. No special configuration is required beyond a parameterized prefix and a regular-expression mount. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU.

The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel
- Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note

Impact:
- Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users
- No confidentiality or integrity impact

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0
CAPEC-10 Application Resource Exhaustion
CAPEC-124 Resource Exhaustion via Algorithmic Complexity

descriptions.description: CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

solutions.value: The fix introduces bounds on table expansion: a maximum padded-cell count (50,000) and a maximum padding ratio (4x filled cells). When a CSV or JSON dataset would exceed these limits, the original content is preserved in a safely fenced code block instead of being rendered as a table. Additionally, nested JSON values in table cells are now serialized in compact form (no indentation), and the JSON fallback path uses the same safe fencing helper, preventing both quadratic cell expansion and indentation-based output inflation.

FlowIntel contains a missing authorization vulnerability in its task file deletion functionality. When a privileged task is in a restricted state (Requested, Rejected, or Request Review), any authenticated user with basic case membership (e.g., editor or queuer) was able to delete evidence files associated with that task via both the browser interface and the REST API. The deletion operation should have been restricted to users holding Admin, Case Admin, or Queue Admin roles.

The vulnerability affects the core file deletion logic, the browser-facing task endpoint, and the API task endpoint. No role-based restriction was enforced prior to performing disk removal, database record deletion, timeline event removal, or history log updates.

An attacker with a low-privilege case membership could destroy evidence files, corrupt investigation timelines, and alter case history, compromising the integrity of ongoing investigations.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.
CAPEC-126 Forced Browsing

solutions.value: The fix enforces role-based authorization before any file deletion side effects occur. It verifies that the file belongs to the specified task (preventing task substitution) and that, when the task is in a restricted state, the requesting user holds Admin, Case Admin, or Queue Admin privileges. Denial is returned with a 403 status and an audit log entry before any disk, database, timeline, or history modification takes place. The check is applied consistently across the core model, the browser endpoint, and the API endpoint.

cna.title: Unconstrained S3 Endpoints in Elasticsearch ES|QL Data Sources

descriptions.value: Unconstrained S3 endpoint settings in Elasticsearch ES|QL data sources can cause requests containing storage credentials to be sent to an attacker-controlled host. A user with data-source management privileges can configure a custom endpoint without the intended host restriction. On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only.

supportingMedia.value: Unconstrained S3 endpoint settings in Elasticsearch ES|QL data sources can cause requests containing storage credentials to be sent to an attacker-controlled host. A user with data-source management privileges can configure a custom endpoint without the intended host restriction. On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only.

configurations.value:
All of the following conditions must hold:
- ES|QL federation is enabled.
- The attacker has data-source management privileges.

workarounds.value: Leave esql.federation.enabled disabled. Where federation is enabled, review the endpoint and sts_endpoint settings of existing S3 data sources and restrict data-source management privileges to trusted administrators.

solutions.value: Upgrade Elasticsearch / ES|QL versions 9.5.0 through 9.5.5 to 9.5.6.

After upgrading, data sources using non-AWS endpoints require an operator to add the trusted host to esql.external.allowed_endpoint_hosts. This is a node setting and requires a restart; until configured, affected custom-endpoint data sources stop serving reads.

descriptions.value:
flowintel contains a vulnerability in the MISP correlation feature that allows unauthorized disclosure of case identifiers.

The application failed to enforce proper access controls when generating correlation lists for MISP attributes. Specifically, the system did not verify whether the requesting user had permission to view the source case or the matching cases returned in the correlation results. This lack of authorization checks allowed authenticated users to potentially discover the existence of cases they do not have access to, leading to information disclosure.

The vulnerability affects the following components:
- Case correlation logic
- API endpoints for retrieving correlation attributes
- MISP object handling

Affected versions: < 4.1.0
CAPEC-126 Forced Browsing

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

solutions.value: The vulnerability is remediated by enforcing strict access control checks on both the source case and the resulting correlation list. The system now verifies that the acting user has permission to view the source case before processing correlations. Additionally, the resulting list of matching case IDs is filtered to include only cases that the user is authorized to access. This ensures that no unauthorized case identifiers are disclosed to the user.

cna.title: Nested Short Ternaries Make the Nesting Check of the Expression Parser Exponential, Letting Untrusted Expressions Hang It

descriptions.value:
The fix for CVE-2026-109449 made the expression parser check the nesting level of long expressions. This check exists since Symfony 5.4.54, 6.4.48, 7.4.21 and 8.1.9. The parser builds a ?: b with the node of a used twice, and the check walked every path to every node. With nested short ternaries, the number of paths doubles at each level, so an expression of 256 bytes never finished parsing.

The expression needs no variable and no function. Any code that parses or lints untrusted expressions is affected, including the ExpressionSyntax validation constraint. evaluate() and compile() parse the expression first, so they hang too.

The nesting check now skips the nodes it already checked, so it takes linear time again. evaluate(), compile() and the messages of runtime errors now use the node of a once, so a is evaluated once, as in PHP.

supportingMedia.value:

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix adds an event-scope ownership check in ObjectReference::captureReference(). After locating an existing reference by UUID, the code now verifies that the reference's event_id matches the event currently being saved. If the UUID belongs to a different event, the reference is skipped (neither updated nor recreated in the saving event) and a warning-level system log entry is written recording the blocked operation, the target event ID, and the foreign event ID that owns the UUID.
assumptions: The affected MISP version range is not specified in the patch; all versions prior to this commit are assumed affected.
PR:L assumes the attacker needs only a standard authenticated user with event add/edit permission; the regression tests confirm a least-privileged role suffices.
The CAPEC-114 mapping is an approximation; no CAPEC specifically covers cross-tenant IDOR via UUID in a multi-tenant application.
VC:N assumes the attack does not enable reading foreign reference data; the patch evidence shows only write/overwrite impact.
VA:N assumes setting the 'deleted' flag on a reference is an integrity modification rather than an availability denial; the reference record still exists in the database.
The commit date of 2026-11-11 is taken at face value from the patch metadata.

solutions.value: The fix adds an event-scope ownership check in ObjectReference::captureReference(). After locating an existing reference by UUID, the code now verifies that the reference's event_id matches the event currently being saved. descriptions.value: MISP contains an authorization and scope flaw in the ObjectReference model's captureReference method. When a user saves an event (via REST API, sync, or feeds), any object reference included in the payload is looked up by its UUID across the entire MISP instance rather than being scoped to the event being saved. An authenticated user with permission to add or edit events can therefore include the UUID of an object reference belonging to a different event—including events in other organizations that the user cannot view—and cause the system to overwrite that foreign reference's relationship_type, comment, deleted flag, and timestamp with attacker-supplied values. The affected reference is neither deleted nor recreated in the attacker's event; its fields are silently rewritten in place. This constitutes a cross-tenant integrity violation: data integrity of object references in events the attacker has no read or write access to is compromised. The vulnerability is reachable through any event save path (REST add/edit, inter-instance sync, feed ingestion) and requires only a valid authenticated session with event modification privileges and knowledge or discovery of a target reference UUID.

The flowintel Docker build workflow used the GitHub Actions checkout action with default credential persistence, causing the job authentication token to be written into the repository's Git configuration file. This file became part of the Docker build context and could be retained in exported build cache layers, even though Git metadata was stripped from the final runtime image.

An attacker with access to the CI/CD build cache or build environment could extract the persisted token and use it to gain unauthorized access to the private source repository.

Impact:
- Exposure of a valid authentication token to the private repository
- Potential unauthorized read access to source code and repository metadata

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0
CAPEC-1 Session Hijacking

descriptions.description: CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

solutions.value: The checkout step is configured to not persist credentials into the workspace, and the full branch history is fetched during the authenticated checkout phase. This ensures the job token is never written to the Git configuration file that enters the Docker build context, eliminating the credential from build cache layers while preserving the ability to resolve release tags against the main branch.

cna.title: Build-time Code Execution in @symfony/stimulus-bridge via a Controller Package That Maps Its package.json to a Script

descriptions.value:
The controllers.json loader of @symfony/stimulus-bridge loads the package.json file of each package listed in controllers.json with require(). Node resolves this path through the exports field of the package, which can map ./package.json to a script. require() then runs that script during the Webpack or Symfony Encore build.

This is a build-time vulnerability: it doesn't affect browsers or end users. A malicious or compromised package listed in controllers.json can run code on the developer machine or the CI server. This works even when the package manager doesn't run install scripts. This code can read the files and environment variables of the build, like CI secrets, and change the built assets.

The loader now reads the resolved file and parses it as JSON, so that a mapped script fails to parse instead of running.

vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the authenticated user's two-factor authentication without requiring password confirmation. Because the state-changing operation was reachable via GET, an attacker with a basic account could embed an image element (or any other GET-triggering markup) in a comment pointing to that endpoint. When a victim with 2FA enabled viewed the comment, their browser silently issued the GET request, disabling the victim's second factor of authentication. No CSRF token was enforced on the GET path, and no password was required to confirm the action. Second, the comment detail page (/comment/<uuid>) rendered unpublished comments to any visitor who possessed the URL, bypassing the moderation workflow that was intended to keep such content hidden until approved. The API correctly restricted access, but the web view did not enforce the same authorization check. The combined effect allows an attacker to degrade a victim's account security (removal of 2FA) through a single page view and to read content that was not yet approved for public release.

x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The /user/toggle_2fa endpoint is restricted to POST only, enabling CSRF token validation, and now requires the user's password to confirm disabling of 2FA. The comment detail view now checks the comment's publication status and returns 404 for unpublished comments unless the requester is the author or holds moderator privileges, matching the existing API behavior.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In website/web/views/user.py, the route decorator for toggle_2FA is changed from methods=["GET"] to methods=["POST"], and a password verification block (request.form.get("password") with current_user.check_password) is added before the 2FA flag is cleared. In website/web/templates/user/edit_user.html, the disable-2FA link is replaced with a modal form that submits a POST with a CSRF token and a password field; the enable-2FA link is converted to a POST form with a hidden csrf_token input. In website/web/views/comment.py, an authorization check is added after the comment lookup: if the comment is unpublished and the current user is neither the author (can_user_edit_comment) nor a moderator (can_user_manage_comment with comment:publish), the view aborts with 404. A new test file tests/test_toggle_2fa.py covers GET rejection, missing/wrong password rejection, successful password-confirmed disable, CSRF token enforcement, and unpublished comment visibility for anonymous users, other users, and the author.

UI:P: the victim passively interacts by viewing the comment page. VC/VI/VA:N: the web application itself is not directly compromised in confidentiality, integrity, or availability. weaknessRationale.rationale: The 2FA disable endpoint accepted GET requests, allowing a state-changing operation to be triggered by an image tag or link in user-supplied content without a CSRF token. This is a textbook CSRF vulnerability where the HTTP method and lack of anti-CSRF protection on a sensitive action enable cross-site request forgery.

Disabling two-factor authentication is a critical security action that did not require re-authentication (password confirmation). The endpoint performed the sensitive operation with only a session cookie, without verifying the user's password, weakening the authentication boundary.

The comment detail web view did not check the comment's publication status or the viewer's role before rendering the content. Unpublished comments were accessible to any user (or anonymous visitor) who knew the UUID, bypassing the authorization model enforced by the API.

This is a direct CSRF pattern where a GET request to a state-changing endpoint is triggered by the victim's browser while viewing attacker-controlled content. The fix (POST-only + CSRF token + password) confirms the CSRF classification.

The unpublished comment was accessible to anyone who knew or guessed the UUID in the URL, without an authorization check on publication status. This maps to insecure direct object reference / broken access control. Note: the exact CAPEC-126 name may vary in the official catalog; this is the closest available pattern for authorization bypass through a user-controlled resource identifier. descriptions.value:
FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass that allows non-approver case members to modify restricted tasks (those in Requested, Rejected, or Request Review status) through several indirect code paths that lacked the required approver permission check.

Affected operations include:
- Self-unassignment from a restricted task
- Reordering tasks, including indirectly moving restricted sibling tasks
- Linking or unlinking MISP objects and attributes to/from restricted tasks
- Creating MISP objects or standalone attributes with task IDs referencing restricted tasks
- Deleting MISP objects or attributes that are linked to restricted tasks
- Executing modules on restricted tasks

A user with case member access (but without Admin, Case Admin, or Queue Admin privileges) could exploit these paths to alter the state of tasks that are supposed to be locked pending approval, effectively bypassing the intended approval workflow and potentially manipulating associated MISP data.

Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0
CAPEC-100 Exploiting Incorrectly Adjusted Privileges

solutions.value: The fix enforces approver-level permission checks (is_task_restricted and can_edit_requested_task) before any state change on restricted tasks across all affected code paths. Checks are applied at both the model layer (TaskCore, CaseCore) and the API/view layer (case_api, case_misp, task), rejecting forbidden operations with a 403 response before any partial writes occur. Reordering additionally validates every affected restricted sibling task, and module execution requires approver permission before dispatch.

descriptions.value:
flowintel contains an authorization bypass in the browser-based admin user editing interface. The edit_user view in the admin panel verified that a non-platform-admin user could only edit accounts belonging to their own organization, but it did not verify that the target account was not a platform-admin account. As a result, an authenticated user holding an organization-admin role could open the edit form for any platform-admin account and submit modifications, including changes to credentials, roles, or other account attributes.

The API layer already enforced a restriction preventing non-admin users from targeting admin accounts, but the browser-based admin view lacked the equivalent check, creating an inconsistent authorization boundary.

Impact:
- Unauthorized modification of platform-admin account data (integrity)
- Potential lockout or privilege manipulation of platform administrators (availability)
- Escalation of an organization-admin role to effectively control platform-level administration

Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
CAPEC-100 Leveraging Broken Logic to Modify Access Controls

solutions.value: The fix adds an explicit authorization check in the browser-based user edit view that rejects the request before rendering or processing the form when the target account is a platform-admin account and the current user is not a platform administrator. This aligns the browser interface with the existing API-level restriction, ensuring that only platform administrators can modify platform-admin accounts.

cna.title: Authorization bypass in symfony/ux-live-component via an empty batch action request

descriptions.value:
A live component protected by #[IsGranted], on its class or on its default action, can be rendered by a caller who is not granted access. POST /_components/{name}/_batch is handled by Symfony\UX\LiveComponent\Controller\BatchActionController, which has no controller attributes: the attributes of the component are only checked by the sub-request issued for each action. With an empty actions list, no sub-request was issued, and the hydrated component was rendered and returned with a 200.

The caller needs a valid signed props payload for the component, such as the data-live-props-value of a page that rendered it: one the caller could see before losing access, or a cached or shared page. The checksum binds the props to the component name, not to a user, a session or a time, so such a payload can be replayed. Actions are not affected, since each action of a non-empty batch is still checked in its own sub-request. Components that load data from their props, like an entity identifier, disclose that data to the caller.

BatchActionController now rejects a batch without any action with a BadRequestHttpException. The JavaScript client never sends such a request: it uses the URL of the component when there is no action, /{action} for a single one and /_batch for two or more.
