cna.title: net/sched: cls_fw: fix NULL pointer dereference on shared blocks

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: cls_fw: fix NULL pointer dereference on shared blocks

The old-method path in fw_classify() calls tcf_block_q() and
dereferences q->handle.  Shared blocks leave block->q NULL, causing a
NULL deref when an empty cls_fw filter is attached to a shared block
and a packet with a nonzero major skb mark is classified.

Reject the configuration in fw_change() when the old method (no
TCA_OPTIONS) is used on a shared block, since fw_classify()'s
old-method path needs block->q which is NULL for shared blocks.

The fixed null-ptr-deref calling stack:
 KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000038-0x000000000000003f]
 RIP: 0010:fw_classify (net/sched/cls_fw.c:81)
 Call Trace:
  tcf_classify (./include/net/tc_wrapper.h:197 net/sched/cls_api.c:1764 net/sched/cls_api.c:1860)
  tc_run (net/core/dev.c:4401)
  __dev_queue_xmit (net/core/dev.c:4535 net/core/dev.c:4790)

cna.title: Parse Server has Stored XSS via file upload of HTML-renderable file types

descriptions.value: Parse Server is an open source backend that can be deployed to any infrastructure that can run Node.js. Prior to 9.6.0-alpha.4 and 8.6.30, an attacker can upload a file with a file extension or content type that is not blocked by the default configuration of the Parse Server fileUpload.fileExtensions option. The file can contain malicious code, for example JavaScript in an SVG or XHTML file. When the file is accessed via its URL, the browser renders the file and executes the malicious code in the context of the Parse Server domain. This is a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability that can be exploited to steal session tokens, redirect users, or perform actions on behalf of other users. Affected file extensions and content types include .svgz, .xht, .xml, .xsl, .xslt, and content types application/xhtml+xml and application/xslt+xml for extensionless uploads. Uploading of .html, .htm, .shtml, .xhtml, and .svg files was already blocked. This vulnerability is fixed in 9.6.0-alpha.4 and 8.6.30.

cna.title: motionEye: Arbitrary File Read via Path Traversal in Picture/Movie Preview Endpoint

descriptions.value: motionEye (mEye) is an online interface for motion software, which is a video surveillance program with motion detection. Versions prior to 0.44.0 are vulnerable to path traversal in the picture and movie API endpoints, suhc as /picture/{id}/preview/{filename}. Neither the API handlers, nor the mediafiles.py functions such as get_media_preview() check for .. sequences in the filename parameter, except for get_media_content(). This allows an authenticated user with normal (non-admin) privileges to read arbitrary files from the filesystem as the motionEye process user, such as:  /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, motionEye config files containing password hashes and plaintext passwords, SSH keys, and other cameras' surveillance footage. This issue has been fixed in version 0.44.0.

descriptions.value: BillaBear (all versions prior to Jan 2026) contains a SQL Injection vulnerability in the EventRepository. User-controlled input from metric filter names and aggregation properties is directly interpolated into SQL queries using sprintf() without proper sanitization or identifier quoting. Although filter values are parameterized, the filter identifiers (keys) are not. An authenticated attacker with ROLE_ACCOUNT_MANAGER permissions can exploit this to execute arbitrary SQL commands.

cna.title: netfilter: nf_conntrack_sip: fix use of uninitialized rtp_addr in process_sdp

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nf_conntrack_sip: fix use of uninitialized rtp_addr in process_sdp

process_sdp() declares union nf_inet_addr rtp_addr on the stack and
passes it to the nf_nat_sip sdp_session hook after walking the SDP
media descriptions. However rtp_addr is only initialized inside the
media loop when a recognized media type with a non-zero port is found.

If the SDP body contains no m= lines, only inactive media sections
(m=audio 0 ...) or only unrecognized media types, rtp_addr is never
assigned. Despite that, the function still calls hooks->sdp_session()
with &rtp_addr, causing nf_nat_sdp_session() to format the stale stack
value as an IP address and rewrite the SDP session owner and connection
lines with it.

With CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO (default on most distributions) this
results in the session-level o= and c= addresses being rewritten to
0.0.0.0 for inactive SDP sessions. Without stack auto-init the
rewritten address is whatever happened to be on the stack.

Fix this by pre-initializing rtp_addr from the session-level connection
address (caddr) when available, and tracking via a have_rtp_addr flag
whether any valid address was established. Skip the sdp_session hook
entirely when no valid address exists.

cna.title: Discourse has a poll authorization bypass via post_id array parameter

descriptions.value: Discourse is an open-source discussion platform. Prior to versions 2026.3.0-latest.1, 2026.2.1, and 2026.1.2, an authorization bypass in the poll plugin allowed authenticated users to vote on, remove votes from, or toggle the open/closed status of polls they did not have access to. By passing post_id as an array (e.g. post_id[]=&post_id[]=), the authorization check resolves to the accessible post while the poll lookup resolves to a different post's poll. This affects the vote, remove_vote, and toggle_status endpoints in DiscoursePoll::PollsController. Versions 2026.3.0-latest.1, 2026.2.1, and 2026.1.2 contain a patch.

cna.title: crypto: af_alg - limit RX SG extraction by receive buffer budget

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

crypto: af_alg - limit RX SG extraction by receive buffer budget

Make af_alg_get_rsgl() limit each RX scatterlist extraction to the
remaining receive buffer budget.

af_alg_get_rsgl() currently uses af_alg_readable() only as a gate
before extracting data into the RX scatterlist. Limit each extraction
to the remaining af_alg_rcvbuf(sk) budget so that receive-side
accounting matches the amount of data attached to the request.

If skcipher cannot obtain enough RX space for at least one chunk while
more data remains to be processed, reject the recvmsg call instead of
rounding the request length down to zero.

cna.title: Vaultwarden WebAuthn credential metadata tampered before signature verification

descriptions.value: Vaultwarden is a Bitwarden-compatible server written in Rust. In versions 1.35.4 and earlier, the WebAuthn authentication flow in `validate_webauthn_login()` updates persistent credential metadata (1backup_eligible1 and 1backup_state flags1) based on unverified `authenticatorData` before signature validation is performed. An attacker who knows a user's password but cannot produce a valid WebAuthn signature can permanently modify the stored backup flags for that user's credential. If signature verification fails, the database update is not rolled back. This can result in a persistent denial of service of WebAuthn two-factor authentication for affected credentials. This issue has been fixed in version 1.35.5.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ext4: replace BUG_ON with proper error handling in ext4_read_inline_folio

Replace BUG_ON() with proper error handling when inline data size

descriptions.value: The TinyZero project thru commit 6652a63c57fa7e5ccde3fc9c598c7176ff15b839 (2025-58-24) contains a critical command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in its HDFS file operation utilities. The vulnerability arises from the unsafe construction and execution of shell commands via os.system() without proper input sanitization or escaping. User-controlled input (such as file paths) is directly interpolated into shell command strings using f-strings within the _copy() function. An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands by supplying a specially crafted path parameter through the Hydra configuration framework. This leads to remote code execution with the privileges of the user running the TinyZero training process.

cna.title: openvswitch: validate MPLS set/set_masked payload length

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The vulnerable path is reached through Open vSwitch generic netlink commands that install or execute datapath actions, not by unauthenticated remote packets alone.
AC:L - An attacker can craft the malformed MPLS SET/SET_MASKED netlink attributes and an MPLS packet directly; there is no race or victim-controlled timing requirement.
PR:L - The relevant OVS commands require CAP_NET_ADMIN, but the families are netns-aware and use GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM, making them reachable with CAP_NET_ADMIN in a user-created network namespace.
UI:N - No victim interaction is required once the attacker can send the crafted netlink request or trigger the installed action.
S:U - The impact remains within the kernel/host networking security authority and does not cross a VM, IOMMU, or similar scope boundary.
C:H - The invalid MPLS payload length can make action execution read beyond the validated netlink action data from kernel heap storage. Although each read is small, repeated attacker-controlled triggering and heap layout influence make high confidentiality impact the safer defensible choice.
I:N - The bug causes out-of-bounds reads and attacker-influenced packet MPLS rewriting, but it does not provide a kernel memory write primitive or control-flow modification.
A:H - The out-of-bounds kernel heap read can trigger a kernel fault or sanitizer-detected panic, and the crafted action can be exercised repeatedly without user interaction.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

openvswitch: validate MPLS set/set_masked payload length

validate_set() accepted OVS_KEY_ATTR_MPLS as variable-sized payload for
SET/SET_MASKED actions. In action handling, OVS expects fixed-size
MPLS key data (struct ovs_key_mpls).

Use the already normalized key_len (masked case included) and reject
non-matching MPLS action key sizes.

Reject invalid MPLS action payload lengths early.

descriptions.value: The imgaug library thru 0.4.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in its BackgroundAugmenter class within the multicore.py module. The class uses Python's pickle module to deserialize data received via a multiprocessing queue in the _augment_images_worker() method without any safety checks. cna.title: xfrm: prevent policy_hthresh.work from racing with netns teardown

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The vulnerable path is reached by a local NETLINK_XFRM request, specifically XFRM_MSG_NEWSPDINFO, not by remote packet processing.
AC:L - The attacker can create the net namespace, send the request that queues policy_hthresh.work, and tear the namespace down; this is an attacker-controlled race and can be retried.
PR:L - XFRM netlink operations require CAP_NET_ADMIN over the target network namespace. This is reachable with low privileges via user and network namespaces rather than requiring real init-namespace root.
UI:N - No victim action is required after the attacker has local execution; the attacker directly drives the netlink request and namespace teardown.
S:U - The impact is within the kernel security authority and does not cross a separate boundary such as guest-to-host or IOMMU isolation.
C:H - The bug is a use-after-free of struct net reached by queued work dereferencing stale namespace memory. Under the required conservative kernel scoring guidance, UAF memory corruption is treated as capable of high confidentiality impact.
I:H - The stale work callback writes through fields in the freed struct net and manipulates policy lists and hash state. As a kernel UAF, this is defensibly scored as high integrity impact due to potential memory corruption and control-flow exploitation.
A:H - The stale struct net dereference can crash or corrupt the kernel during workqueue execution. Kernel crashes and UAF-triggered failures are high availability impact.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfrm: prevent policy_hthresh.work from racing with netns teardown

A XFRM_MSG_NEWSPDINFO request can queue the per-net work item
policy_hthresh.work onto the system workqueue.

The queued callback, xfrm_hash_rebuild(), retrieves the enclosing
struct net via container_of(). If the net namespace is torn down
before that work runs, the associated struct net may already have
been freed, and xfrm_hash_rebuild() may then dereference stale memory.

xfrm_policy_fini() already flushes policy_hash_work during teardown,
but it does not synchronize policy_hthresh.work.

Synchronize policy_hthresh.work in xfrm_policy_fini() as well, so the
queued work cannot outlive the net namespace teardown and access a
freed struct net.

cna.title: media: em28xx: fix use-after-free in em28xx_v4l2_open()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: em28xx: fix use-after-free in em28xx_v4l2_open()

em28xx_v4l2_open() reads dev->v4l2 without holding dev->lock,
creating a race with em28xx_v4l2_init()'s error path and
em28xx_v4l2_fini(), both of which free the em28xx_v4l2 struct
and set dev->v4l2 to NULL under dev->lock.

This race leads to two issues:
 - use-after-free in v4l2_fh_init() when accessing vdev->ctrl_handler,
   since the video_device is embedded in the freed em28xx_v4l2 struct.
 - NULL pointer dereference in em28xx_resolution_set() when accessing
   v4l2->norm, since dev->v4l2 has been set to NULL.

Fix this by moving the mutex_lock() before the dev->v4l2 read and
adding a NULL check for dev->v4l2 under the lock.

cna.title: Dagu SSE Authentication Bypass in Basic Auth Mode

descriptions.value: Dagu is a workflow engine with a built-in Web user interface. Prior to 2.2.4, when Dagu is configured with HTTP Basic authentication (DAGU_AUTH_MODE=basic), all Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoints are accessible without any credentials. This allows unauthenticated attackers to access real-time DAG execution data, workflow configurations, execution logs, and queue status — bypassing the authentication that protects the REST API. The buildStreamAuthOptions() function builds authentication options for SSE/streaming endpoints. When the auth mode is basic, it returns an auth.Options struct with BasicAuthEnabled: true but AuthRequired defaults to false (Go zero value). The authentication middleware at internal/service/frontend/auth/middleware.go allows unauthenticated requests when AuthRequired is false. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.2.4.

descriptions.description: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

cna.title: Cockpit CMS has SQL Injection in MongoLite Aggregation Optimizer via toJsonExtractRaw()

descriptions.value: Cockpit is a headless content management system. Any Cockpit CMS instance running version 2.13.4 or earlier with API access enabled is potentially affected by a a SQL Injection vulnerability in the MongoLite Aggregation Optimizer. Any deployment where the `/api/content/aggregate/{model}` endpoint is publicly accessible or reachable by untrusted users may be vulnerable, and attackers in possession of a valid read-only API key (the lowest privilege level) can exploit this vulnerability — no admin access is required. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via unsanitized field names in aggregation queries, bypass the `_state=1` published-content filter to access unpublished or restricted content, and extract unauthorized data from the underlying SQLite content database. This vulnerability has been patched in version 2.13.5. The fix applies the same field-name sanitization introduced in v2.13.3 for `toJsonPath()` to the `toJsonExtractRaw()` method in `lib/MongoLite/Aggregation/Optimizer.php`, closing the injection vector in the Aggregation Optimizer.

descriptions.description: CWE-776 Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')

descriptions.value: Docling's METS GBS backend is vulnerable to XML Entity Expansion (XXE) attacks thru 2.61.0. The backend extracts and validates XML files from .tar.gz archives using etree.fromstring() without disabling entity resolution. An attacker can craft a malicious XML file with nested entity definitions (XML Bomb) and package it into a .tar.gz archive. When processed by Docling, the exponential expansion of entities during XML parsing leads to excessive resource consumption, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition on the system running the Docling parser.

cna.title: HID: magicmouse: avoid memory leak in magicmouse_report_fixup()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: magicmouse: avoid memory leak in magicmouse_report_fixup()

The magicmouse_report_fixup() function was returning a
newly kmemdup()-allocated buffer, but never freeing it.

The caller of report_fixup() does not take ownership of the returned
pointer, but it *is* permitted to return a sub-portion of the input
rdesc, whose lifetime is managed by the caller.

cna.title: OOBR in libpcap before 1.10.7

exploits.value: A functional exploit exists.

solutions.value: Upgrade to libpcap 1.10.7 and migrate from bpf_filter() to pcap_offline_filter().

descriptions.value: libpcap BPF interpreter detects neither reaching the end of the filter program buffer due to lack of a return instruction nor executing a jump instruction with an offset that translates to a pointer outside of the buffer.  In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause the interpreter to try reading the OS process memory in the 32GiB around the buffer on 64-bit architectures and in the entire address space on 32-bit architectures.

descriptions.description: CWE-1285 Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input
CWE-823 Use of Out-of-range Pointer Offset

configurations.value: The problem is specific to applications that use pcap_offline_filter() or bpf_filter() with an externally-supplied compiled filter program without validating the program first.

cna.title: FreeRDP has a `size_t` underflow in ADPCM decoder leads to heap-buffer-overflow write

descriptions.value: FreeRDP is a free implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol. Prior to 3.24.0, a size_t underflow in the IMA-ADPCM and MS-ADPCM audio decoders leads to heap-buffer-overflow write via the RDPSND audio channel. In libfreerdp/codec/dsp.c, the IMA-ADPCM and MS-ADPCM decoders subtract block header sizes from a size_t variable without checking for underflow. When nBlockAlign (received from the server) is set such that size % block_size == 0 triggers the header parsing at a point where size is smaller than the header (4 or 8 bytes), the subtraction wraps size to ~SIZE_MAX. The while (size > 0) loop then continues for an astronomical number of iterations. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.24.0.

cna.title: HTSlib CRAM reader has out-of-bounds read due to improper validation of input

descriptions.value: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. CRAM is a compressed format which stores DNA sequence alignment data. In the `cram_decode_slice()` function called while reading CRAM records, the value of the mate reference id field was not validated. Later use of this value, for example when converting the data to SAM format, could result in the out of bounds array reads when looking up the corresponding reference name. If the array value obtained also happened to be a valid pointer, it would be interpreted as a string and an attempt would be made to write the data as part of the SAM record. This bug may allow information about program state to be leaked. It may also cause a program crash through an attempt to access invalid memory. Versions 1.23.1, 1.22.2 and 1.21.1 include fixes for this issue. There is no workaround for this issue.

workarounds.value:
To mitigate this issue, if SMB client functionality is not required, the `cifs` kernel module can be blacklisted to prevent it from loading. This can be achieved by creating a modprobe configuration file.

1. Create a file named `/etc/modprobe.d/disable-cifs.conf` with the following content:
   ```
   install cifs /bin/true
   blacklist cifs
   ```
2. Regenerate the initramfs to ensure the change takes effect on boot:
   ```bash
   dracut -f -v
   ```
   or for systems using `mkinitrd`:
   ```bash
   mkinitrd -f /boot/initramfs-$(uname -r).img $(uname -r)
   ```
3. A system reboot is required for the changes to take effect.

Warning: Disabling the `cifs` module will prevent the system from mounting SMB/CIFS shares. Ensure this functionality is not critical before applying this mitigation.

refer: https://access.redhat.com/solutions/4117281

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's Server Message Block (SMB) client, specifically within the cifsacl functionality. A malicious SMB server could provide a malformed Discretionary Access Control List (DACL) that claims to contain more Access Control Entries (ACEs) than are actually present. This insufficient validation allows the kernel to read or copy data beyond the intended memory boundaries, leading to memory corruption. This could potentially result in information disclosure or a denial of service.

descriptions.description: Improper Validation of Consistency within Input

cna.title: smb: client: validate the whole DACL before rewriting it in cifsacl

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The vulnerable DACL is supplied by an SMB server over network SMB/CIFS ACL query responses and parsed by the Linux SMB client in kernel context. A malicious or compromised SMB server can deliver the crafted security descriptor over TCP.
AC:L - After the client reaches the CIFS ACL path, the attacker controls the DACL offsets, sizes, ACE count, and ACE bytes in the server response. There is no race or condition outside attacker control needed to trigger the malformed ACE walk.
PR:N - The attacker needs no privileges on the victim system; they only need to act as or control the SMB server that the client uses. Local chmod/chown permission checks apply to the victim-side process, not to the remote attacker.
UI:R - Exploitation requires the victim system or an automated victim workflow to mount/use the SMB share and issue metadata operations such as stat, chmod, chown, or chgrp. The server cannot trigger this parser without a client request.
S:U - The vulnerable component and the impacted resource are the same Linux kernel security authority on the SMB client. This is not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-authority boundary violation.
C:H - The malformed DACL can drive out-of-bounds reads while copying ACE/SID data, and rewritten ACL data can be sent back to the malicious server. Under the required high-severity tie-break rule, this is treated as high confidentiality impact.
I:H - The chown/chgrp rewrite path can copy attacker-influenced ACEs into a newly allocated security descriptor beyond the size derived from the declared DACL, creating kernel heap memory corruption. Such corruption is potentially exploitable for arbitrary write or code execution.
A:H - Malformed server-controlled ACL structures can drive out-of-bounds kernel memory access during ACL parsing or rewriting. Even without full exploitation, this can crash or oops the kernel.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: validate the whole DACL before rewriting it in cifsacl

build_sec_desc() and id_mode_to_cifs_acl() derive a DACL pointer from a
server-supplied dacloffset and then use the incoming ACL to rebuild the
chmod/chown security descriptor.

The original fix only checked that the struct smb_acl header fits before
reading dacl_ptr->size or dacl_ptr->num_aces.  That avoids the immediate
header-field OOB read, but the rewrite helpers still walk ACEs based on
pdacl->num_aces with no structural validation of the incoming DACL body.

A malicious server can return a truncated DACL that still contains a
header, claims one or more ACEs, and then drive
replace_sids_and_copy_aces() or set_chmod_dacl() past the validated
extent while they compare or copy attacker-controlled ACEs.

Factor the DACL structural checks into validate_dacl(), extend them to
validate each ACE against the DACL bounds, and use the shared validator
before the chmod/chown rebuild paths.  parse_dacl() reuses the same
validator so the read-side parser and write-side rewrite paths agree on
what constitutes a well-formed incoming DACL.

cna.title: net: rfkill: prevent unlimited numbers of rfkill events from being created

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: rfkill: prevent unlimited numbers of rfkill events from being created

Userspace can create an unlimited number of rfkill events if the system
is so configured, while not consuming them from the rfkill file
descriptor, causing a potential out of memory situation.  Prevent this
from bounding the number of pending rfkill events at a "large" number
(i.e. 1000) to prevent abuses like this.

descriptions.value: Xibo is an open source digital signage platform with a web content management system and Windows display player software. Versions 1.7 through 4.4.0 have an SQL injection vulnerability in the API routes inside the CMS responsible for Filtering DataSets. This allows an authenticated user to to obtain and modify arbitrary data from the Xibo database by injecting specially crafted values in to the API filter parameter. Exploitation of the vulnerability is possible on behalf of an authorized user who has either of the `Access to DataSet Feature` privilege or the `Access to the Layout Feature` privilege. Users should upgrade to version 4.4.1 which fixes this issue. Customers who host their CMS with Xibo Signage have been patched if they are using 4.4, 4.3, 3.3, 2.3 or 1.8. Upgrading to a fixed version is necessary to remediate. Patches are available for earlier versions of Xibo CMS that are out of support, namely 3.3, 2.3, and 1.8.

descriptions.value: Parse Server is an open source backend that can be deployed to any infrastructure that can run Node.js. Prior to 9.5.2-alpha.13 and 8.6.26, the LDAP authentication adapter is vulnerable to LDAP injection. User-supplied input (authData.id) is interpolated directly into LDAP Distinguished Names (DN) and group search filters without escaping special characters. This allows an attacker with valid LDAP credentials to manipulate the bind DN structure and to bypass group membership checks. This enables privilege escalation from any authenticated LDAP user to a member of any restricted group. The vulnerability affects Parse Server deployments that use the LDAP authentication adapter with group-based access control. This vulnerability is fixed in 9.5.2-alpha.13 and 8.6.26.

cna.title: s390/mm: Add missing secure storage access fixups for donated memory

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/mm: Add missing secure storage access fixups for donated memory

There are special cases where secure storage access exceptions happen
in a kernel context for pages that don't have the PG_arch_1 bit
set. That bit is set for non-exported guest secure storage (memory)
but is absent on storage donated to the Ultravisor since the kernel
isn't allowed to export donated pages.

Prior to this patch we would try to export the page by calling
arch_make_folio_accessible() which would instantly return since the
arch bit is absent signifying that the page was already exported and
no further action is necessary. This leads to secure storage access
exception loops which can never be resolved.

With this patch we unconditionally try to export and if that fails we
fixup.

cna.title: KVM: SEV: Lock all vCPUs when synchronzing VMSAs for SNP launch finish

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: SEV: Lock all vCPUs when synchronzing VMSAs for SNP launch finish

Lock all vCPUs when synchronizing and encrypting VMSAs for SNP guests, as
allowing userspace to manipulate and/or run a vCPU while its state is being
synchronized would at best corrupt vCPU state, and at worst crash the host
kernel.

Opportunistically assert that vcpu->mutex is held when synchronizing its
VMSA (the SEV-ES path already locks vCPUs).

Horovod thru 0.28.1 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability (CWE-502) in its KVStore HTTP server component. The KVStore server, used for distributed task coordination, lacks authentication and authorization controls, allowing any remote attacker to write arbitrary data via HTTP PUT requests. When a Horovod worker reads data from the KVStore (via HTTP GET), it deserializes the data using cloudpickle.loads() without verifying its source or integrity. An attacker can exploit this by sending a malicious pickle payload to the server before the legitimate data is written, causing the victim worker to deserialize and execute arbitrary code, leading to remote code execution.

cna.title: Bluetooth: btintel: serialize btintel_hw_error() with hci_req_sync_lock

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: btintel: serialize btintel_hw_error() with hci_req_sync_lock

btintel_hw_error() issues two __hci_cmd_sync() calls (HCI_OP_RESET
and Intel exception-info retrieval) without holding
hci_req_sync_lock().  This lets it race against
hci_dev_do_close() -> btintel_shutdown_combined(), which also runs
__hci_cmd_sync() under the same lock.  When both paths manipulate
hdev->req_status/req_rsp concurrently, the close path may free the
response skb first, and the still-running hw_error path hits a
slab-use-after-free in kfree_skb().

Wrap the whole recovery sequence in hci_req_sync_lock/unlock so it
is serialized with every other synchronous HCI command issuer.

Below is the data race report and the kasan report:

  BUG: data-race in __hci_cmd_sync_sk / btintel_shutdown_combined

  read of hdev->req_rsp at net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c:199

   __hci_cmd_sync+0x55/0x80 net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c:223
   btintel_hw_error+0x114/0x670 drivers/bluetooth/btintel.c:254

cna.title: ipv6: avoid overflows in ip6_datagram_send_ctl()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: avoid overflows in ip6_datagram_send_ctl()

Yiming Qian reported :
<quote>
 I believe I found a locally triggerable kernel bug in the IPv6 sendmsg
 ancillary-data path that can panic the kernel via `skb_under_panic()`
 (local DoS).

 The core issue is a mismatch between:

 - a 16-bit length accumulator (`struct ipv6_txoptions::opt_flen`, type
 `__u16`) and
 - a pointer to the *last* provided destination-options header (`opt->dst1opt`)

 when multiple `IPV6_DSTOPTS` control messages (cmsgs) are provided.

 - `include/net/ipv6.h`:
   - `struct ipv6_txoptions::opt_flen` is `__u16` (wrap possible).
 (lines 291-307, especially 298)
 - `net/ipv6/datagram.c:ip6_datagram_send_ctl()`:
   - Accepts repeated `IPV6_DSTOPTS` and accumulates into `opt_flen`
 without rejecting duplicates. (lines 909-933)
 - `net/ipv6/ip6_output.c:__ip6_append_data()`:
   - Uses `opt->opt_flen + opt->opt_nflen` to compute header
 sizes/headroom decisions. (lines 1448-1466, especially 1463-1465)
 - `net/ipv6/ip6_output.c:__ip6_make_skb()`:
   - Calls `ipv6_push_frag_opts()` if `opt->opt_flen` is non-zero.
 (lines 1930-1934)
 - `net/ipv6/exthdrs.c:ipv6_push_frag_opts()` / `ipv6_push_exthdr()`:
   - Push size comes from `ipv6_optlen(opt->dst1opt)` (based on the
 pointed-to header). (lines 1179-1185 and 1206-1211)

 1. `opt_flen` is a 16-bit accumulator:

 - `include/net/ipv6.h:298` defines `__u16 opt_flen; /* after fragment hdr */`.

 2. `ip6_datagram_send_ctl()` accepts *repeated* `IPV6_DSTOPTS` cmsgs
 and increments `opt_flen` each time:

 - In `net/ipv6/datagram.c:909-933`, for `IPV6_DSTOPTS`:
   - It computes `len = ((hdr->hdrlen + 1) << 3);`
   - It checks `CAP_NET_RAW` using `ns_capable(net->user_ns,
 CAP_NET_RAW)`. (line 922)
   - Then it does:
     - `opt->opt_flen += len;` (line 927)
     - `opt->dst1opt = hdr;` (line 928)

 There is no duplicate rejection here (unlike the legacy
 `IPV6_2292DSTOPTS` path which rejects duplicates at
 `net/ipv6/datagram.c:901-904`).

 If enough large `IPV6_DSTOPTS` cmsgs are provided, `opt_flen` wraps
 while `dst1opt` still points to a large (2048-byte)
 destination-options header.

 In the attached PoC (`poc.c`):

 - 32 cmsgs with `hdrlen=255` => `len = (255+1)*8 = 2048`
 - 1 cmsg with `hdrlen=0` => `len = 8`
 - Total increment: `32*2048 + 8 = 65544`, so `(__u16)opt_flen == 8`
 - The last cmsg is 2048 bytes, so `dst1opt` points to a 2048-byte header.

 3. The transmit path sizes headers using the wrapped `opt_flen`:

- In `net/ipv6/ip6_output.c:1463-1465`:
  - `headersize = sizeof(struct ipv6hdr) + (opt ? opt->opt_flen +
 opt->opt_nflen : 0) + ...;`

 With wrapped `opt_flen`, `headersize`/headroom decisions underestimate
 what will be pushed later.

 4. When building the final skb, the actual push length comes from
 `dst1opt` and is not limited by wrapped `opt_flen`:

 - In `net/ipv6/ip6_output.c:1930-1934`:
   - `if (opt->opt_flen) proto = ipv6_push_frag_opts(skb, opt, proto);`
 - In `net/ipv6/exthdrs.c:1206-1211`, `ipv6_push_frag_opts()` pushes
 `dst1opt` via `ipv6_push_exthdr()`.
 - In `net/ipv6/exthdrs.c:1179-1184`, `ipv6_push_exthdr()` does:
   - `skb_push(skb, ipv6_optlen(opt));`
   - `memcpy(h, opt, ipv6_optlen(opt));`

 With insufficient headroom, `skb_push()` underflows and triggers
 `skb_under_panic()` -> `BUG()`:

 - `net/core/skbuff.c:2669-2675` (`skb_push()` calls `skb_under_panic()`)
 - `net/core/skbuff.c:207-214` (`skb_panic()` ends in `BUG()`)

 - The `IPV6_DSTOPTS` cmsg path requires `CAP_NET_RAW` in the target
 netns user namespace (`ns_capable(net->user_ns, CAP_NET_RAW)`).
 - Root (or any task with `CAP_NET_RAW`) can trigger this without user
 namespaces.
 - An unprivileged `uid=1000` user can trigger this if unprivileged
 user namespaces are enabled and it can create a userns+netns to obtain
 namespaced `CAP_NET_RAW` (the attached PoC does this).

 - Local denial of service: kernel BUG/panic (system crash).
 -

cna.title: crypto: ccp: Don't attempt to copy PDH cert to userspace if PSP command failed

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The vulnerable code is reached through the local `/dev/sev` misc device via the `SEV_ISSUE_CMD` ioctl and `SEV_PDH_CERT_EXPORT` command, not by network or adjacent packets.
AC:L - An attacker who can access `/dev/sev` can supply undersized nonzero certificate buffers and reliably make firmware return the required larger lengths; no race or hard-to-influence condition is required.
PR:L - The kernel path has no capability check, and although `/dev/sev` is often root-restricted by default, SEV-capable hosts commonly delegate access to non-root virtualization users or groups; using the higher-severity reasonable case makes this low privileges.
UI:N - No victim action is required after the attacker has local access to the device; the ioctl directly triggers the vulnerable path.
S:U - The bug leaks or crashes kernel memory in the same host kernel security authority; it is not a VM escape or other cross-scope boundary violation by itself.
C:H - The failed firmware command overwrites the returned lengths with larger required sizes, and the vulnerable code copies that many bytes from smaller kernel heap buffers to userspace, producing an out-of-bounds kernel memory disclosure.
I:N - The bug is an out-of-bounds read during `copy_to_user`, with no direct write, memory corruption, or control-flow modification primitive.
A:H - The same out-of-bounds usercopy is reported as a KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read and can also trip hardened usercopy BUG/oops paths on hardened kernels, making a kernel crash a defensible impact.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

crypto: ccp: Don't attempt to copy PDH cert to userspace if PSP command failed

When retrieving the PDH cert, don't attempt to copy the blobs to userspace
if the firmware command failed.  If the failure was due to an invalid
length, i.e. the userspace buffer+length was too small, copying the number
of bytes _firmware_ requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and
leak data to userspace.

cna.title: smb: smbdirect: introduce smbdirect_socket.recv_io.credits.available

scenarios.value:
AV:N - SMBDirect is reached by a remote RDMA peer through RDMA CM listeners on SMBDirect/SMB ports such as 5445 and 445. The ksmbd server path processes the affected negotiation and data-transfer credit handling from network-originated RDMA messages.
AC:L - The issue is a receive-credit accounting race, but the remote peer can repeatedly drive both message arrival and credit-request/response behavior with crafted SMBDirect traffic. No unusual victim state or uncontrollable condition is required beyond an enabled SMBDirect RDMA deployment.
PR:N - The server-side path accepts the RDMA connection and performs SMBDirect negotiation and data-transfer credit handling before SMB session authentication. A remote peer does not need SMB credentials to reach the vulnerable credit logic.
UI:N - Exploitation against the server path requires only network/RDMA traffic from the attacker. No local user or administrator action is needed after the service is exposed.
S:U - The impact remains within the kernel SMBDirect/SMB service security authority. There is no VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-authority boundary crossing.
C:N - The bug overgrants receive credits but does not expose a kernel read primitive; incoming payload bounds are checked before reassembly. An RDMA send without a posted receive should produce transport/RNR failure rather than disclose memory.
I:N - The investigation did not identify an arbitrary write or memory-corruption primitive. The false credit causes receive-queue/transport state inconsistency, not attacker-controlled modification of kernel data.
A:H - False credits can allow the peer to send when no real receive buffer is posted, causing RDMA QP/transport errors and SMBDirect disconnects with RNR retries disabled. Because this is remotely and unauthenticatedly repeatable against the exposed SMBDirect service, availability impact is high.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: introduce smbdirect_socket.recv_io.credits.available

The logic off managing recv credits by counting posted recv_io and
granted credits is racy.

That's because the peer might already consumed a credit,
but between receiving the incoming recv at the hardware
and processing the completion in the 'recv_done' functions
we likely have a window where we grant credits, which
don't really exist.

So we better have a decicated counter for the
available credits, which will be incremented
when we posted new recv buffers and drained when
we grant the credits to the peer.

cna.title: DoS in Quill via unbounded read of HTTP response body during notarization

descriptions.value: Quill provides simple mac binary signing and notarization from any platform. Quill before version v0.7.1 has unbounded reads of HTTP response bodies during the Apple notarization process. Exploitation requires the ability to modify API responses from Apple's notarization service, which is not possible under standard network conditions due to HTTPS with proper TLS certificate validation; however, environments with TLS-intercepting proxies (common in corporate networks), compromised certificate authorities, or other trust boundary violations are at risk. When processing HTTP responses during notarization, Quill reads the entire response body into memory without any size limit. An attacker who can control or modify the response content can return an arbitrarily large payload, causing the Quill client to run out of memory and crash. The impact is limited to availability; there is no effect on confidentiality or integrity. Both the Quill CLI and library are affected when used to perform notarization operations. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.7.1.

cna.title: smb: client: fix OOB reads parsing symlink error response

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The crafted data is delivered over SMB by a remote SMB server in response to client CREATE/path-info operations. A malicious server can trigger the parser once the victim connects to or uses the share.
AC:L - The attacker controls the relevant SMB error context fields, offsets, and lengths in a single response. No race or condition outside attacker control is required.
PR:N - The attacker needs no privileges on the victim system; they only need to operate or impersonate the SMB server endpoint. SMB session setup is victim-side interaction, not attacker privilege.
UI:R - A victim must mount/connect to the SMB share or access a path on an already-mounted share. The server cannot trigger the vulnerable client path without such client activity.
S:U - The bug affects the kernel SMB client and exposes or disrupts resources within the same client security authority. It does not cross a VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary.
C:H - The malformed symlink error response can make kernel heap bytes past the received SMB buffer get UTF-16 decoded into the symlink target and returned to userspace. The over-read is not strictly limited to only a few bytes in the error-context case.
I:N - The bug is an out-of-bounds read, not a write or control-flow primitive. The malicious server already controls symlink response contents, so this adds disclosure and possible crash impact rather than data modification.
A:H - The unchecked over-read occurs in kernel parsing/conversion paths and can read beyond the allocated receive buffer, which can fault or oops the kernel. A malicious server can also repeatedly trigger the malformed response when the client accesses the path.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix OOB reads parsing symlink error response

When a CREATE returns STATUS_STOPPED_ON_SYMLINK, smb2_check_message()
returns success without any length validation, leaving the symlink
parsers as the only defense against an untrusted server.

symlink_data() walks SMB 3.1.1 error contexts with the loop test "p <
end", but reads p->ErrorId at offset 4 and p->ErrorDataLength at offset
0.  When the server-controlled ErrorDataLength advances p to within 1-7
bytes of end, the next iteration will read past it.  When the matching
context is found, sym->SymLinkErrorTag is read at offset 4 from
p->ErrorContextData with no check that the symlink header itself fits.

smb2_parse_symlink_response() then bounds-checks the substitute name
using SMB2_SYMLINK_STRUCT_SIZE as the offset of PathBuffer from
iov_base.  That value is computed as sizeof(smb2_err_rsp) +
sizeof(smb2_symlink_err_rsp), which is correct only when
ErrorContextCount == 0.

With at least one error context the symlink data sits 8 bytes deeper,
and each skipped non-matching context shifts it further by 8 +
ALIGN(ErrorDataLength, 8).  The check is too short, allowing the
substitute name read to run past iov_len.  The out-of-bound heap bytes
are UTF-16-decoded into the symlink target and returned to userspace via
readlink(2).

Fix this all up by making the loops test require the full context header
to fit, rejecting sym if its header runs past end, and bound the
substitute name against the actual position of sym->PathBuffer rather
than a fixed offset.

Because sub_offs and sub_len are 16bits, the pointer math will not
overflow here with the new greater-than.

cna.title: bpf: Fix exception exit lock checking for subprogs

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf: Fix exception exit lock checking for subprogs

process_bpf_exit_full() passes check_lock = !curframe to
check_resource_leak(), which is false in cases when bpf_throw() is
called from a static subprog. This makes check_resource_leak() to skip
validation of active_rcu_locks, active_preempt_locks, and
active_irq_id on exception exits from subprogs.

At runtime bpf_throw() unwinds the stack via ORC without releasing any
user-acquired locks, which may cause various issues as the result.

Fix by setting check_lock = true for exception exits regardless of
curframe, since exceptions bypass all intermediate frame
cleanup. Update the error message prefix to "bpf_throw" for exception
exits to distinguish them from normal BPF_EXIT.

Fix reject_subprog_with_rcu_read_lock test which was previously
passing for the wrong reason. Test program returned directly from the
subprog call without closing the RCU section, so the error was
triggered by the unclosed RCU lock on normal exit, not by
bpf_throw. Update __msg annotations for affected tests to match the
new "bpf_throw" error prefix.

The spin_lock case is not affected because they are already checked [1]
at the call site in do_check_insn() before bpf_throw can run.

[1] https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/kernel/bpf/verifier.c?h=v7.0-rc4#n21098

credits.value: Calvin Kirs, Security Researcher at SelectDB

descriptions.value:
An Improper Authentication vulnerability in the Apache Doris Frontend (FE) meta service allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access internal metadata service endpoints.



The affected endpoints relied on client-supplied node information for authentication without providing sufficient authentication of the requesting party. Under certain network configurations, a remote attacker may be able to bypass the intended access control and access internal FE metadata interfaces, potentially exposing sensitive cluster information.



This issue affects Apache Doris: from 2.0.0 through 2.0.*, from 2.1.0 through 2.1.*, from 3.0.0 through 3.0.*, from 3.1.0 through 3.1.*, from 4.0.0 before 4.0.8, and from 4.1.0 before 4.1.4. Versions 1.2.x and earlier are not affected by this header-trust vulnerability.




Users are recommended to upgrade to a fixed release (4.0.8 or 4.1.4), which fixes the issue.

cna.title: bpf: Fix undefined behavior in interpreter sdiv/smod for INT_MIN

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The vulnerable interpreter code is reached by locally loading and executing a crafted eBPF program through the bpf() syscall, or by attaching/running that program through local BPF interfaces. It is not reachable directly from unauthenticated network packets without first installing attacker-controlled BPF locally.
AC:L - There is no race or probabilistic prerequisite; the attacker controls the BPF arithmetic operands and can deterministically create the verifier/interpreter mismatch. The interpreter/JIT setting is an affected-deployment precondition, not exploit complexity once present.
PR:L - A basic local user can reach BPF program and unprivileged map creation on systems with unprivileged BPF enabled for permitted program types such as socket filters. If disabled, higher privileges or delegation are needed, but the highest reasonable affected deployment supports PR:L.
UI:N - The attacker can load and run or attach the malicious BPF program directly. No victim action is required.
S:U - The impact is compromise of kernel memory and privileges within the same operating-system security authority. This is standard local kernel privilege escalation rather than a VM or hardware boundary escape.
C:H - The verifier/interpreter mismatch can be exploited for out-of-bounds BPF map value access. Such map OOB access can disclose kernel memory and be shaped into stronger read primitives.
I:H - Out-of-bounds map value writes allow kernel memory corruption. In BPF verifier-style bugs, this is defensibly exploitable for arbitrary write, privilege escalation, or control-flow compromise.
A:H - The same out-of-bounds kernel memory access can corrupt critical state and crash or panic the kernel. The malicious program can be executed repeatedly by the local attacker.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf: Fix undefined behavior in interpreter sdiv/smod for INT_MIN

The BPF interpreter's signed 32-bit division and modulo handlers use
the kernel abs() macro on s32 operands. The abs() macro documentation
(include/linux/math.h) explicitly states the result is undefined when
the input is the type minimum. When DST contains S32_MIN (0x80000000),
abs((s32)DST) triggers undefined behavior and returns S32_MIN unchanged
on arm64/x86. This value is then sign-extended to u64 as
0xFFFFFFFF80000000, causing do_div() to compute the wrong result.

The verifier's abstract interpretation (scalar32_min_max_sdiv) computes
the mathematically correct result for range tracking, creating a
verifier/interpreter mismatch that can be exploited for out-of-bounds
map value access.

Introduce abs_s32() which handles S32_MIN correctly by casting to u32
before negating, avoiding signed overflow entirely. Replace all 8
abs((s32)...) call sites in the interpreter's sdiv32/smod32 handlers.

s32 is the only affected case -- the s64 division/modulo handlers do
not use abs().

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When a task marked `no_log: true` fails, the task result is censored before being emitted, but the `exception` field is retained because it is present in the PRESERVE allow-list in lib/ansible/_internal/_task.py, and the default stdout callback prints it through CallbackBase._handle_exception. As a result, sensitive values the operator explicitly asked to hide can be disclosed: module argument-validation errors echo the argument value, templating errors print an Origin source snippet (the failing line plus the two preceding lines of the variables file, exposing neighbouring secrets from an -e @secrets.yml file), and fail/assert messages are printed in full. Secret material supplied as extra variables or variables files can therefore leak to terminal output, CI logs, and the stdout logs of any automation wrapping ansible-playbook, even though every task touching the secrets is marked no_log: true. This is a regression introduced with the ansible-core 2.19 data-tagging/templating rework; the behaviour does not occur on 2.16, where the error text is correctly censored.

descriptions.value: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 6.0.0 until 6.0.24, 7.0.23, 8.0.7, 9.0.6, 9.1.6, 9.2.7, 9.3.5, 10.0.8, 10.1.9, 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, Multitenancy.checkPermissionsForCreateOrUpdate in src/main/java/io/supertokens/multitenancy/Multitenancy.java does not adequately authorize updates to a parent connection URI domain or the base tenant. In a licensed multi-tenant deployment with multiple applications under one non-default connection URI domain and separate api_keys, an attacker holding one application's valid API key can update the parent domain because the CUD-target branch checks the domain without requiring the source application and tenant to be public. Because api_keys is not protected, the attacker can replace the parent key and then sibling application keys, read or modify sibling users, obtain sessions as those users, establish persistence through a sibling dashboard user, and lock out the sibling application's own key. In the advisory's v2 create or update handlers, omitting the optional identifier produces a base-tenant target that skips the permission branches and enterprise-feature gate, allowing changes to firstFactors, required secondary factors, and recipe-enabled flags that affect login integrity and availability. The base-target variant still rejects coreConfig and does not establish key theft. This issue is fixed in versions 6.0.24, 7.0.23, 8.0.7, 9.0.6, 9.1.6, 9.2.7, 9.3.5, 10.0.8, 10.1.9, 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.

cna.title: Symfony: Programmatic Logins Skip the checkPostAuth() Method of User Checkers

descriptions.value:
The Symfony Security HTTP component AuthenticatorManager::authenticateUser() does not run the firewall user checker’s checkPostAuth() method when a user is authenticated programmatically, allowing an account rejected by a custom user checker, such as an expired account, to be authenticated in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11.



AuthenticatorManager::authenticateUser() is used by UserAuthenticatorInterface::authenticateUser() and by the SecurityBundle’s Security::login() to authenticate a user programmatically, but it does not dispatch the security.authentication.success event, on which checkPostAuth() runs. The fix for CVE-2024-50341 made Security::login() call checkPreAuth(), but checkPostAuth() was still skipped. As a result, an account rejected by a custom user checker in checkPostAuth() is refused by form login and the other authenticators of the firewall, but can still be authenticated programmatically.



Applications are affected when they use a custom user checker that rejects users in checkPostAuth() and authenticate users programmatically, for example after a password reset or an e-mail verification link. A user whose account is rejected can then obtain an authenticated session through that flow. The default user checker does nothing in checkPostAuth(), so the default configuration is not affected.



The fix makes AuthenticatorManager::authenticateUser() dispatch the security.authentication.success event once the token is created and before it is stored, as authentications through the firewall do, so that checkPostAuth() runs and can reject the user.

cna.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a per-host mTLS authorization bypass via a CA-only SNI context failing open to the default CA

descriptions.value: A per-host mutual-TLS authorization bypass in Node.js lets a client authorized for the default hostname reach a protected hostname it is not authorized for. When a TLS server assigns a hostname a different client-certificate CA with `server.addContext(host, { ca: protectedCA })` but no server certificate in that SNI context, the per-host client CA is never installed and the handshake falls back to the default client CA. In `src/crypto/crypto_tls.cc`, `CertCbDone` installs the SNI context's CA only when `setSniContext` succeeds, but `setSniContext` returns `false` for a context with no server certificate, so a CA-only SNI context silently keeps the default CA. A client holding a certificate trusted by the default CA, but not the protected CA, can therefore complete mTLS to the protected hostname and read its response even with `requestCert` and `rejectUnauthorized` enabled, while a client certified by the protected CA is rejected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

cna.title: Signal K Server: Unauthenticated path traversal in resources-provider v2 API leads to JWT secret disclosure, admin impersonation and remote code execution

descriptions.value: Signal K Server is a server application that runs on a central hub in a boat. From 2.0.0 until 2.34.0 for Signal K Server and from 1.0.0 until 1.5.3 for @signalk/resources-provider, the v2 REST route GET /signalk/v2/api/resources/:resourceType/:resourceId accepts an unsafe resourceId that can escape the intended resource directory. The route passes the attacker-controlled resourceId through src/api/resources/index.ts to FileStore.getResource() in packages/resources-provider-plugin/src/filestorage.ts without adequate path containment, allowing arbitrary JSON files reachable by the server to be read. Related PUT and DELETE resource operations can write or delete files outside the storage root. Deployments with allow_readonly enabled permit anonymous reads, while other deployments require a readonly user token. Reading security.json exposes the HS256 JWT signing secret and password hashes, allowing an attacker to forge an administrator token. Administrative access to POST /skServer/providers can then create an Execute provider that runs commands with the server process privileges and persists its configuration across restarts. This issue is fixed in Signal K Server 2.34.0 and @signalk/resources-provider 1.5.3.

cna.title: SuperTokens Core: SAML callback accepts a replayed RelayState + SAMLResponse, minting a fresh authorization code on each replay

descriptions.value: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 11.3.0 until 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, SAML.handleCallback does not consume RelayState, record assertion identifiers, or enforce Response.InResponseTo. In the SP-initiated flow, an attacker who obtains a legitimately issued, still-valid SAML response and its matching RelayState can resubmit the pair to /recipe/saml/callback before the assertion's NotOnOrAfter time; in the IdP-initiated flow, the assertion can be replayed without RelayState. The missing Response.InResponseTo check also permits an in-progress login to be completed with an assertion for a different identity and fails to enforce allowIDPInitiatedLogin=false. The callback does not validate Destination or SubjectConfirmationData Recipient and NotOnOrAfter, and each accepted callback mints a fresh, independently redeemable authorization code carrying the captured user's identity. This issue is fixed in versions 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.

descriptions.value: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. cna.title: Symfony: XXE (Local File Read) in Config XmlUtils::parse() via validateOnParse = true

descriptions.value:
The Symfony Config component XmlUtils::parse() enables DTD validation before rejecting documents that carry a doctype, allowing XML external entity (XXE) injection in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. A remote attacker who can supply XML to this method can determine whether local files exist, cause a denial of service, and, in some configurations, exfiltrate local file content via a crafted XML document whose doctype declares an external file:// entity.
XmlUtils::parse() sets $dom->validateOnParse = true before calling loadXML() and only rejects documents carrying a doctype afterwards. Enabling DTD validation makes libxml resolve external entities during loadXML(), and LIBXML_NONET blocks http:// but not file://, so a file:// entity is read from disk before the doctype rejection runs. The content of the file is not returned to the caller, but the distinct libxml error for a missing path reveals whether a file exists, and an entity pointing at a large or slow file causes a denial of service. If the application registers a network-capable stream wrapper such as s3://, a parameter entity can also send the content of a local file to an external server. This is the same issue as CVE-2026-45071, which was fixed in the DomCrawler component but not in Config.

Applications are affected if they pass untrusted XML to XmlUtils::parse() directly. The Symfony components that call it process developer-provided or operator-configured sources, such as configuration files and the XLIFF documents fetched by the translation providers.

SuperTokens Core: Unknown tenant path bypasses API key and public-tenant enforcement

descriptions.value: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. Prior to 11.3.6, 11.4.6, and 12.0.8, app-specific management requests using an unknown tenant path and an older supported cdi-version can bypass API-key and public-tenant enforcement. In src/main/java/io/supertokens/webserver/WebserverAPI.java, checkIPAccess and assertThatAPIKeyCheckPasses suppress TenantOrAppNotFoundException, while the later app-specific handler resolves app/public storage and the public-tenant guard applies only to CDI versions 5.0 and later. An unauthenticated caller able to reach the Core endpoint can therefore use PUT /ghosttenant/recipe/role and GET /ghosttenant/recipe/roles to create and enumerate application roles without a valid API key. This issue is fixed in versions 11.3.6, 11.4.6, and 12.0.8.

cna.title: SQL Injection via unescaped DataFrame column names in Snowflake Connector for Python and Snowflake Connector for Python (Universal Core)

references.name: Snowflake Connector for Python Release Notes
Snowflake Connector for Python (Universal Core) Release Notes

descriptions.value: When identifier escaping is disabled through a non-default configuration, the write_pandas() data-loading functionality in the Snowflake Connector for Python and the Snowflake Connector for Python (Universal Core) did not escape DataFrame column names before including them in generated SQL, which could allow SQL injection. In both products, a crafted column name could have been used to chain additional SQL statements onto the generated statement, potentially allowing an attacker to read, modify, or delete other data accessible to the application's Snowflake role. cna.title: Symfony: NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient Does Not Pin the Checked IP of Cached Hosts, Letting DNS Rebinding Enumerate Internal Ports (Incomplete Fix for CVE-2024-50342)

descriptions.value:
The Symfony HttpClient component NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient does not pin the checked IP address of cached hosts, allowing for DNS rebinding to bypass private network restrictions, resulting in enumeration of internal hosts and ports in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11.

NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient resolves the host of each request and checks the IP before connecting. It caches the result per host, and passes the IP to the decorated client through the resolve option so that the client connects to the exact IP that was checked. The issue is that resolve was only passed on the first lookup of a host: on subsequent requests, the decorated client resolved the host again on its own.

An attacker who controls a host's DNS can exploit this with DNS rebinding by answering the first lookup with a public IP, and subsequent lookups with a private IP, so when an application sends several requests to that host through the same client, the later requests connect to the private IP. This happens, for example, when an application fetches several URLs of a repository provided by a user. The check of the primary_ip in the on_progress callback still aborts the request before anything is sent, but the connection is made, and the error differs depending on whether the port is open or closed. This allows enumerating internal hosts and ports, as in CVE-2024-50342.

descriptions.value: In Gogs 0.14.3, the Git Smart HTTP authorization layer in internal/route/repo/http.go allows a push when only read access was intended, a different vulnerability than CVE-2026-52810. This occurs because of a case-sensitivity desync between the authorization classifier and the request dispatcher: the gitHTTPIsPull function compares the Git action verb case-sensitively and defaults to pull (read access) for any unrecognized string, whereas the request dispatcher lowercases the same verb before routing it to the receive-pack handler. Capitalizing a single letter in the URL (e.g. info/Refs instead of info/refs, or git-receive-Pack instead of git-receive-pack) causes the classifier to misidentify a push as a pull, granting only read-level authorization, whereas the dispatcher routes it to the write handler. An authenticated read-only collaborator can exploit this to push to a private repository, creating, updating, or deleting refs.

cna.title: Apache Axis2/Java: SSRF via WS-Addressing ReplyTo and FaultTo endpoints

An unauthenticated caller could supply a non-anonymous WS-Addressing wsa:ReplyTo or wsa:FaultTo address, and Axis2 would open a connection to that address to deliver the response or fault, allowing requests to internal hosts and delivery of response content to a host of the caller's choosing. From 2.0.2, decoupled responses are refused unless allowNonAnonymousResponseEndpoints is enabled, and enabled endpoints are restricted by scheme and screened at both the header-parsing and transport-selection layers. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue.

descriptions.value: Hickory DNS hickory-proto 0.25.0 through 0.26.0-alpha.1 and hickory-net 0.26.0-beta.1 before 0.26.2 invert the relational operators in the wrap-around branch of find_covering_record() in nsec3.rs, so the last NSEC3 record in a zone's hash ring covers every hash except its owner. cna.title: SuperTokens Core SAML: identity taken from an assertion that never passed the audience check, allowing sign-in as any IdP user

descriptions.value: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 11.3.0 until 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, a licensed deployment with a configured SAML client can authenticate an identity from an assertion that did not satisfy the audience check. When the identity provider uses assertion-level signing, an attacker who has a still-valid IdP-signed assertion naming the victim for any audience and the attacker's own valid assertion for the target audience can combine them because validateSamlResponseAudience accepts an audience from one assertion while extractAllClaims takes the final NameID and attributes from another; response-level signing does not expose this multi-assertion variant. Independently, an assertion from an identity provider configured for the target deployment but issued to another SuperTokens deployment using the shared default saml_sp_entity_id can satisfy the target's audience check. Successful exploitation authenticates the attacker as the victim IdP user. This issue is fixed in versions 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.

cna.title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 memory exhaustion denial of service via unaccounted inbound DATA on an undrained stream

descriptions.value: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can exhaust Node.js server memory because inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream is charged to no session budget. Each inbound DATA frame creates one JavaScript Buffer view in the receiving stream's readable queue, but nothing charges that queue to current_session_memory_: the socket read buffer is accounted only during parsing and released immediately, so whatever stays queued is accounted to nothing. A peer that fills a stream's receive window with one-byte DATA frames pays about 10 wire bytes per frame while the server retains about 114 bytes per frame, so a single stream on one connection can retain hundreds of megabytes from tens of megabytes sent. maxSessionMemory neither bounds the growth nor refuses new streams, because Http2Session::CanAddStream gates admission on the same counter that never sees the queue. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

workarounds.value: Until a fixed package is available, remove or disable dnf5daemon-server if GNOME Software / dnf5daemon-client is not required, or restrict system D-Bus access to org.rpm.dnf.v0 to trusted users. cna.title: SuperTokens Core: WebAuthn sign-in accepts a passkey across tenant boundaries

descriptions.description: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control

descriptions.value: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 10.1.0 until 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, loadOptionsById_Transaction and getUserInfoByCredentialId_Transaction perform application-scoped WebAuthn lookups without constraining them to the requested tenant, and WebAuthN.signIn does not verify tenant membership. In a multi-tenant deployment using WebAuthn with a shared user pool, an ordinary user who possesses their own valid passkey in one tenant can submit its assertion to another tenant's sign-in endpoint in the same application and be authenticated there despite having no membership in the target tenant. This issue is fixed in versions 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.

cna.title: Node.js is vulnerable to cross-connection memory disclosure via TLS write re-entrancy in the HTTPS request parser

credits.value: Chris Rohlf in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research

descriptions.value: A re-entrancy flaw in Node.js HTTPS lets an unauthenticated client read memory belonging to other connections, including TLS private keys and other users' requests. TLSWrap::DoWrite() calls ClearOut() directly when asked to write zero bytes; if that write is issued from JavaScript running inside the HTTP parser's on_body callback, ClearOut() decrypts the next TLS record while the parser is still mid-body, re-entering llhttp_execute() and causing a use-after-free and an out-of-bounds heap read. The server then copies that freed or unrelated heap memory into the response for the request body. Triggering it requires a handler that calls res.flushHeaders() before the request body ends and later calls res.end() with a non-empty chunk, and reading the leaked memory requires any ordinary route that echoes or stores a request body. Cleartext node:http is not affected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

cna.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow in HTTP/2 session.altsvc() via a long origin

descriptions.value: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's :authority header to Http2Session.altsvc(), the AltSvc implementation in src/node_http2.cc allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid :authority triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

cna.title: SureDash <= 1.13.0 - Authenticated (Custom+) Privilege Escalation to /suredash/v1/save-settings REST Endpoint

descriptions.value: The SureDash – Community, Courses & Member Dashboard plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.13.0 This is due to the `save_settings()` REST handler at `/suredash/v1/save-settings` being gated only by `admin_permission_callback()`, which authorizes any holder of the custom `manage_portal_dashboard` capability (Portal Manager role) without requiring `promote_users`, `edit_users`, or `manage_options`, combined with `sanitize_settings_data()` iterating all attacker-supplied keys with no allow-list, allowing arbitrary keys such as `default_role` to pass through `sanitize_text_field()` unchanged and be persisted into the `portal_settings` option via `update_option()` with no role-validity check. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Portal Manager-level access and above to poison the `default_role` setting to `administrator`, after which any subsequent new-user registration through the publicly accessible block-register endpoint reads the corrupted setting and passes it directly to `wp_insert_user()`, producing a full WordPress Administrator account under the attacker's control. The exploit requires two steps: a POST to the authenticated `save-settings` endpoint to overwrite `default_role`, followed by triggering a new registration through the unauthenticated block-register endpoint to receive the escalated account. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

cna.title: Spring Data Elasticsearch SpEL Expression Injection through String-based Query Method Arguments

descriptions.value:
Spring Data Elasticsearch replaces positional placeholders in string-based @Query methods with the method arguments before it evaluates SpEL expressions in the resulting query string.



As a result, an argument that contains a SpEL expression is evaluated as part of the query, even if the declared query does not use SpEL.



 An application is affected if it passes untrusted input as an argument to a repository query method that declares a @Query with positional placeholders.



In that case, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary code in the application, and repeated requests can exhaust memory through the unbounded expression cache.

In `init/3`, the handler calls `:cowboy_stream.init/3` and adds a `{:flow, size}` command when the request has a body, where `size` is Cowboy's `max_frame_size_received` (16384 by default). It passes all other callbacks to `:cowboy_stream`.

descriptions.value:
Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows a client to stall all later calls on a shared HTTP/2 connection via calls that the server refuses while their DATA frames are in flight.

The stream handler grpc_stream_h (grpc_server/src/grpc_stream_h.erl) requests flow from Cowboy only for request data that has arrived. When the server refuses a call early, for example because the body exceeds max_body_size or the method is not implemented, Cowboy drops the DATA frames still in flight for that stream. Their bytes are not returned to the connection flow-control window. After enough refused calls the window is empty. No call on that connection can then send a request body, and each call waits until its deadline. Other connections are not affected.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Flow is requested only for data that arrived

Cowboy increases the HTTP/2 connection window only when a stream handler returns a {flow, N} command. grpc_stream_h returns that command only for request data it has received.

2. A refused call leaves data uncredited

When the server refuses a call, the stream stops. The client can still have DATA frames in flight for it. Cowboy drops those frames without running the handler, so no flow is requested for their bytes and no connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE is sent.

3. The window empties

Each refused call with DATA in flight reduces the connection window for good. With the default 65,535-byte window, the window was empty after two refused calls in a test against v1.0.6. An empty window stops all request data, so no handler requests flow again and the window stays empty.

4. Result

Every later call on the connection that has a request body waits until its deadline. A new connection works normally.

cna.title: Node.js is vulnerable to proxy credential disclosure via ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages

descriptions.value: Node.js discloses proxy credentials in ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages. CVE-2026-48615 established that a proxy credential must not appear in a Node.js error message and redacted the username and password from ProxyConfig.href, but that fix missed four error paths in the same subsystem, one of them inside the same constructor, which interpolate the raw proxy URL, credentials included, into an ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG message. The proxy URL comes from the environment, but the defect is the sink: a secret that Node.js redacts everywhere else is emitted verbatim into a much wider audience than the process environment, such as stderr, container logs, log aggregation, and crash reporting services. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

cna.title: NGINX ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module vulnerability

credits.value: F5 acknowledges Vivek Parikh of BreachX Zero Day Labs using Typhon AI Mil v2 for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

supportingMedia.value:
Disable the ssl_preread directive in favor of SSL/TLS termination on NGINX. For more information, refer to https://nginx.org/en/docs/stream/ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module.html

For example, the following configuration includes the ssl_preread on; directive:

stream {
    log_format sni "PREREAD_SNI=[$ssl_preread_server_name] -> [$backend]";
    access_log /var/log/nginx/stream.log sni;
    map $ssl_preread_server_name $backend {
        internal.test   127.0.0.1:9002;   # privileged backend
        default          127.0.0.1:9001;   # public backend
    }
    server {
        listen 9443;
        ssl_preread on;
        proxy_pass $backend;
    }
}

To mitigate the issue for this configuration, make the following changes:

  • Remove the ssl_preread directive.
  • Terminate TLS on NGINX by adding the following:
    • Change the listener to ssl.
    • Configure a certificate and key.
    • Replacing $ssl_preread_server_name with $ssl_server_name to use SNI-based routing.

stream {
    log_format sni "TLS_SNI=[$ssl_server_name] -> [$backend]";
    access_log /var/log/nginx/stream.log sni;
    map $ssl_server_name $backend {
        internal.test   127.0.0.1:9002;   # privileged backend
        default          127.0.0.1:9001;   # public backend
    }
    server {
        listen 9443 ssl;
        ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/ssl/fullchain.pem;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/ssl/privkey.pem;
        ssl_protocols       TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
        # ssl_preread removed; NGINX terminates client TLS.
        proxy_pass $backend;
        # Use these if the backends still expect TLS.
        proxy_ssl on;
        proxy_ssl_server_name on;
        proxy_ssl_name $ssl_server_name;
    }
}

After making the configuration changes, validate the configuration and reload, using the following commands:

nginx -t
nginx -s reload

descriptions.value:
Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support.

Impact
This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

descriptions.value: Dynatrace MCP Server is an MCP server for Dynatrace Observability. Prior to 2.1.1, several read capabilities interpolate caller-controlled values into DQL without sufficient validation or escaping. The src/capabilities/find-monitored-entity-by-name.ts capability embeds entityNames in string searches, src/capabilities/list-problems.ts, src/capabilities/list-vulnerabilities.ts, and src/capabilities/list-exceptions.ts embed timeframe values, and src/capabilities/get-events-for-cluster.ts embeds timeframe, clusterId, and kubernetesEntityId. The issue does not grant data access beyond the configured token's existing execute_dql capability, but it breaks the narrower auto-approved tool contract. This issue is fixed in version 2.1.1.
