descriptions.value:
Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in hexpm hex_core allows an attacker who can intercept HTTPS connections to impersonate hex.pm, repo.hex.pm or any other repository or API server to programs that use hex_core's default HTTP adapter on Erlang/OTP 24, or on OTP 25 when the operating system's CA certificates can't be loaded.

hex_core:default_config/0 selects the built-in hex_http_httpc adapter. For an HTTPS request whose adapter config has no ssl option, hex_http_httpc:http_options/2 builds options that verify the server certificate against public_key:cacerts_get/0. When that call raises, the adapter prints a warning and sends the request without ssl options, so httpc uses the defaults of the ssl application, which before OTP 26 don't verify the server certificate. public_key:cacerts_get/0 doesn't exist on OTP 24, so every HTTPS request falls back there, and on OTP 25 it raises when no CA store is found. hex_core versions before 0.11.0 never set ssl options, so they don't verify the server certificate on OTP 25 and earlier whether or not a CA store is found.

The fallback was intended and documented, but the documentation didn't make clear that it meant no certificate verification. Since hex_core 0.8.2 the README has warned that the built-in httpc adapter "has insecure default settings" and recommended other HTTP clients, and the adapter prints "using default ssl options which are insecure" on every request that falls back. hex_core 0.11.0 added certificate verification with the changelog entry "Use secure SSL defaults for OTP 25+". Neither the README nor the warning says that the server certificate isn't verified, the README doesn't say which OTP versions the warning applies to, and on OTP 25 without CA certificates the warning tells users to upgrade to OTP 25 or later, which they already run. This advisory is published so that users who took those notices as general advice know their HTTPS requests weren't authenticated.

This issue affects hex_core: from 0.1.0 before 0.20.0.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
* hex_core:default_config/0 sets http_adapter to {hex_http_httpc, #{profile => default}}.
* hex_http_httpc:request/5 and hex_http_httpc:request_to_file/6 build their httpc options with http_options/2.
* For an https URI whose adapter config has no ssl entry in http_options, http_options/2 adds {ssl, [{verify, verify_peer}, {cacerts, public_key:cacerts_get()}, ...]} inside a try.
* When public_key:cacerts_get/0 raises (undef on OTP 24; an error on OTP 25 when no CA store is found), the catch prints a warning with io:format/1 and returns the options without ssl.
* httpc then uses the ssl application's defaults, which are verify_none before OTP 26, and completes the handshake with any certificate.
* hex_core before 0.11.0 (e57b4fb) had no step 3: it never passed ssl options, so step 5 applied on every OTP version before 26.

cna.title: PingTools Network Utilities 4.64 - OS command injection through Watcher ICMP host

descriptions.value: Successful exploitation lets an attacker execute commands as the PingTools application UID, read or alter application-accessible data, use the application's outbound network access, and disrupt the application. The commands remain confined by the Android application sandbox.

solutions.value: Remove sh -c from the Watcher ICMP execution path. Pass a validated Host as one unchanged element of an argument list to a non-shell process API backed by ProcessBuilder.command(...); never join, quote, or reparse the argument list. Validate Host before storage and immediately before execution in the editor and backup import/restore paths. Add unit, argument-capture, and end-to-end tests that prove rejected values never reach a shell or any process.

supportingMedia.value: Remove sh -c from the Watcher ICMP execution path. Pass a validated Host as one unchanged element of an argument list to a non-shell process API backed by ProcessBuilder.command(...); never join, quote, or reparse the argument list. Validate Host before storage and immediately before execution in the editor and backup import/restore paths. Add unit, argument-capture, and end-to-end tests that prove rejected values never reach a shell or any process.

workarounds.value: Until a vendor-confirmed fixed version is available, disable Watcher ICMP where possible. Otherwise use only reviewed task configuration, do not import untrusted Watcher backups, and remove existing Host values containing whitespace, control characters, option-like prefixes, or shell syntax. These measures reduce exposure but do not remediate the sh -c execution path.

descriptions.value: PingTools Network Utilities 4.64 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the Host field of a Watcher ICMP service. The application appends the attacker-controlled Host value to a ping command, serializes the command as a single string, and executes it through sh -c. A local attacker who can create or modify a Watcher service can inject shell syntax and execute arbitrary commands with the PingTools application UID and its granted Android permissions.

descriptions.value: Bitpoll through 0.11.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read votes and comments from other polls via unscoped object lookups in views.py. references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 NULL Pointer Dereference via TGV Decoder eatgv.c

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in tgv_decode_inter() in libavcodec/eatgv.c that ignores init_get_bits() failure on oversized packets. cna.title: Konflux-ci: unvalidated hostname fields enable caddyfile config injection in the konflux ui proxy generator, allowing an unauthenticated route to be spliced ahead of the forward_auth/impersonate authorization chain

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Konflux UI proxy. Hostname values defined in the KonfluxUI custom resource are inserted directly into proxy configuration files without adequate validation or sanitization. An authenticated user with permissions to modify the custom resource can inject malicious configuration directives to bypass authentication and authorization controls, potentially exposing internal backend services. In addition, providing malformed input can cause the configuration generator to fail, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) by preventing the proxy from starting.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Firekylin through 2.18.1 Improper Authorization via Admin REST API GET Actions

Editors can query options.js for TOTP secrets, push credentials, and cloud storage keys, or user.js for other users' app_key/app_secret to publish posts as administrators via admin/post_push.

cna.title: HarnessRouter: Service-only routes that write an organization's provider connections could be reached through a multi-tenant console with a made-up bearer

descriptions.value: HarnessRouter is a self-hosted unified API for running agent harnesses with sessions, streaming, files, cancellation, and failure handling. Prior to 0.31.8, a console that is not in self-hosted mode attaches the server's internal key to requests carrying an Authorization header before validating the bearer, while the service-only PUT and GET /v1/orgs/{org}/connections/{name}, PUT /v1/orgs/{org}/policy/{backend}, and /internal/* routes trust that key and take the organization from the URL. In a multi-organization deployment, a remote caller can use a made-up bearer to rewrite another organization's provider connection to an attacker-controlled endpoint, causing later prompts to be disclosed and attacker-controlled responses to influence tasks. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.8.

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Out-of-Bounds Memory Access in Huffyuv/FFVHUFF Median Predictor

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Out-of-Bounds Memory Access in Huffyuv/FFVHUFF Median Predictor

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability in the encode_frame() function of libavcodec/huffyuvenc.c, because encode_init() never validates minimum frame dimensions for the median predictor. Attackers can supply a tiny video, such as a 2-pixel-wide or 1-2-pixel-tall frame, that causes negative sub_median_pred lengths and out-of-bounds reads and writes when transcoded to huffyuv or ffvhuff, crashing the encoder.

cna.title: Rack: Rack::Request#host_with_port (and #base_url / #url) return the raw invalid Host header — incomplete fix of CVE-2026-34835

descriptions.value: Rack is a modular Ruby web server interface. From 3.0 until 3.1.23 and 3.2.8, Rack::Request#host_with_port, #base_url, and #url can return an attacker-controlled invalid authority from Host, X-Forwarded-Host, or Forwarded: host= verbatim. Applications without an independent host allowlist that use these methods for absolute URLs, redirects, or origin-dependent checks can emit attacker-chosen delimiters, enabling redirect manipulation, string-based allowlist bypass, or unescaped markup reflection. Rails overrides these methods and is not expected to be affected. This issue is fixed in versions 3.1.23 and 3.2.8.

cna.title: Forge: ReDoS in forge.http response header and cookie trimming

descriptions.value: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. From 0.1.2 until 1.4.3, forge.http uses _trimString() in lib/http.js to remove trailing whitespace from response header values and cookie names and values with a regular expression that can take quadratic time. A malicious server or on-path attacker can supply a long whitespace run followed by a non-whitespace character in a response header, causing response.readHeader() or response.getCookies() to repeatedly scan the input and block the Node.js event loop or browser tab for minutes. Applications are affected only when they use forge.http with a socket pool to communicate with an untrusted server; forge.http is not loaded by require('node-forge'), and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

cna.title: TYPO3 CMS - Information Disclosure in Form Framework

descriptions.value:
Files uploaded through FileUpload or ImageUpload elements are stored in an unguessable sub-folder that remains the same for the whole form session. If storing an uploaded file failed, for example because of a file name exceeding the file system's length limit, the raw error message was shown to the frontend user disclosing the storage path including the unguessable folder name and the server's temporary upload directory. With this information, attackers could determine the public URL of files they upload through the form.

If a form allows uploading files that browsers can execute, such as HTML documents, this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder. This vulnerability is known to be actively exploited.

cna.title: Winter CMS: Reflected XSS through the search query parameter in the backend Table widget

descriptions.value: Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.0.420 until 1.2.14, the backend Table widget partial modules/backend/widgets/table/partials/_table.php emits the search query parameter without HTML encoding inside a script template. A script-closing sequence in a crafted top-level GET URL terminates the raw-text template and causes the remaining input to be parsed as backend markup, even when the widget uses searching: false. Any Table or DataTable page is a sink, including the core Editor Settings route /backend/system/settings/update/winter/backend/editor, and an unauthenticated attacker can induce an authorized backend user to follow the link. Script executing in the victim's backend origin can read the CSRF token and issue credentialed requests with that user's permissions. For the core sink, a victim with backend.manage_editor, normally a Developer-role user or superuser, can edit CMS templates, so the injected script can conditionally chain to server-side code execution; this does not grant permissions the victim lacks and does not apply automatically to every third-party plugin sink. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

cna.title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can still issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's output

descriptions.value: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint escapes GitHub Actions workflow-command openers only after ASCII spaces and tabs, while the runner strips all leading Unicode whitespace before interpreting a line. Untrusted Compose values or repository paths beginning with Unicode whitespace followed by :: can therefore reach the text report, fix guidance, the fix dry-run diff, and stderr diagnostics as workflow commands when the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image runs directly in CI. The GitHub Action is not affected because it disables command processing, and the flaw does not change the lint pass or fail result. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

cna.title: Forge: TLS client crash on an unsupported ServerHello compression method

descriptions.value: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, a forge.tls client accepts a ServerHello compression_method that it did not offer. When the client later handles ServerHelloDone, tls.createConnectionState() rejects the unsupported compression algorithm by throwing an Error that propagates from connection.process(). A malicious server or an on-path attacker can alter the unauthenticated ServerHello compression byte before the server Finished message and terminate a Node.js process when the application does not catch the exception. The affected client paths include direct forge.tls use, forge.tls.wrapSocket, and forge.http; forge.tls servers are not affected, and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

descriptions.value: Kubero 3.0.0 through 3.1.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to forge administrative JWTs by using a hardcoded fallback signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset. Attackers can sign tokens with arbitrary role, userGroups and permissions claims, which JwtStrategy.validate() trusts without a database lookup, to take control of pipelines, applications, users and API tokens.

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Use-After-Free in MJPEG Hardware-Accelerated Decoding

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Use-After-Free in MJPEG Hardware-Accelerated Decoding

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a use after free vulnerability in libavcodec/mjpegdec.c that allows attackers to trigger freed buffer reads by sending a SOF marker without a preceding SOI. Attackers can supply crafted MJPEG streams causing ff_mjpeg_decode_sof() to pass a stale raw_image_buffer pointer to hwaccel decoders like NVDEC, crashing applications or leaking heap contents.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

cna.title: compose-lint: A file path in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's command-line error messages

descriptions.value: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint's argument parser writes rejected repository paths to stderr without the output sanitizer when a path is passed without a preceding -- separator. A pull request can supply a path containing workflow-command syntax; a carriage return can position that command at the start of a new line recognized by the GitHub Actions runner, allowing the package, Docker image, or a pre-commit hook with misconfigured args to issue the command in the job log. The default pre-commit configuration includes -- and is not affected, the GitHub Action is not affected, and the lint pass or fail result is unchanged. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

cna.title: Rack: Multipart boundary ambiguity guard in Rack::Multipart::Parser can be bypassed with a quoted boundary value, allowing WAF bypass

descriptions.value: Rack is a modular Ruby web server interface. Prior to 2.2.25, 3.1.23, and 3.2.8, Rack::Multipart::Parser.parse_boundary can skip a leading empty or quoted boundary parameter in a multipart Content-Type header and accept a later parameter. Rack can therefore parse a request body with a boundary that a conforming intermediary would not derive, allowing form fields or file uploads to reach an application without the intended proxy or web application firewall inspection. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.25, 3.1.23, and 3.2.8.

cna.title: Mongoose: Prototype pollution via Schema.prototype.virtual()

descriptions.value: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Schema.prototype.virtual() builds nested virtual paths without applying the special-property validation already used by Schema.path() and Schema.add(). An attacker who can influence virtual field names in dynamic schemas, content-management form builders, or schema-as-code systems can supply path segments such as __proto__, constructor, or prototype, causing the virtual-path reducer to write enumerable properties to Object.prototype or Function.prototype. The resulting prototype pollution can spoof inherited property checks such as authorization flags and can provide function-prototype gadget state to other server-side JavaScript code. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

supportingMedia.value:
Use After Free vulnerability in Erlang/OTP erts allows an attacker who can create a file system entry with a chosen name to hang or abort the Erlang VM on macOS.

On macOS, the VM decodes file names with do_utf8_to_list_normalize in erts/emulator/beam/erl_unicode.c. When a name starts with a combining mark, such as U+0301, cleanup_norm builds the first list cells but does not return its advanced heap pointer. The caller then releases the heap words that hold those cells, and the returned list refers to released process heap memory that the next allocation overwrites. file:list_dir/1, file:list_dir_all/1, file:del_dir_r/1 and filelib:wildcard/1 on a directory that contains such a name do not return, and the VM does not stop on SIGTERM. file:read_link/1 on a symbolic link with such a target aborts the VM with size_object: bad tag. Only loss of availability was demonstrated.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2.

1. On macOS, create a directory with one file whose name starts with U+0301: mkdir d && printf x > "d/$(printf '\314\201b')".
  2. Run erl -noshell -eval 'io:format("~w~n", [file:list_dir("d")]), halt().'. The command prints nothing and does not return. The VM does not stop on SIGTERM. The expected output is {ok,[[769,98]]}.
  3. Run erl -noshell -eval 'erlang:display(prim_file:internal_native2name(<<204,129,$b>>)), halt().'. The output starts with [<cp/header:0x00000000000000c0>. The expected output is [769,98].
  4. Create a symbolic link with the same name as its target (ln -s "$(printf '\314\201b')" link) and call file:read_link("link"). The VM aborts with size_object: bad tag for 0x80.

supportingMedia.value:
1. Decoder entry

prim_file:list_dir/1 and prim_file:read_link/1 decode each native name with prim_file:internal_native2name/1. Its implementation, prim_file_internal_native2name_1 in erts/emulator/beam/erl_unicode.c, calls do_utf8_to_list_normalize when the file name encoding is ERL_FILENAME_UTF8_MAC. erts_init_sys_common_misc selects that encoding only on macOS.

2. Missing heap pointer write-back

do_utf8_to_list_normalize reserves 2 * num heap words with HAlloc, reads the name from its end, and keeps code points that can compose (U+0300 and above) in savepoints. If saved points remain when it reaches the start of the name, it calls cleanup_norm(&hp, savepoints, numpoints, &ret) and then HRelease(p, hp_end, hp). cleanup_norm copies *hpp to a local hp, builds one cons cell per saved point, and writes back only *retp. The caller's hp still points below the new cells, so HRelease returns them to the process heap. handle_potential_norm has the same structure and does write *hpp = hp.

3. Effect

The returned list starts in released heap memory. The next allocation of the process overwrites the cells. erlang:display/1 shows a header word in place of the first code point. When the term is copied, for example in the reply of the file server, size_object_x either loops without end on a cyclic term or aborts the VM with size_object: bad tag.

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/qsvenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt memory by reusing an undersized pooled QSVFrame buffer when input dimensions increase. Attackers can supply crafted input whose resolution grows mid-stream, transcoded with Intel Quick Sync encoders without rescaling, to crash the application or corrupt heap memory.

cna.title: pgEdge RAG Server shared keyword index leaked results between concurrent unauthenticated requests

descriptions.value: pgEdge RAG Server is an API server for retrieval-augmented generation over PostgreSQL content using pgvector. Prior to 2.0.0, the BM25 keyword index is a single per-pipeline object shared by the unauthenticated query endpoint, and concurrent requests lock its clear, refill, and search operations separately. This allows one request to search a corpus populated through another request's search filter, which can return documents belonging to a different tenant or customer without malformed input. The affected responses cannot be identified retrospectively from the server logs. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.0.

workarounds.value: For applications that automatically select GStreamer plugins, set GST_PLUGIN_FEATURE_RANK=mpegpsdemux:NONE in the affected process to prevent automatic selection of the MPEG Program Stream demuxer. Applications that explicitly instantiate mpegpsdemux or rsndvdbin must avoid processing untrusted MPEG Program Stream or DVD input until a fixed package is available. These measures disable affected playback paths and are not a complete fix.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-bad MPEG Program Stream demuxer and resindvd DVD-playback plugin. The PES header parsers do not adequately check remaining data before reading timestamps and optional header fields. Opening a specially crafted MPEG Program Stream file can cause an out-of-bounds read and potentially crash the application, resulting in a denial of service.

cna.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server login rate limiting can be evaded by a caller-supplied header

descriptions.value: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, deployments exposing the nondefault HTTP transport with authentication enabled used the leftmost caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For value as the client address for login rate limiting. ExtractIPAddress in internal/auth/middleware.go supplied that value to IsAllowed and RecordFailedAttempt in internal/auth/rate_limiter.go, allowing an unauthenticated caller to rotate addresses to evade throttling or assert another user's address to consume that user's limiter bucket. The published nginx configuration appended rather than replaced X-Forwarded-For, making the issue reachable without an operator misconfiguration. Username-keyed account lockout did not use the client address, but shipped defaults disabled that separate control through MaxFailedAttemptsBeforeLockout: 0. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

descriptions.value: A repository created with auto-init accepted pushes before its initialization had finished, and the initial commit was built in a checkout of whatever the repository already contained. descriptions.value: pgEdge RAG Server is an API server for retrieval-augmented generation over PostgreSQL content using pgvector. cna.title: Forge: Ed25519 signature verification accepts small-order public keys

descriptions.value: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, ed25519.verify() decodes a public key in crypto_sign_open() without rejecting small-order points or their non-canonical encodings. With S = 0 and a small-order R value, an attacker who can choose the public key can produce signatures that verify for many messages, or all messages with the identity key, without a private key. This can defeat proof-of-possession, attribution, non-repudiation, or deduplication checks that rely on a signature being bound to the message. Keys produced by normal Ed25519 key generation are not small-order, so applications that verify only trusted or internally generated public keys are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

cna.title: Winter CMS: ImportExportController AJAX handlers bypass granular import/export permission gate

descriptions.value: Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. Prior to 1.2.14, the ImportExportController behavior applies userHasAccess() only to the import() and export() page actions, while Backend\Classes\Controller::execAjaxHandlers() dispatches onImport(), onImportLoadForm(), onImportLoadColumnSampleForm(), onExport(), and onExportLoadForm() before those gated actions run, and the separately reachable download() action also lacks the granular export check. An authenticated backend user with a valid session and coarse access through $requiredPermissions, but without the configured import[permissions] or export[permissions], can use the import handlers to write or overwrite records and can use onExport() followed by download() to retrieve the complete dataset exposed by the export model. Controllers without granular permission keys are unaffected because userHasAccess() is intentionally default-permissive. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

cna.title: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 -dSAFER Bypass via .putgstringcopy .forceput Recovery

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 -dSAFER Bypass via .putgstringcopy .forceput Recovery

descriptions.value: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 contains a -dSAFER bypass vulnerability in the .putgstringcopy procedure in gs_fonts.ps, which calls the privileged .forceput operator without checking operand types. Attackers can supply crafted PostScript or PDF documents that trigger a type error, recover .forceput via a custom error handler, and cause a use-after-free across save/restore to execute arbitrary code.

cna.title: Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via sslw_remove_sts

credits.value: Adiel Sol, Arad Inbar, Erez Cohen, Nir Somech, Ben Grinberg, Daniel Lubel, Shir Sadon (DREAM Security Research Team)

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Out-of-Bounds Read via sslw_remove_sts

descriptions.value: Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains an out-of-bounds read and size_t underflow vulnerability in sslw_remove_sts() in src/ec_sslwrap.c, caused by a stale length and an unchecked memmem() result when stripping Strict-Transport-Security headers. A malicious HTTPS server whose response passes through Ettercap's SSL interception can trigger out-of-bounds reads and memory corruption in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

cna.title: pgEdge Go LLM Library discloses provider API key fragments in error messages

descriptions.value: pgEdge Go LLM Library provides a unified Go interface for multiple LLM providers with streaming, tool calling, retries, and an HTTP and server-sent events proxy. From 0.1.0 until 0.2.0, GET /v1/health in llm/proxy/handlers.go uses handleHealth to ping providers with the operator's real credentials and returns their error text, while the Authorize hook in llm/proxy/proxy.go permits access by default when the consuming application does not configure it. When a provider rejects the configured credential, a remote caller who can reach the proxy can obtain part of the operator's third-party provider API key from the resulting error. This issue is fixed in version 0.2.0.

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization bypass through User-Controlled key

descriptions.value:
The checkout of JTL-Shop stores the delivery address
ID submitted by the customer in the session and adopts it into the order

attacker with access to the checkout, including a guest, can thereby attach

account. As the IDs are sequential, addresses can be enumerated. Goods may
also be shipped to the wrong address.

cna.title: Stored cross-site scripting in the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting')

descriptions.value:
The administration page "Offene
Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the
customer name of pending orders without output encoding. A registered
customer (free self-registration) can submit an HTML-entity-encoded name, which is
decoded to markup when the billing address of an order is written. If
the PayPal payment is left unfinished, the order is listed on the page and the
name is rendered as markup in the browser of an administrator who opens
the page. The script code runs with the privileges of that administrator
and can, for example, create a new administrator account. Guest orders are
not affected, because the name is encoded again.

cna.title: Forge: X.509 nameConstraints not enforced by verifyCertificateChain()

descriptions.value: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, pki.verifyCertificateChain() in lib/x509.js does not decode or enforce the X.509 nameConstraints extension while validating certificate paths. A name-constrained certificate authority with a non-critical extension can therefore issue a leaf certificate with a subjectAltName dNSName or subject commonName outside a permitted subtree or inside an excluded subtree, and node-forge accepts the chain. Exploitation requires a name-constrained CA that chains to a trusted root and either its private key or the ability to obtain an out-of-scope certificate, allowing impersonation of names outside the delegated namespace, including against forge.tls clients. Chains without nameConstraints are not affected, and affected versions safely reject critical nameConstraints as unsupported rather than accepting them. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

cna.title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's JSON and SARIF output on stdout

descriptions.value: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint does not sanitize the ##[ workflow-command opener inside strings written by --format json or --format sarif to stdout. A pull request can place that opener in a service name or other Compose value, and the GitHub Actions runner recognizes it even in the middle of a serialized line when the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image prints JSON or SARIF to the job log. Writing the output to a file and using the compose-lint GitHub Action are not affected, and the flaw does not change the lint pass or fail result. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

cna.title: Nexter Blocks Pro <= 5.0.10 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Unicode Collation Confusion in 'tpgb_acf_key' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Nexter Blocks Pro plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.10 via the `tpgb_ajax_register_user()` function. This is due to a byte-level denylist on the `tpgb_acf_key[]` and `tpgb_acf[]` parameters that fails to block Unicode look-alike characters — such as U+1E87 and U+00E7 in a key like `ẇp_çapabilities` — whose UTF-8 byte sequences do not match any ASCII-based pattern check, while the database's default accent-insensitive collation (`utf8mb4_unicode_ci` / `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`) treats the decorated key as equivalent to the canonical `wp_capabilities` row, causing `update_user_meta()` to overwrite the newly registered user's role with `administrator`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register a new account bearing the full Administrator role, gaining complete control over the WordPress site including the ability to install plugins, modify files, and execute arbitrary code. The nonce required by the handler is publicly emitted on any page containing the tp-login-register block, making the full exploit chain — nonce retrieval, a single crafted registration POST, and the plugin's own `autologin` flow — trivially reachable on any default install where user registration is enabled. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

cna.title: Plack::Middleware::CSP versions before 0.03 for Perl send the Content Security Policy under the wrong header name, so browsers never enforce it

solutions.value: Upgrade to Plack-Middleware-CSP 0.03 or later.

descriptions.value:
Plack::Middleware::CSP versions before 0.03 for Perl send the Content Security Policy under the wrong header name, so browsers never enforce it.

The call method sets the policy in a response header named "content-security-protocol" instead of "Content-Security-Policy". Browsers ignore that header.

Any cross-site scripting flaw in the wrapped application can run scripts the policy was meant to block.

cna.title: pgEdge Control Plane generates pg_hba.conf with trust authentication for local and loopback connections

descriptions.value: pgEdge Control Plane is a distributed application for managing and orchestrating Postgres databases across multiple hosts. From 0.1.0 to 0.10.1, generated pg_hba.conf files began with hard-coded trust entries for Unix-socket and loopback connections. Because PostgreSQL evaluates the file from top to bottom, those entries also preempted operator-supplied rules in the pg_hba_conf field. Under the systemd orchestrator, any unprivileged operating-system account on a database host could authenticate as any PostgreSQL role, including the superuser, without credentials and obtain full control of the host's databases. Under Docker Swarm, reaching the container-local socket or loopback interface required code execution inside the database container. Publishing the PostgreSQL port to the host did not expose these trust rules because host connections did not appear to originate from 127.0.0.1 or ::1. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

cna.title: Rack: Rack::Static header_rules bypass via dot-segment normalization mismatch

descriptions.value: Rack is a modular Ruby web server interface. Prior to 2.2.25, 3.1.23, and 3.2.8, Rack::Static serves a path after Utils.clean_path_info normalization but evaluates header_rules against a path that is only URL-decoded. An unauthenticated attacker can request a known file through raw or percent-encoded dot segments and receive it without path-specific security headers such as Content-Disposition or Content-Security-Policy. Applications that do not use path-specific header_rules are not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.25, 3.1.23, and 3.2.8.

cna.title: Passster <= 4.3.21 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'metavalue' Parameter

affected.product: Passster – Password Protect Pages and Content

descriptions.value: The Passster – Password Protect Pages and Content plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (metakeyinput=passster_id | passster_headline)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.21 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor can break out of the shortcode attribute context by embedding a ] character in the passster_id or passster_headline meta value to prematurely close the opening shortcode tag, then append a [/passster] closing tag so that the trailing HTML payload is emitted verbatim by do_shortcode() — bypassing the per-attribute escaping present inside render_shortcode() — and the script will also execute in an editor's or administrator's browser when they preview the Contributor's pending post, since filter_the_content() has no edit-permission capability gate.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Although wp_kses_post sanitizes post content on save, the payload is kses-legal at save time; the plugin's output-buffer rewrite transforms it into an executable form at render time by overwriting the valueless data-src attribute with the unescaped src value, meaning save-time sanitization provides no effective mitigation.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

cna.title: Gstreamer: gstreamer: use-after-free in gstreamer core buffer value deserialization

workarounds.value: There is no complete mitigation for applications that continue to deserialize untrusted GStreamer caps or structure strings. Restrict access to network-facing GStreamer Data Protocol receivers to trusted peers, and avoid passing externally supplied strings to gst_caps_from_string() or gst_structure_from_string() until an update is available. These measures reduce exposure only where the application can control those input paths.

descriptions.value: A use-after-free flaw was found in GStreamer core buffer value deserialization. When serialized buffer text contains an invalid character, an error path frees a mapped buffer before unmapping it. Applications that parse untrusted caps or structure data can reach a freed-buffer read and may crash. A network-facing GStreamer Data Protocol receiver can process such caps data without user interaction; further impact has not been established.

cna.title: Mongoose: Connection-level sanitizeFilter not applied

descriptions.value: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. From 6.0.0 until 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Mongoose stores the connection-level sanitizeFilter option in Connection.config, but Query.prototype._castConditions() and query casting check other option locations and do not read that configuration. An application that enables sanitizeFilter through mongoose.connect() or createConnection() and passes an attacker-controlled object into a query filter therefore receives a connection that reports the defense as enabled while query selector objects remain unsanitized. A crafted password value using a query operator can match an account record without the expected literal password, while global configuration through mongoose.set('sanitizeFilter') and per-query Model.find().sanitizeFilter() remain unaffected. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

descriptions.description: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

cna.title: Winter CMS: CSRF through AJAX handler names reachable as backend page actions

descriptions.value: Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.0.319 until 1.2.14, Backend\Classes\Controller::actionExists() accepts public handler-shaped methods as page actions, so a top-level GET request can invoke state-changing backend AJAX handlers without a CSRF token. Because backend routes use Route::any, CSRF validation skips GET, and the default SameSite=Lax session cookie is sent on cross-site navigation, an unauthenticated attacker can induce an authorized backend user to follow a link such as /backend/system/eventlogs/index_onEmptyLog. Affected handlers in the backend, CMS, and system modules can truncate logs, reset settings, alter backend user state, or delete CMS templates, while URL path segments can select a target record. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

cna.title: Mongoose walks into inherited properties when hydrating, setting, and merging, allowing overwrites of built-in functions (denial of service) and shared schema state

descriptions.value: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Mongoose can descend into inherited properties while loading database documents in init(), setting dotted paths in $__set, and merging update documents in utils.mergeClone. Attacker-controlled keys such as toString or valueOf can therefore cause Mongoose to write into shared built-in functions instead of an own property. A crafted document, Mixed path, non-strict document or subdocument, findOneAndReplace() replacement, chained update, or Query.prototype.merge() source can overwrite Object.prototype.toString.call, causing later queries on unrelated models to fail until the process restarts. Separately, when an attacker controls the dotted path passed to doc.set(path, value) for a subdocument configured with strict: false, descent through $__set can reach $__schema and alter shared validators or schema options for later documents. Mongoose already blocks __proto__, constructor, and prototype, so this issue overwrites properties on reachable shared objects rather than adding new properties directly to Object.prototype. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

descriptions.description: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

cna.title: HarnessRouter: A workspace's API key could read and change sessions, files and responses of other workspaces in the same organization

descriptions.value: HarnessRouter is a self-hosted unified API for agent harnesses. From version 0.4.2 until 0.31.7, routes that accept a session ID or response ID validate only the caller's organization and do not enforce the workspace scope of a non-default workspace API key. A key holder who learns a non-guessable identifier from another workspace in the same organization can read sessions, conversation turns, files, traces, and responses, overwrite files, cancel or delete sessions, and publish share links. The issue does not cross organization boundaries, and console users, organization keys, and Default Workspace keys intentionally retain organization-wide access. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.7.

descriptions.description: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

cna.title: Rack: Multipart parsing allows DoS via unbounded scan buffer growth

descriptions.value: Rack is a modular Ruby web server interface. Prior to 2.2.25, 3.1.23, and 3.2.8, Rack::Multipart::Parser can retain parsed data in its internal StringScanner buffer when reads end inside or immediately after multipart headers. An unauthenticated attacker can align many small parts with rack.multipart.buffer_size boundaries so the buffer grows with the request despite per-field, header, and preamble limits, causing a worker to exhaust memory. The attack requires only a well-formed multipart body and affects applications that parse multipart requests. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.25, 3.1.23, and 3.2.8.

cna.title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can reach Azure Pipelines as logging commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's output

descriptions.value: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint does not neutralize the Azure Pipelines ##vso[ logging-command opener on any output path. A pull request can place that opener in a Compose value or file name, allowing output from the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image to issue logging commands when printed to an Azure Pipelines job log. The maintainer did not reproduce the behavior on an Azure Pipelines agent. The GitHub Action is not affected because it runs only on GitHub Actions, and releases before 0.31.0 are outside this advisory because they did not claim Azure Pipelines coverage. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

cna.title: Mongoose: Discriminator key values matching inherited properties (e.g. __t: 'constructor') bypass schema casting and can poison collections

descriptions.value: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4, Mongoose uses attacker-controlled discriminator key values, including the default __t field, to index plain-object registries such as Model.discriminators and schema.discriminators without requiring an own property. Values such as constructor, toString, or hasOwnProperty can therefore resolve to inherited built-in functions instead of a registered discriminator, causing type confusion in model construction, document creation, hydration, query and update casting, embedded discriminators, and populate operations. In the bulkWrite() insertOne path with skipValidation enabled, a constructor value can cause a raw input object to be stored without schema casting or strict filtering, and a stored poisoned document can make every query that hydrates it fail until the document is removed. The weakness reads inherited properties but does not modify Object.prototype and is not prototype pollution. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.12, 7.8.13, 8.24.7, and 9.11.4.

descriptions.description: CWE-843: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

cna.title: XRootD: Path traversal in directory listing allows access to the parent directory via trailing ".." pattern

descriptions.value: The XRootD project provides a high-performance, fault-tolerant, and secure solution for handling large amounts of data distributed across multiple storage resources. Prior to version 5.9.2, XRootD's rpCheck() function in src/XrdXrootd/XrdXrootdXeq.cc rejects a parent-directory component only when two dots are followed by a slash and does not reject a terminal two-dot component. An unauthenticated attacker can append /.. to an exported path in xrdfs ls or an HTTP PROPFIND request, bypass the all.export directory scope, and cause directory and filename enumeration in the parent directory under oss.localroot. The demonstrated vector does not permit file download or disclose file contents. This issue is fixed in version 5.9.2.

cna.title: TYPO3 CMS - Unrestricted File Upload in Form Framework

descriptions.value: The FileUpload and ImageUpload elements of the Form Framework use the property allowedMimeTypes as an allow list of MIME types accepted for upload. An empty allowedMimeTypes list was treated as "no restriction". Forms containing upload elements without any configured MIME type, for example in manually created form definitions or when all MIME types were deselected in the form editor, accepted any file except those blocked by the file deny pattern, which only covers PHP-related file extensions. This allowed unauthenticated users to upload files with browser-executable content, such as HTML or SVG documents, to the configured upload folder, which by default is located in a public storage. If attackers know the URL of an uploaded file (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-029), this could lead to Cross-Site Scripting on web servers that do not apply the Content-Security-Policy recommended by TYPO3 to the form upload target folder.

workarounds.value:
Set DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE to a bundle that holds no public root and no root that signs device certificates, for example a file with one self-signed certificate made for this purpose. A certificate from an unregistered CA is then refused once and the handshake ends. Devices whose certificate or CA is registered in NervesHub continue to connect.

Restarting a node ends the handshakes that are already stuck on it.

descriptions.value:
Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in device certificate verification in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a TLS client certificate whose CA is not registered. When a client certificate chains to a root in the device endpoint's trust store but no CA in the chain is registered in NervesHub, NervesHub.SSL.decide/2 refuses it with the reason :unknown_ca. Erlang/OTP ssl reads that reason as a missing trust anchor, looks for an alternative root, finds the same root and validates again without end. The handshake process queries the database on each pass and keeps running after the client disconnects, until the node restarts.

The device endpoint trusts the public roots from CAStore unless DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE is set, so a client certificate from a public CA whose chain allows client authentication is sufficient. A chain that ends at a root outside the trust store is refused once.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.4.

configurations.value:
The certificate chain must end at a root in the device endpoint's trust store. With DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE unset, which is the default from 2.0.0, the trust store holds the public roots from CAStore. With DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE set to a bundle that holds a root which signs device certificates, any certificate from that root whose CA is not registered is sufficient, including the certificate of a deleted device.

The retry in Erlang/OTP ssl was confirmed on Erlang/OTP 28.3, 29.0 and 29.1. Earlier releases were not checked.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* Make a self-signed root and a client certificate signed by it, directly or through an intermediate that the client sends. Do not register either CA in NervesHub.
* Run a device endpoint whose trust store holds that root, by adding it to the DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE bundle. Against the default trust store, a client certificate from a public CA replaces steps 1 and 2.
* Open one TLS connection to the device endpoint with that certificate, then disconnect.
* The handshake process on the server keeps running. The nerves_hub.ssl.fail telemetry event with reason unknown_ca and the database queries repeat until the node restarts.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Refusal reason. The device endpoint gives ssl the verify function NervesHub.DeviceLink.PeerVerification.verify_fun/3, which asks NervesHub.SSL.decide/2. For a :valid_peer event on a certificate that is not on file, decide/2 tries to register the certificate. check_known_ca/1 in lib/nerves_hub/ssl.ex looks for the signer among the registered CAs and returns :unknown_ca when it finds none. do_verify/2 passes that to ssl as {:fail, :unknown_ca}.

2. Retry in ssl. unknown_ca is also the reason Erlang/OTP uses for a path with no trust anchor. In ssl_handshake:path_validate/11, a {bad_cert, unknown_ca} result makes ssl look for a cross-signed alternative root and validate again. Unlike the root_cert_expired branch, this branch does not add the root it tried to the list of roots to skip.

3. Loop. When the chain ends at a self-signed root in the trust store, ssl finds the same root, calls the verify function again, and receives unknown_ca again. The recursion is a tail call, so the process does not grow or crash. It does not return to its mailbox, so it sees neither the handshake timeout nor the closed socket. Each pass runs the database queries of the registration checks.

cna.title: BIG-IP and BIG-IQ iControl SOAP vulnerability

credits.value: F5 acknowledges Dan Stefan Alexandru of Pentest-Tools for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

workarounds.value:
As this attack is conducted by legitimate, authenticated users, there is no viable mitigation that also allows users access to iControl SOAP. The only mitigation is to remove access for users who are not completely trusted.

Until it is possible to install a fixed version, you can use the following sections as temporary mitigations. These mitigations restrict access to iControl SOAP to only trusted networks or devices, thereby limiting the attack surface.

  *  Block iControl SOAP access through self IP addresses

  *  Block iControl SOAP access through the management interface



Block iControl SOAP access through self IP addresses

You can block all access to iControl SOAP of your BIG-IP system using self IP addresses. To do so, you can change the  Port Lockdown setting to  Allow None  for each self IP address on the system. If you must open any ports, you should use the  Allow Custom  option, taking care to block access to iControl SOAP. By default, iControl SOAP listens on TCP port 443. If you modified the default port, ensure that you block access to the alternate port you configured.

Note: Performing this action prevents all access to iControl SOAP using the self IP address. These changes may also impact other services, including breaking high availability (HA) configurations. For more information, refer to  K46122561: Restrict access to the BIG-IP management interface using network firewall rules https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K46122561 . 

Before you make changes to the configuration of your self IP addresses, F5 strongly recommends that you refer to the following articles:

As this attack is conducted by legitimate, authenticated users, there is no viable mitigation that also allows users access to iControl SOAP. The only mitigation is to remove access for users who are not completely trusted.

Until it is possible to install a fixed version, you can use the following sections as temporary mitigations. These mitigations restrict access to iControl SOAP to only trusted networks or devices, thereby limiting the attack surface.

  • Block iControl SOAP access through self IP addresses
  • Block iControl SOAP access through the management interface

Block iControl SOAP access through self IP addresses

You can block all access to iControl SOAP of your BIG-IP system using self IP addresses. To do so, you can change the  Port Lockdown setting to  Allow None  for each self IP address on the system. If you must open any ports, you should use the  Allow Custom  option, taking care to block access to iControl SOAP. By default, iControl SOAP listens on TCP port 443. If you modified the default port, ensure that you block access to the alternate port you configured.

Note: Performing this action prevents all access to iControl SOAP using the self IP address. These changes may also impact other services, including breaking high availability (HA) configurations. For more information, refer to K46122561: Restrict access to the BIG-IP management interface using network firewall rules.

Before you make changes to the configuration of your self IP addresses, F5 strongly recommends that you refer to the following articles:

cna.title: TYPO3 CMS - Open Redirection in URL Sanitization

descriptions.value: The fix for TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-009 was incomplete. GeneralUtility::sanitizeLocalUrl performed its checks on the URL-decoded value, but returned the original, URL-encoded value. URLs containing certain percent-encoded characters therefore passed the sanitization checks as local URLs, although they point to an external host. Applications that use the sanitized URL for redirects are vulnerable to open redirect attacks. This enables attackers to redirect users to external content and carry out phishing attacks. In the TYPO3 core, this affects redirects in the backend, which require the victim to be logged in to the backend.

cna.title: TYPO3 CMS - Information Disclosure in Image Processing

descriptions.value:
ImageMagick and GraphicsMagick use small modules, called "coders", to read each image format. When processing images, TYPO3 determined the coder from the file type detected by the file contents, as long as the detected mime-type started with image/. A file containing MVG (Magick Vector Graphics) instructions, uploaded with an image file extension like .png, was therefore processed with the MVG coder. MVG instructions can read local files into the processed image, which allows disclosing the contents of arbitrary files readable by the web server, for example configuration files containing credentials, through a publicly accessible processed image.

Exploiting this vulnerability requires a way to upload files without a mime-type check, for example a public form of the Form Framework using a FileUpload or ImageUpload element without configured allowedMimeTypes (see TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-032), which allows exploitation by unauthenticated visitors. Additionally, ImageMagick must be used for image processing, and its default system configuration must allow the MVG coder.

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in hap_parse_frame_header() in libavcodec/hapdec.c that allows attackers to trigger a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit builds. Attackers can craft Hap video frames with Snappy length prefixes that wrap tex_size, causing decompress_chunks_thread() to write outside tex_buf and crash the application or potentially execute code.

cna.title: FFmpeg 7.1 through 9.0.2 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via Vulkan Slice Buffer Sizing

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg 7.1 through 9.0.2 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via Vulkan Slice Buffer Sizing

descriptions.value: FFmpeg 7.1 through 9.0.2 contains an integer overflow in ff_vk_decode_add_slice() in libavcodec/vulkan_decode.c that miscalculates the Vulkan hwaccel bitstream buffer size. Attackers can supply a crafted stream with over 2 GiB of slice data per frame, causing memcpy() to write past a smaller pooled host-mapped buffer.

Out of bounds write in GPU in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.50 allowed a remote attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 GIF Encoder Heap Buffer Overflow via shrunk_buf Remap

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow in the GIF encoder's gif_image_write_image() in libavcodec/gif.c because shrunk_buf is sized from the first frame's linesize. Attackers can supply PAL8 video whose frame linesize grows mid-stream, causing remap_frame_to_palette() to write past shrunk_buf and corrupt the heap during GIF transcoding.

cna.title: FFmpeg 8.1 through 9.0.2 Denial of Service via DPX Vulkan Hwaccel Error Path

descriptions.value: FFmpeg 8.1 through 9.0.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in libavcodec/dpx.c that leaves dpx->hwaccel_picture_private allocated when Vulkan hwaccel callbacks fail. Attackers can supply crafted DPX images that make start_frame, decode_slice or end_frame fail, triggering an av_assert0 abort on the next frame and terminating the decoding application.

cna.title: SiteOrigin CSS <= 1.6.9 - Unauthenticated Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via 'class' Attribute of Stored Content via Visual Inspector

descriptions.value: The SiteOrigin CSS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'class' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a Contributor-level or higher attacker to store a crafted class attribute value in a post, which then fires when a user with the edit_theme_options capability opens the Visual Inspector on the affected post and clicks anywhere in the preview iframe. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that a third-party plugin providing wp_kses_post()-filtered unauthenticated front-end submission is installed and configured, and a moderator approves the submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

cna.title: Meteroid before 2.2.0 Cross-Tenant API Token Hash Disclosure via GetApiTokenById

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Meteroid before 2.2.0 Cross-Tenant API Token Hash Disclosure via GetApiTokenById

descriptions.value: Meteroid before 2.2.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the ApiTokensService GetApiTokenById gRPC handler that fails to apply the caller's tenant context. Authenticated users with settings:read permission can supply another tenant's API token ID to obtain its Argon2 secret hash and owning tenant ID.

cna.title: Automation-controller: automation-controller: quadratic regex in schedule rrule validation allows an authenticated user to exhaust api web workers (denial of service)

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Jiawei Guo for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: The schedule preview endpoint is available to any authenticated user and cannot be restricted by RBAC, so exposure can only be reduced by limiting API access to trusted users.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the rrule validation of schedules in automation controller. Several non-anchored regular expressions with lazy wildcard prefixes are applied to the user-supplied rrule value; when the expected DTSTART/RRULE tokens are absent, validation time grows quadratically with the length of the value. An authenticated user can submit a large token-free rrule through the REST API, including the schedule preview endpoint, which requires no resource-level permissions; validation runs synchronously in the API web worker, so a single such request occupies a worker for an extended time and repeated requests can exhaust the web worker pool, denying access to the API and web UI while the attack is sustained. The impact is limited to availability.

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via HEVC DXVA Tile Parameters

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via HEVC DXVA Tile Parameters

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in ff_dxva2_hevc_fill_picture_parameters() that allows attackers to corrupt memory via unbounded non-uniform tile counts. Attackers can supply crafted HEVC bitstreams with many non-uniformly spaced tiles to write controlled 16-bit values past fixed-size DXVA arrays during DXVA2, D3D11VA, or D3D12VA decoding on Windows.

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via LCEVC Enhancement Decoding

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Heap Buffer Overflow via LCEVC Enhancement Decoding

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/lcevcdec.c because LCEVC output picture dimensions are not validated against the allocated frame. Attackers can embed crafted LCEVC enhancement data with differing global configurations in H.264 or HEVC streams to corrupt heap memory in decoding applications.

cna.title: FFmpeg 8.0 through 9.0.2 Memory Leak in VP9 Decoder via vp9_decode_frame

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg 8.0 through 9.0.2 Memory Leak in VP9 Decoder via vp9_decode_frame

descriptions.value: FFmpeg 8.0 through 9.0.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in the VP9 decoder that allows attackers to exhaust memory because vp9_decode_frame() skips resetting the CBS fragment on error paths. Attackers can supply a crafted VP9 stream with invalid tile sizes decoded with slice threading to leak packet buffers and units, exhausting memory in the decoding application.

descriptions.description: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Division by Zero via VVC ff_vvc_slice_rpl()

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Division by Zero via VVC ff_vvc_slice_rpl()

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a division by zero vulnerability in the VVC decoder because ff_vvc_slice_rpl() fails to validate num_ref_idx_active against built reference list entries. Attackers can supply a crafted VVC bitstream whose excess reference indices yield a zero POC difference in ff_vvc_mv_scale(), crashing the decoding process.

cna.title: Mongoose: sanitizeFilter not applied on countDocuments

descriptions.value: Mongoose is a MongoDB object modeling tool designed to work in an asynchronous environment. Prior to 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3, and 9.9.2, Mongoose countDocuments() does not apply the configured sanitizeFilter query selector injection defense. An application that enables sanitizeFilter and passes attacker-controlled filter values to countDocuments() can therefore process query operator objects as operators rather than literal values, causing the count to include documents that should not match and potentially undermining authorization or application logic based on that count. This issue is fixed in versions 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3, and 9.9.2.

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Uninitialized Heap Disclosure via MLZ Decompressor in ALS Decoder

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Uninitialized Heap Disclosure via MLZ Decompressor in ALS Decoder

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in ff_mlz_decompression() in libavcodec/mlz.c, which accepts string codes beyond the dictionary's next free code. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG-4 ALS file with malformed initial or out-of-range codes to copy uninitialized heap bytes into decoded audio output.

cna.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server did not validate the Origin header, allowing DNS rebinding

descriptions.value: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, the HTTP transport did not validate the Origin header on incoming requests. A user who visited an attacker-controlled page could be targeted through DNS rebinding, allowing the page to reach a locally running server and read schemas and query results from configured databases. The issue affected deployments with the HTTP transport enabled on a machine that also ran a browser, while the default stdio transport was not reachable through this path. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 ProRes prores_aw Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in Interlaced Encoding

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libavcodec/proresenc_anatoliy.c that occurs when the prores_aw encoder processes interlaced, odd-height frames. Attackers can supply odd-height video that causes subimage_with_fill_template() to fill padding rows from memory before the fill_y buffer, leaking heap contents into the encoded output.

cna.title: FFmpeg 4.4 through 9.0.2 NULL Pointer Dereference via adx_decode_header()

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg 4.4 through 9.0.2 NULL Pointer Dereference via adx_decode_header()

descriptions.value: FFmpeg 4.4 through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in libavcodec/adxdec.c because adx_decode_header() updates the channel layout before validating the sample rate. Attackers can supply a crafted ADX/AAX stream with mid-stream new-extradata side data carrying an invalid sample rate, causing adx_decode() to write through NULL plane pointers and crash the application.

cna.title: FFmpeg 7.0 before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 Heap Overflow via vulkan_av1.c

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: FFmpeg 7.0 before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 Heap Overflow via vulkan_av1.c

descriptions.value: FFmpeg 7.0 before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in vk_av1_decode_slice() in libavcodec/vulkan_av1.c because the tile-count limit is checked only on entry. Attackers can supply a crafted AV1 stream with more than 256 tiles decoded via the Vulkan hardware accelerator to overflow tile_sizes and corrupt heap memory.

cna.title: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 Uninitialized Memory Disclosure via Tiertex SEQ Decoder

cna.title: WEB-Translation <= 2.0.7 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via `#!etmst#`/`#!etmen#` Delimiter Substitution

descriptions.value: The WEB-Translation – eTranslation Multilingual plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires that at least one secondary language is configured in the plugin and that comments are open on the target post; because the stored payload contains no literal HTML brackets at save-time, WordPress core KSES filtering does not remove it, and the malicious script is only materialized when a visitor loads the post under a secondary-language URL slug.

cna.title: NGINX try_files vulnerability

credits.value: F5 acknowledges Marc Luchian & Liviu-Alexandru Bud for bringing this issue to our attention and following the highest standards of coordinated disclosure.

modules: The map directive with regex matching
The map directive with regex matching

workarounds.value: Avoid unnamed regex captures; use named captures instead. Do not reuse the same capture variable in other regex matches or for other purposes.

supportingMedia.value: Avoid unnamed regex captures; use named captures instead. Do not reuse the same capture variable in other regex matches or for other purposes.

descriptions.value:
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the try_files and alias directives with a map variable, certain combinations of regular expression captures in map and try_files can cause a segmentation fault in an NGINX worker process.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to cause an NGINX worker process to terminate unexpectedly. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

cna.title: TYPO3 CMS - Cache Flooding in Page Cache Handling

descriptions.value: The cHash argument, which ensures that only URL arguments originally generated by TYPO3 create separate page cache entries, was treated inconsistently when it was passed as an array. The cHash validation treated such a value as missing, while the page cache identifier treated it as present and included all URL arguments. As a result, unauthenticated visitors could create an unlimited number of page cache entries and trigger uncached page renderings by adding an array cHash with arbitrary values to any URL. This could exhaust server resources and fill the page cache storage. Only installations where the cHash validation is not enforced via $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['FE']['cacheHash']['enforceValidation'] are affected. This setting is enabled by default for new installations since TYPO3 v12, but is often still disabled in installations upgraded from older versions.

cna.title: Gst-plugins-base: gst-plugins-base: quadratic regex processing in srt/webvtt subtitle parser causes denial of service

workarounds.value: Update gst-plugins-base to version 1.28.2 or later. Where updating is not yet possible, applications that do not require untrusted SRT/WebVTT subtitles can prevent automatic selection of the subparse element (for example, by setting GST_PLUGIN_FEATURE_RANK=subparse:NONE).

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the SRT and WebVTT subtitle parser in GStreamer's gst-plugins-base. While sanitizing inline subtitle markup, the parser repeatedly searches the remaining text with unanchored regular expressions. A crafted subtitle cue with a long line of unmatched markup-like text can force quadratic CPU use and make a GStreamer-based application unresponsive.

cna.title: Winter CMS: Stored XSS through cached Brand Settings and Editor Settings custom styles

descriptions.value: Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. Prior to 1.2.14, BrandSetting::renderCss() and EditorSetting::renderCss() store raw LESS compiler output with Cache::forever() but apply strip_tags() only to the value returned on a cache miss. The first render after saving custom CSS appears sanitized while priming an unsafe cache entry, and later cache hits return unsanitized output into the backend style element, allowing a user with backend.manage_branding or backend.manage_editor to cause stored cross-site scripting when another backend page renders the styles. The styles also appear on unauthenticated backend sign-in, password restore, and password reset layouts. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14.

cna.title: Cypher injection via orderBy placeholder in Spring Data Neo4j custom queries

descriptions.description: CWE-943 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

descriptions.value: CAPEC-676 NoSQL Injection

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the orderBy placeholder handling for custom queries in Neo4j Spring Data Neo4j versions 6.1.0 through 8.0.8 and 8.1.0 through 8.1.2 allows a remote attacker to read database contents via blind reads, write read content into new nodes, or, if APOC and APOC file export are enabled, to write query results to a file in the database's accessible file system via crafted sort order parameters. Exploitation requires an application that passes unvalidated user input as the orderBy value to a custom Cypher query using the placeholder directive.

supportingMedia.value: Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the orderBy placeholder handling for custom queries in Neo4j Spring Data Neo4j versions 6.1.0 through 8.0.8 and 8.1.0 through 8.1.2 allows a remote attacker to read database contents via blind reads, write read content into new nodes, or, if APOC and APOC file export are enabled, to write query results to a file in the database's accessible file system via crafted sort order parameters. Exploitation requires an application that passes unvalidated user input as the orderBy value to a custom Cypher query using the placeholder directive.

configurations.value: Exploitation requires an application that (1) uses a custom Cypher query containing the orderBy SpEL (Spring Expression Language) directive and (2) passes an unvalidated, attacker-controlled value to the orderBy input of that query. Writing query results to a file additionally requires the APOC plugin with APOC file export enabled on the database.

supportingMedia.value: Exploitation requires an application that (1) uses a custom Cypher query containing the orderBy SpEL (Spring Expression Language) directive and (2) passes an unvalidated, attacker-controlled value to the orderBy input of that query. Writing query results to a file additionally requires the APOC plugin with APOC file export enabled on the database.

workarounds.value: Validate any user-supplied orderBy value against an allow list of known property names and sort directions before passing it to Spring Data Neo4j. Do not expose the orderBy input to untrusted users without validation.

supportingMedia.value: Validate any user-supplied orderBy value against an allow list of known property names and sort directions before passing it to Spring Data Neo4j. Do not expose the orderBy input to untrusted users without validation.

solutions.value: Upgrade Spring Data Neo4j to 8.0.9, 8.1.3, 8.2.0 or later (depending on your release line). The fix restricts functions callable in the orderBy directive to an allow list of built-in (non-APOC) functions; the list must be extended intentionally if other functions are needed.

descriptions.value:
This vulnerability exists in the eMudhra emBridge due to missing authorization checks in the FileBrowser API endpoints. These endpoints perform file system enumeration using the LocalSystem account without adequately validating the requesting caller's authorization. An unauthenticated attacker on the same LAN could exploit this vulnerability by sending malicious webpage to the local HTTPS Web API.

 

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate file and directory names and obtain information about the directory structure of the targeted system. 



The vulnerability however, does not provide access to file contents or permit file modification, deletion, or code execution, or access to cryptographic keys and hardware token PINs.

cna.title: compose-lint: A symlink in a pull request can issue workflow commands through the compose-lint Action's SARIF-directory error message

descriptions.value: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From version 0.30.0 until 0.32.0, the compose-lint GitHub Action prints the resolved directory from a failed sarif-file subdirectory creation without effective command suppression. Version 0.30.0 has no stop-commands window, while version 0.31.0 prints this error outside its stop-commands window. A pull request can place a committed symlink on that path to a directory whose name contains a newline followed by a workflow command, causing the SARIF-directory error to issue commands in the job log. Only the Action with sarif-file pointing into a subdirectory is affected; a workspace-root SARIF file, the compose-lint package, the pre-commit hook, and the Docker image do not expose this message. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

cna.title: Apache Arrow Rust: Bloom filters written as plaintext when writing encrypted Parquet

descriptions.description: CWE-313 Cleartext storage in a file or on disk

descriptions.value:
Cleartext storage in encrypted parquet file vulnerability in Apache Arrow Rust (`parquet` crate), from version 55.0.0 through to 57.3.2, 58.4.1, 59.3.2 and 60.1.0.



When writing an encrypted parquet file with a column with bloom filters, the header and bitsets of the bloom filter are written in plaintext in the final parquet.



Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 57.3.3, 58.4.2, 59.3.3 or 60.2.0 which fix the issue by raising an error when trying to write encrypted parquet files with bloom filters enabled, preventing such files from being written out.



Existing encrypted parquet files written with bloom filters are still vulnerable, and it is recommended to rewrite those files with bloom filters disabled if possible.
