cna.title: Out-of-Bounds Access After SSL_set_SSL_CTX() During a Handshake

descriptions.value:
Issue summary: A TLS server that calls SSL_set_SSL_CTX() to switch a
connection to a different SSL_CTX part way through a handshake may access
memory beyond the end of an internal array if the replacement context knows
about more provider signature algorithms than the context the connection was
created from. Applications which never call SSL_set_SSL_CTX() are not
affected.

Impact summary: A remote peer may be able to cause a small out-of-bounds
read, and in some circumstances a fixed-value out-of-bounds write, on the
server heap. This may lead to a Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-787: Out-of-bounds Write

Description: A TLS connection records how many certificate slots it has
when it is created, taken from the SSL_CTX that created it: the built-in
certificate types plus one slot for each provider TLS-SIGALG entry that
context was aware of. That count sizes an internal array of per-slot
certificate validity flags.

An application may replace a connection's SSL_CTX part way through the
handshake by calling SSL_set_SSL_CTX(), most commonly from a servername
callback in order to serve a different virtual host. Doing so did not
refresh the recorded count. A provider signature algorithm's slot index is
its position in the list of whichever context resolves it, so if the
replacement context is aware of more of them than the original, an
algorithm offered by the peer can resolve to an index beyond the end of the
array. Processing the peer's signature algorithms then reads one four byte
word past the end for each such algorithm and, where the word read is zero,
writes a fixed value over it. A peer offering many of them can corrupt heap
metadata and abort the process.

Only provider signature algorithms which occupy one of the excess slots,
and which the server also has configured, have this effect. Codepoints the
replacement context does not recognise are discarded without being resolved
to a slot, and provider signature algorithms are usable only from TLS 1.3.

The two contexts must therefore be aware of different numbers of provider
signature algorithms, which requires separate library contexts, a provider
loaded between the two being created, or providers which differ in what
they advertise - in 4.0, for example, the default provider advertises SM2
where the FIPS provider does not. A deployment meeting the condition is
also unable to negotiate the affected algorithms with legitimate clients,
since the same stale count hides the corresponding certificates, so the
misconfiguration is likely to be noticed. For that reason, and because the
configuration is not the default, this issue has been assessed as Low
severity.

FIPS impact: no
No FIPS modules are affected by this issue as the affected code is outside
the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

misconfiguration is likely to be noticed. For that reason, and because the
configuration is not the default, this issue has been assessed as Low
severity.

FIPS impact: no
No FIPS modules are affected by this issue as the affected code is outside
the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

cna.title: Koha Community Koha - Stored SQL Injection via agefield in Automatic Item Modifications by Age

descriptions.value: A stored SQL injection vulnerability in Koha through 24.11.17, 25.05.12, 25.11.06, and 26.05.01 allows authenticated staff with the tools => items_batchmod permission to read arbitrary database contents by storing a SQL payload in the agefield value of an automatic item modification rule. The agefield value is stored verbatim to the system preference and later interpolated without parameterization into a SQL query in C4::Items::ToggleNewStatus (line 1228) when the scheduled cron job executes. The injection is SELECT-only under standard MariaDB/MySQL DBI single-statement execution; a time-based SLEEP payload is also achievable via the cron trigger. An attacker can read the entire Koha database including patron PII and staff bcrypt password hashes.

cna.title: netfilter: xt_connmark: reject invalid shift parameters

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Malformed CONNMARK rev2 rules are installed via IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt or nftables NFNetlink (nft_compat); per kernel CNA guidance netfilter/xtables rule setup is Local even though installed rules later evaluate on ingress/egress packets through ipt_do_table/ip6t_do_table.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls shift_bits and shift_dir in xt_connmark_tginfo2 when installing the rev2 CONNMARK target and can send conntrack-tracked packets to reliably hit connmark_tg_shift(); no race, memory layout, or victim state outside attacker control is required.
PR:L - Installing CONNMARK iptables/nftables rules requires CAP_NET_ADMIN in the target network namespace, obtainable by unprivileged users via unshare -Urn; ip_tables.c do_ipt_set_ctl() and nfnetlink.c nfnetlink_rcv() enforce ns_capable/netlink_net_capable against the namespace user_ns.
UI:N - The attacker installs the malformed CONNMARK rev2 rule and generates matching conntrack-associated traffic in their namespace; no separate victim action such as opening files, mounting media, or clicking links is required.
S:U - Undefined shift during xt_CONNMARK packet targeting and resulting mark corruption remain within the host kernel security authority; this is standard local kernel netfilter compromise, not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or sandbox boundary crossing.
C:L - Undefined-behavior shifts on 32-bit mark values produce attacker-influenced unpredictable ct->mark and skb->mark results observable through conntrack netlink and mark-based iptables/nftables matches, leaking altered connection-classification state within the namespace.
I:H - Invalid shift_bits or shift_dir corrupt connmark_tg_shift() output written to nf_conn->mark and skb->mark, subverting mark-dependent firewall, policy-routing, QoS, and multi-tenant container egress controls on cloud routers and internet-facing servers.
A:H - Evaluating a malformed CONNMARK rev2 rule with shift_bits>=32 triggers C11 undefined-shift UB in connmark_tg_shift() during softirq netfilter processing; UBSAN-instrumented kernels panic on shift-out-of-bounds, and UB in the packet hot path can destabilize conntrack-driven forwarding.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: xt_connmark: reject invalid shift parameters

Revision 2 of the CONNMARK target accepts user-controlled shift
parameters and applies them to 32-bit mark values in
connmark_tg_shift().

A shift_bits value of 32 or more triggers an undefined-shift bug when
the rule is evaluated. Invalid shift_dir values are also accepted and
silently fall back to the left-shift path.

Reject invalid revision-2 shift parameters in connmark_tg_check() so
malformed rules fail at installation time, before they can reach the
packet path.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: act_ct: preserve tc_skb_cb across defragmentation

tcf_ct_handle_fragments() calls nf_ct_handle_fragments() without saving
and restoring skb->cb. The defrag helper clears IPCB/IP6CB, which aliases
the tc_skb_cb/qdisc_skb_cb control buffer. Fragmented traffic through
act_ct therefore loses qdisc metadata such as pkt_segs and can trigger
WARN_ON_ONCE() in qdisc_pkt_segs() when panic_on_warn is enabled.

Save and restore the full tc_skb_cb around nf_ct_handle_fragments(),
matching the pattern used by ovs_ct_handle_fragments().

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The bug fires in tcf_ct_act() on the packet datapath (sch_handle_ingress/egress → tc_run → tcf_classify) when IP fragments arrive; on OVN/Kubernetes/SDN gateways and mlx5 offload nodes with act_ct already installed, a remote peer triggers it by sending fragmented traffic with no local access.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls fragment boundaries and ordering; nf_ct_handle_fragments() memset of IPCB/IP6CB that aliases tc_skb_cb runs deterministically on each matching fragment through the configured ct action without races or memory-layout dependencies.
PR:N - Installing act_ct requires CAP_NET_ADMIN, but triggering the bug on an already-configured internet-facing or tenant-facing gateway needs no target credentials; a remote attacker only sends crafted IP fragments, matching CNA precedent for packet-driven act_ct issues (e.g., CVE-2023-52610).
UI:N - Exploitation requires only attacker-generated fragmented packets reaching a host with act_ct on clsact/ingress; no victim login, mount, or other interactive action is needed.
S:U - WARN/panic and corrupted qdisc/tc metadata occur entirely within the host kernel security domain; this is not a VM escape, sandbox breakout, or IOMMU boundary bypass.
C:N - memset(IPCB/IP6CB) zeroes tc_skb_cb/qdisc_skb_cb fields in place without out-of-bounds read or use-after-free; no kernel memory contents are disclosed to the attacker, only skb control-block metadata is clobbered.
I:L - Clearing pkt_segs, pkt_len, post_ct, and zone corrupts tc/qdisc state consumed by bstats_update, sch_cake/sch_qfq, and cls_flower zone matching, enabling attacker-driven mis-accounting and mis-handling of packets on the affected path.
A:H - Zeroed pkt_segs makes qdisc_pkt_segs() hit DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE when it disagrees with GSO segment count; with panic_on_warn enabled this kernel-panics the host, and the condition is repeatable with sustained fragmented traffic.

can: bcm: fix CAN frame rx/tx statistics

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: bcm: fix CAN frame rx/tx statistics

KCSAN detected a data race within the bcm_rx_handler() when two CAN frames
have been simultaneously received and processed in a single rx op by two
different CPUs.

Use atomic operations with (signed) long data types to access the
statistics in the hot path to fix the KCSAN complaint.

Additionally simplify the update and check of statistics overflow by
using the atomic operations in separate bcm_update_[rx|tx]_stats()
functions. The rx variant runs under bcm_rx_update_lock to prevent
races when resetting the two rx counters; the tx variant runs under
bcm_tx_lock and only needs to guard its own counter's overflow.

As the rx path resets its values already at LONG_MAX / 100, there is
no conflict between the two locking domains (bcm_rx_update_lock vs.
bcm_tx_lock) even for ops that use both paths.

The rx statistics update and the frames_filtered update in
bcm_rx_changed() were previously performed in two separate
bcm_rx_update_lock sections. For an rx op subscribed on all interfaces
(ifindex == 0), bcm_rx_handler() can run concurrently on different
CPUs, so a counter reset by one CPU between these two sections could
leave frames_filtered larger than frames_abs on another CPU, producing
a bogus (even negative) reduction percentage in procfs. Update the
statistics in the same critical section as bcm_rx_changed() to close
this gap, which also removes the now unneeded extra lock/unlock pair
around the traffic_flags calculation.

cna.title: selinux: avoid sk_socket dereference in selinux_sctp_bind_connect()

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The vulnerable code runs in the SCTP receive softirq path when a remote peer sends an authenticated ASCONF chunk (ADD_IP/SET_PRIMARY) on an existing association; packets enter via sctp_rcv() from the network stack, not local syscalls.
AC:L - An attacker with an established SCTP association controls ASCONF timing and can flood ADD_IP/SET_PRIMARY during the documented post-close() teardown window when sk_socket is NULL but associations still process shutdown-state packets.
PR:N - Exploitation requires only the ability to complete a normal SCTP association handshake with a SELinux-protected peer; no Linux capabilities, root, or local shell access are needed to send the triggering ASCONF packets over the network.
UI:N - No victim user action is required beyond normal server operation; the crash is triggered by attacker-sent ASCONF traffic arriving while the kernel processes socket teardown after application close(), not by opening files or clicking links.
S:U - Impact is a kernel NULL pointer dereference panic/oops within the same kernel security domain; it does not cross VM, container, or IOMMU boundaries and is a standard remote denial-of-service against the host kernel.
C:N - The failure mode is a direct NULL pointer dereference of sk->sk_socket before reading sock->sk; there is no use-after-free, out-of-bounds access, or memory corruption that could yield information disclosure.
I:N - The bug does not write or corrupt memory; selinux_socket_bind()/connect_helper() crash immediately on the NULL socket pointer without modifying kernel data structures or achieving code execution.
A:H - Dereferencing a NULL sk_socket in softirq causes a kernel oops/panic, crashing the entire system; this is repeatable whenever ASCONF arrives during the post-close() window on SCTP associations in shutdown states.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

selinux: avoid sk_socket dereference in selinux_sctp_bind_connect()

selinux_sctp_bind_connect() dereferences sk->sk_socket to pass a
struct socket * to selinux_socket_bind() and
selinux_socket_connect_helper().  However, when the hook is invoked
from the ASCONF softirq path (sctp_process_asconf), there is no file
reference guaranteeing that sk->sk_socket is non-NULL.  The setsockopt
callers (bindx, connectx, set_primary, sendmsg connect) hold a file
reference and are not affected.

Both selinux_socket_bind() and selinux_socket_connect_helper()
immediately resolve sock->sk, never using the struct socket * for
anything else.  Refactor the inner logic into helpers that take a
struct sock * directly so that selinux_sctp_bind_connect() never needs
to touch sk->sk_socket at all.

cna.title: net: ife: require ETH_HLEN to be pullable in ife_decode()

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The flaw is hit on the ingress packet receive path (__netif_receive_skb_core→sch_handle_ingress→tc_run→tcf_ife_act→ife_decode) when a remote peer sends a malformed IFE-encapsulated Ethernet frame to a netdev with clsact/ingress IFE decode, as in SDN/NFV/ForCES edge nodes.
AC:L - Once ingress IFE decode is present, the attacker fully controls the crafted frame (metalen, metadata size, and skb layout) to leave the inner Ethernet header non-linear or shorter than ETH_HLEN, deterministically reaching eth_type_trans() without races or uncontrollable memory layout.
PR:N - Remote exploitation needs no credentials or capabilities on the victim—only delivery of a malformed frame to an interface already configured with IFE decode; CAP_NET_ADMIN is an operator deployment prerequisite, not attacker privilege (same model as pre-configured nftables offload bugs).
UI:N - No victim user action is required beyond normal network delivery of attacker-crafted IFE traffic; exploitation does not depend on mounting, opening files, or administrator interaction at attack time.
S:U - Impact is confined to kernel packet-processing memory within the same kernel security authority; this is not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-namespace scope change.
C:H - eth_type_trans() reads the inner struct ethhdr (h_dest/h_proto) via eth_skb_pull_mac()/eth_skb_pkt_type() without ensuring ETH_HLEN bytes are linear, causing an out-of-bounds kernel read that can disclose adjacent skb/page memory beyond a few bytes.
I:N - The defect is a missing pskb_may_pull() bounds check leading to out-of-bounds reads and crash; there is no write, UAF, or demonstrated arbitrary modification or control-flow hijack primitive.
A:H - The fix commit states malformed IFE frames can crash the kernel; accessing a non-linear or undersized inner Ethernet header in eth_type_trans() can trigger KASAN faults, oops, or panic on the softirq receive path.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: ife: require ETH_HLEN to be pullable in ife_decode()

ife decode may return after making only the outer IFE header and
metadata pullable. The caller then passes the decapsulated packet to
eth_type_trans(), which expects the inner Ethernet header to be
accessible from the linear data area.

With a malformed IFE frame, the inner Ethernet header may still be
shorter than ETH_HLEN in the linear area, which can lead to a crash in
the original code.

Fix this by extending the pull check in ife_decode() so that the inner
Ethernet header is also guaranteed to be pullable before returning.

cna.title: Authentik Security authentik - Privilege Escalation

descriptions.value: A privilege escalation vulnerability in Authentik Security authentik through 2026.5.6 allows an attacker with a source-scoped SCIM provisioning token to take over any user account including superusers by provisioning a SCIM user that matches an existing local user by username. The SCIM user ingest function adopts pre-existing local accounts by username without validating scope boundaries. An attacker can rewrite or delete any account, including the superuser, using only a limited provisioning credential.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cpu: hotplug: Preserve per instance callback errors

cpuhp_invoke_callback() unwinds earlier callbacks for the same
hotplug state when one instance fails. The rollback path currently
reuses ret, so a successful rollback can hide the original error and
make the failed transition look successful.

Keep the rollback result separate from the original error.

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The bug is in cpuhp_invoke_callback() during CPU hotplug state transitions, reached only via local kernel paths such as sysfs /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/online, device_online/offline, and cpu_up()/cpu_down() from privileged local callers.
AC:L - An attacker can reliably trigger the bug by inducing multi-instance callback failure (e.g., -ENOMEM via memory pressure) during CPU online/offline on cloud autoscaled nodes or servers running RAID/padata where rollback callbacks succeed and overwrite the original error.
PR:L - CPU hotplug is normally admin-initiated, but an unprivileged local user can force multi-instance callback failures through memory exhaustion during system/hypervisor CPU hotplug without needing CAP_SYS_ADMIN or user-namespace admin capabilities.
UI:N - Exploitation requires no victim interaction beyond normal system operation; it is triggered during kernel CPU hotplug transitions without the user opening files, mounting filesystems, or performing other deliberate actions.
S:U - The vulnerability corrupts kernel CPU hotplug state-machine consistency and affects kernel subsystems on the same host; it does not cross a VM, container, or IOMMU security boundary to impact a separate authority.
C:H - Silently completing hotplug after a failed multi-instance rollback leaves subsystems like padata and RAID5 in a state inconsistent with the hotplug machine, which can desynchronize RCU-protected structures and enable kernel memory disclosure primitives.
I:H - When rollback overwrites the original error with success, cpuhp_up_callbacks()/cpuhp_down_callbacks() proceed and mark the CPU transition complete while multi-instance subsystem callbacks were only partially applied, corrupting kernel integrity and enabling further memory corruption.
A:H - Proceeding past a failed multi-instance hotplug step while subsystems such as padata, RAID5, or virtio-net instances are left in an inconsistent partially-rolled-back state can cause kernel oops, panic, or hang on production cloud and server systems.

cna.title: Unintended Proxy or Intermediary in Elastic Cloud on Kubernetes Leading to Cross-Namespace Secret Disclosure

descriptions.value: The Elastic Cloud on Kubernetes (ECK) operator reads a list of secret references from an annotation on secrets it manages, and it accepts the namespace recorded in each reference without validating that the reference is authorized for the resource being reconciled. A user whose Kubernetes permissions are limited to their own namespace can write that annotation, trigger a reconcile, and cause the operator to use its cluster-wide secret permissions to copy the contents of a secret from any other namespace into a secret the user can read.

cna.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in CTI-Transmute Conversion Graph via Malicious STIX/MISP Content

descriptions.value: CAPEC-63 Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

CTI-Transmute is affected by a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the conversion graph used to visualise converted MISP and STIX content.

Attacker-controlled values originating from converted CTI data were passed to multiple HTML-parsing sinks in the graph user interface without sufficient neutralisation. In particular, node labels, node sublabels, edge labels, node properties, edge properties, and node types could contain crafted HTML or JavaScript content.

The Pivotick graph library renders some of these values through HTML-parsing operations. Consequently, a malicious value such as an HTML element containing an event handler could be interpreted as markup rather than displayed as plain text. The first remediation explicitly notes that Pivotick rendered node and edge labels as HTML and therefore introduced escaping before data was handed to the graph renderer.

A separate vulnerable sink was present in the Open raw JSON functionality. The raw object associated with a graph node was inserted into a new document using document.write() and an interpolated HTML string. Crafted JSON content could therefore break out of the intended <pre> element and inject executable markup. The fix replaced this construction with DOM APIs and assigns the JSON using textContent.

The initial correction did not cover all Pivotick rendering paths. A subsequent patch addressed additional XSS vectors in the graph properties panel. Values derived from the original CTI object—including property names, property values, hash algorithm names, child attributes, edge properties, and STIX object types—could still reach Pivotick's HTML resolver. According to the patch, Pivotick's tryResolveHTMLElement processes string values using template.innerHTML, allowing malicious markup to execute when a graph node is hovered over or selected.

The complete remediation therefore:

  *  HTML-escapes node labels, node sublabels, and edge labels before they are passed to Pivotick.
  *  Restricts graph node type values to a safe identifier character set.
  *  Wraps node and edge property values in DOM elements populated through textContent, preventing Pivotick from treating attacker-controlled strings as HTML.
  *  Replaces the raw-JSON popup's interpolated document.write() with DOM construction and textContent.

cna.title: ocfs2: avoid moving extents to occupied clusters

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Exploitation requires the OCFS2_IOC_MOVE_EXT ioctl on a locally mounted ocfs2 volume via sys_ioctl→vfs_ioctl→ocfs2_ioctl; OCFS2 has no network-facing handler exposing this code path.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls me_goal and move length on the non-auto path; an occupied goal at the end of an alloc group deterministically bypasses ocfs2_probe_alloc_group() and reaches __ocfs2_move_extent() with no races or external preconditions.
PR:L - OCFS2_IOC_MOVE_EXT performs no capable() check (unlike FITRIM); any local user with FMODE_WRITE on a regular file on an ocfs2 mount can invoke ioctl(), including root inside a user namespace per kernel CNA guidance.
UI:N - The attacker issues OCFS2_IOC_MOVE_EXT on their own writable fd with crafted parameters; no victim interaction or third-party action is required beyond the enterprise ocfs2 mount already being present.
S:U - Impact is confined to on-disk data corruption and filesystem availability within the same cluster node/kernel authority; it does not cross VM, container, or IOMMU security boundaries.
C:H - __ocfs2_move_extent() copies into clusters still allocated to other inodes, creating cross-file block aliasing on shared cluster storage so later reads through the new extent can return another tenant's or root-owned file contents.
I:H - ocfs2_duplicate_clusters_by_page() writes attacker-controlled file data into physical clusters owned by other inodes before the bitmap is updated, enabling arbitrary corruption of files the attacker lacks write permission to on shared OCFS2 storage.
A:H - Dual allocation and bitmap/extent inconsistency can trigger ocfs2_error(), forcing remount-ro or panic on the node and corrupting shared storage in ways that impair availability for all cluster members until fsck.ocfs2.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: avoid moving extents to occupied clusters

For non-auto OCFS2_IOC_MOVE_EXT operations, userspace supplies a physical
me_goal.  ocfs2_move_extent() initializes new_phys_cpos from that goal and
expects ocfs2_probe_alloc_group() to replace it with a free run in the
target block group.

The probe currently leaves *phys_cpos unchanged if the scan reaches the
end of the group without finding a free run.  An occupied goal at the last
bit can therefore survive the probe and be passed to
__ocfs2_move_extent(), which copies file data into a cluster still owned
by another inode before the bitmap is updated.

When the probe does find a free run, it also subtracts move_len from the
ending bit.  The start of an N-bit run ending at i is i - N + 1, so the
current calculation can report the bit immediately before the free run.

Clear *phys_cpos before scanning and use the correct free-run start. 
Callers already treat a zero result as -ENOSPC, so failed probes no longer
continue with an occupied caller-controlled goal.

cna.title: fs/ntfs3: add bounds check to run_get_highest_vcn()

scenarios.value:
AV:L - mount(2)/get_tree_bdev on a crafted NTFS block device or loop image reaches ntfs_fill_super()→ntfs_loadlog_and_replay()→log_replay()→do_action(UpdateMappingPairs)→run_get_highest_vcn(); no network handler parses $LogFile.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls the on-disk $LogFile UpdateMappingPairs record and embedded non-resident mapping-pairs bytes; omitting the 0x00 terminator deterministically drives the unbounded parser past the attribute buffer on the first replay mount with no race.
PR:N - The attacker needs no account or privilege on the victim; supplying a malicious NTFS image on USB/removable media, a disk image, or shared storage is sufficient for udisks2/systemd automount or an administrator mount to reach journal replay.
UI:N - Desktop/kiosk/shared-workstation automounters mount attacker-supplied NTFS media and run $LogFile replay without the user opening files or running commands; insertion of the crafted volume is sufficient to trigger parsing on mount.
S:U - Slab out-of-bounds reads and resulting mount-time kernel faults stay within the host kernel security authority; no VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-boundary scope change.
C:H - run_get_highest_vcn() scans mapping pairs with no length bound, performing slab out-of-bounds byte reads via run_unpack_s64(); kernel guidance treats heap out-of-bounds reads as enabling broad adjacent-slab information disclosure.
I:H - Parsed run lengths and offsets come from attacker-chosen and out-of-bounds heap bytes and, if the loop terminates, are written into attr->nres.evcn during log replay, corrupting non-resident extent metadata and redirecting later replayed cluster I/O.
A:H - The demonstrated KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read in the mount task can fault into unmapped adjacent memory, producing a kernel oops/panic and denying service until reboot.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fs/ntfs3: add bounds check to run_get_highest_vcn()

run_get_highest_vcn() parses a packed NTFS mapping-pairs buffer without
any length bound, relying solely on a 0x00 terminator to stop.  A
crafted $LogFile UpdateMappingPairs record whose embedded attribute
contains mapping-pairs runs without a terminator causes the function to
read past the slab allocation, triggering a KASAN slab-out-of-bounds
read on mount.

The sibling function run_unpack() received an analogous bounds-check in
commit b62567bca474 ("ntfs3: add buffer boundary checks to run_unpack()"),
but run_get_highest_vcn() was missed.

Take a run_buf_size parameter and reject any run header whose payload
would extend past the buffer end, mirroring the pattern used by
run_unpack().  The caller in fslog.c passes the remaining attribute
bytes after the mapping-pairs offset.

KASAN report (on mainline v7.1 merge window HEAD):

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in run_get_highest_vcn+0x3c0/0x410
  Read of size 1 at addr ffff88800e2d5400 by task mount/72
  Call Trace:
   run_get_highest_vcn+0x3c0/0x410
   do_action.isra.0+0x3ba8/0x7b50
   log_replay+0x9ddd/0x10200
   ntfs_loadlog_and_replay+0x4ad/0x610
   ntfs_fill_super+0x214a/0x4540

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

macsec: don't read an unset MAC header in macsec_encrypt()

macsec_encrypt() reads the Ethernet header via eth_hdr(skb)
(skb->head + skb->mac_header) to memmove() the 12 source/destination MAC
bytes forward and make room for the SecTAG.

On the AF_PACKET SOCK_RAW + PACKET_QDISC_BYPASS transmit path the skb
reaches the macsec ndo_start_xmit() with the MAC header unset, so
eth_hdr(skb) resolves to skb->head + (u16)~0 and the read is out of
bounds: a 12-byte heap over-read that is also emitted on the wire as the
frame's outer source/destination MAC. KASAN reports a slab-out-of-bounds
read in macsec_start_xmit() on 6.0; on current mainline a CONFIG_DEBUG_NET
build flags it as an unset mac header in skb_mac_header().

On the TX path the L2 header is at skb->data, so use skb_eth_hdr(), added
by commit 96cc4b69581d ("macvlan: do not assume mac_header is set in
macvlan_broadcast()") for exactly this purpose.

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The bug is reached only via local AF_PACKET SOCK_RAW transmit with PACKET_QDISC_BYPASS to a macsec netdev; it is a TX-only ndo_start_xmit path, not reachable from remote network packet reception.
AC:L - An attacker fully controls the trigger: create a raw packet socket with a specific ethertype, enable PACKET_QDISC_BYPASS, and send a frame on a configured macsec interface with protect_frames enabled.
PR:L - Exploitation requires CAP_NET_RAW for AF_PACKET and CAP_NET_ADMIN to create/configure a macsec netdev and TX SA keys; both are obtainable by an unprivileged user inside a user namespace with delegated capabilities.
UI:N - No victim interaction is required; the attacker sends crafted frames directly through the vulnerable transmit path without any action from another user or administrator.
S:U - Impact is confined to kernel heap disclosure and possible kernel crash on the same host; it does not cross a VM, container, or IOMMU security boundary to affect a separate authority.
C:H - eth_hdr(skb) performs a 12-byte slab out-of-bounds heap read when mac_header is unset; the leaked kernel memory is copied into the transmitted frame's source/destination MAC fields, disclosing sensitive heap contents.
I:L - The memmove in macsec_encrypt() overwrites the outgoing frame's 12-byte Ethernet addresses with leaked heap data, causing unauthorized modification of transmitted packet contents without arbitrary kernel memory writes.
A:H - Reading from skb->head plus unset mac_header offset 65535 causes a slab out-of-bounds access that KASAN flags and can page-fault into a kernel oops or panic when macsec_encrypt() runs on affected builds.

cna.title: drbd: reject data replies with an out-of-range payload size

scenarios.value:
AV:N - Exploitation is delivered over the DRBD replication TCP protocol when a victim node receives a malicious P_DATA_REPLY from its peer or a man-in-the-middle on that link; recv_dless_read() is reached from drbdd() without any local syscall or ioctl on the victim.
AC:L - The peer fully controls the wire length in the P_DATA_REPLY header, and two independent triggers (unsigned-to-signed overflow or digest subtraction underflow) deterministically force expect negative so drbd_recv_all_warn() receives SIZE_MAX bytes whenever the victim issues a remote read.
PR:N - No account, capability, or administrative access on the victim host is required; a malicious DRBD peer or network man-in-the-middle on the replication link can send the crafted reply after connection setup, and cram-hmac-alg peer authentication is optional.
UI:N - No end-user action is needed because diskless-primary and read-balancing configurations automatically send P_DATA_REQUEST packets to the peer, and the malicious P_DATA_REPLY is processed in the kernel receiver thread during normal I/O.
S:U - The out-of-bounds socket receive corrupts kernel memory on the same host that runs DRBD; successful exploitation yields kernel compromise on that node but does not by itself cross a VM, container, or IOMMU security boundary.
C:H - Receiving up to SIZE_MAX attacker-controlled bytes past the mapped bio page is an out-of-bounds kernel write that can corrupt adjacent heap or page data and be leveraged for arbitrary kernel memory disclosure, not merely a bounded leak.
I:H - The bug copies attacker-chosen network data beyond the allocated bio buffer boundary, providing a kernel out-of-bounds write primitive that can corrupt kernel structures and enable arbitrary code execution or privilege escalation.
A:H - Writing gigabytes past a bio page can immediately corrupt critical kernel memory and cause oops or panic, and repeated malicious replies can keep the node unavailable even before full exploitation.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drbd: reject data replies with an out-of-range payload size

recv_dless_read() receives a P_DATA_REPLY from a peer into the bio of an
outstanding read request. The peer-supplied payload length reaches it as
the signed int data_size, and two peer-controlled inputs can make it
negative. With a negotiated data-integrity-alg the digest length is
subtracted first, so a reply whose payload is smaller than the digest
underflows data_size. With no integrity algorithm (the default) data_size
is assigned from the unsigned h95/h100 wire length and drbdd() never
bounds it for a payload-carrying command, so a length above INT_MAX casts
it negative; this path needs no non-default feature. The bio receive loop
then computes expect = min_t(int, data_size, bv_len), which is negative,
and drbd_recv_all_warn(mapped, expect) receives with a size_t of SIZE_MAX
into the first mapped page.

The sibling receive path read_in_block() is not affected: it uses an
unsigned size and rejects it against DRBD_MAX_BIO_SIZE before receiving.
Reject a data reply whose size is negative after the optional digest
subtraction, covering both triggers.

Impact: a malicious or man-in-the-middle DRBD peer copies attacker-chosen
bytes past a bio page in the receiver, corrupting kernel memory. A node
that reads from its peer (a diskless node, or read-balancing to the peer)
is exposed in the default configuration; data-integrity-alg is not
required.

cna.title: can: bcm: extend bcm_tx_lock usage for data and timer updates

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The bug is reached only through PF_CAN/CAN_BCM socket sendmsg() TX_SETUP updates racing hrtimer-driven bcm_can_tx(); it is not triggered by remote network services or CAN bus traffic alone.
AC:L - The attacker controls both sides of the race by creating cyclic TX ops with STARTTIMER/SETTIMER and repeatedly issuing TX_SETUP while the softirq hrtimer fires, making the window reliably winnable without external timing luck.
PR:L - bcm_sendmsg()/bcm_connect() enforce no capability checks; any local user with access to a CAN interface (including vcan created with CAP_NET_ADMIN inside an unprivileged user namespace) can open BCM sockets and drive TX_SETUP.
UI:N - Exploitation requires only the attacker opening a BCM socket and sending TX_SETUP messages; no victim interaction such as mounting filesystems or opening files is needed.
S:U - Impact is confined to kernel memory/state corruption and local privilege effects on the host running CAN BCM; it does not cross a VM, container, or IOMMU security boundary by itself.
C:H - Racing updates can let bcm_can_tx() transmit partially updated or unvalidated frames (e.g., len>64) before bcm_tx_setup() rejects them, and many CAN driver xmit paths memcpy(cf->data, cf->len) trusting len, causing kernel out-of-bounds reads.
I:H - Concurrent unsynchronized writes to op->frames, flags, count, and ktime_t timer fields corrupt shared in-kernel BCM state that directly feeds skb construction and driver transmission, providing attacker-influenced memory corruption primitives.
A:H - Observing torn/unvalidated frames in bcm_can_tx() during active timers can trigger kernel WARN/Oops/panic via out-of-bounds accesses in CAN drivers, and torn ktime_t/count reads can disrupt cyclic transmission causing denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: bcm: extend bcm_tx_lock usage for data and timer updates

Stage new CAN frame content for an existing tx op into a kmalloc()'d
buffer and validate it there, mirroring the approach already used in
bcm_rx_setup(). Only copy the validated data into op->frames while
holding op->bcm_tx_lock, so bcm_can_tx() and bcm_tx_timeout_handler()
can no longer observe a partially updated or unvalidated frame.

Add a missing error path for memcpy_from_msg() when copying CAN frame
data from userspace.

Also move the kt_ival1/kt_ival2/ival1/ival2 updates in bcm_tx_setup()
under op->bcm_tx_lock, and read kt_ival1/kt_ival2/count under the same
lock in bcm_tx_set_expiry() and bcm_tx_timeout_handler(), closing the
torn 64-bit ktime_t read on 32-bit platforms.

descriptions.value: Craft CMS versions from 4.0.0-RC1 before 4.18.2 and from 5.0.0-RC1 before 5.10.6 contain an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the control panel element-search condition handling. Craft cleanses the outer request-controlled condition array via Component::cleanseConfig(), but Conditions::createCondition() later decodes and merges the JSON string in condition.config without re-running cleanseConfig() on the decoded configuration. Because condition.config is a JSON string during the first cleanse, Yii special config keys such as 'as ...' and 'on ...' can be hidden inside it and, after JSON decoding, are interpreted by Yii as behavior/event configuration during FieldLayout object creation. An attacker with an authenticated control panel session (and a valid CSRF token) can exploit this to execute operating system commands as the PHP/web user.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fbdev: broadsheetfb: fix potential memory leak in broadsheetfb_probe()

The memory allocated for pagerefs in fb_deferred_io_init() is not freed

cna.title: dm era: fix NULL pointer dereference in metadata_open()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

dm era: fix NULL pointer dereference in metadata_open()

metadata_open() returns NULL when kzalloc_obj() fails, but the
caller era_ctr() only checks IS_ERR(md).  Since IS_ERR(NULL)
returns false, the NULL pointer is treated as a valid result
and later assigned to era->md, leading to a NULL pointer
dereference when the metadata is accessed.

Fix this by returning ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) on allocation failure,
consistent with dm-cache-metadata.c, dm-thin-metadata.c, and
dm-clone-metadata.c which all use ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) for the
same pattern.

cna.title: netfilter: nf_queue: pin bridge device while NFQUEUE holds fake dst

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The bug is reached via netfilter NFQUEUE and local bridge/rtnetlink setup (__nf_queue skb_dst_force on br_netfilter's embedded fake rtable, then bridge teardown while packets remain queued), not from unauthenticated remote input alone; kernel guidance classifies netfilter/nftables paths as Local.
AC:L - With CAP_NET_ADMIN in a user namespace, an attacker can bind NFQUEUE, queue br_netfilter bridged packets, and delete the bridge while packets sit in the queue, deterministically hitting nfqnl_dev_drop/dst_release after struct net_bridge is freed.
PR:L - Configuring NFQUEUE/nftables rules, loading br_netfilter, creating/deleting bridges, and binding nfnetlink queues require CAP_NET_ADMIN, obtainable by unprivileged users via user/network namespaces (unshare -Urn), not init-namespace root.
UI:N - Exploitation requires only the attacker's own netlink, nftables, and traffic generation; no victim must mount filesystems, open files, or perform other interactive actions beyond the attacker's programmatic setup.
S:U - Impact is kernel heap corruption in the same host security domain via freed embedded fake_rtable/metrics inside struct net_bridge; this is standard kernel UAF/privilege-escalation territory, not a VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary escape.
C:H - skb_dst_force in __nf_queue holds a dst reference to fake_rtable storage embedded in struct net_bridge; after bridge unregister frees that object, dst_release operates on freed kmalloc memory—a UAF that can disclose kernel memory via slab reuse.
I:H - The dangling fake rtable/metrics pointer in queued skbs can be combined with heap grooming to obtain arbitrary kernel writes or control-flow hijack during dst_destroy/netdev_put, consistent with kernel UAF integrity guidance.
A:H - Freeing queued NFQUEUE entries after bridge teardown dereferences freed net_bridge/fake_rtable in dst_release, causing kernel oops/panic-class faults; repeated triggering yields reliable denial of service on bridge/NFQUEUE deployments.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nf_queue: pin bridge device while NFQUEUE holds fake dst

The br_netfilter fake rtable is embedded in struct net_bridge and is
attached to bridged packets with skb_dst_set_noref(). If such a packet is
queued to NFQUEUE, __nf_queue() upgrades that fake dst with
skb_dst_force().

At that point the queued skb can hold a real dst reference after bridge
teardown has started. The problem is not that every bridged packet needs
its own dst reference. The problem is that NFQUEUE can keep the bridge
private fake dst alive after unregister begins.

Fix this by keeping the bridge fake dst model unchanged and pinning the
bridge master device only while the packet sits in NFQUEUE. Record the
bridge device in nf_queue_entry when the queued skb carries a bridge fake
dst, take a device reference for the queue lifetime, and drop it when the
queue entry is freed.

Also make sure queued entries are reaped when that bridge device goes
down, and drop the redundant nf_bridge_info_exists() test from the fake
dst detection.

This keeps netdev_priv(br->dev) alive until verdict completion, so the
embedded fake rtable and its metrics backing storage cannot be freed out
from under dst_release(). It also avoids the constant refcount bump and
avoids using ipv4-specific dst helpers for IPv6 bridge traffic.

cna.title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: Missing authentication on the management interface

credits.value: Llorenç Romá Alvarez, Security Researcher, Cyber Defence Campus, Switzerland

scenarios.value: Score agreed with the vendor for the standalone impact of the interface. Adjacent (AV:A) reach via the multicast discovery on 225.0.0.37:16001. C:N because the readable data is device identifiers and non-confidential configuration; I:L because configuration changes alone have limited impact; A:N. Command injection and firmware replacement through the same interface are scored in their own records. If the management interface is IP-routed, use AV:N -> CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N = 5.3 MEDIUM.

timeline.value: DJI acknowledged the vulnerability and provided its assessment

solutions.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

supportingMedia.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

references.name: DJI AeroScope Mobile research repository (technical details)

workarounds.value: Connect the unit's management Ethernet port only to an isolated network segment with no untrusted hosts, and do not route or bridge that segment to other networks, so that TCP port 16000 and the multicast discovery traffic (225.0.0.37, UDP port 16001) cannot be reached. Restrict physical access to the USB operator port.

supportingMedia.value: Connect the unit's management Ethernet port only to an isolated network segment with no untrusted hosts, and do not route or bridge that segment to other networks, so that TCP port 16000 and the multicast discovery traffic (225.0.0.37, UDP port 16001) cannot be reached. descriptions.value:
Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306) in the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to read device information, such as the serial number, MAC address, IP address and radio configuration, and to change configuration settings. The service accepts commands in DJI's proprietary DUML protocol without any authentication. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. The same commands are also accepted over the USB operator port. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

cna.title: AIOHTTP: Concatenated compressed streams cause excessive CPU use

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, aiohttp decompresses each member of a payload containing many concatenated gzip, deflate, or zstd streams by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, causing quadratic CPU use. Empty members produce no output, so client_max_size and output backpressure do not limit the work. A remote attacker can block a server event loop with a crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message, and a malicious server can similarly block a client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: OpenMage magento-lts 20.17.0 before 20.18.2 Unrestricted File Upload RCE via Custom Options

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenMage magento-lts 20.17.0 before 20.18.2 Unrestricted File Upload RCE via Custom Options

descriptions.value: OpenMage magento-lts 20.17.0 before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability because the general/file/protected_extensions blocklist omits phar, php8, and phps. Unauthenticated attackers can upload a .phar file through a product File custom option to a predictable media/custom_options path and request it directly to execute code on servers that map .phar to PHP and serve that directory.

An attacker able to influence build input could cause file contents interpreted as dependency entries to appear in debug logs or build-step metadata, subject to the envd process’s permissions. cna.title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Incorrect Authorization in Admin Controllers ACL

Authenticated restricted administrators can mass cancel or hold orders, rewrite order shipping addresses, export customer report data, or create REST roles despite their role denying those permissions.

cna.title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow saving TIFF with libtiff when tags override image size

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 2.3.0 through 12.3.0, Pillow applications that save compressed TIFF images through libtiff can pass attacker-controlled image geometry tags to the encoder while allocating its row buffer from the actual image dimensions. The affected TiffImagePlugin._save path allows ImageWidth, ImageLength, or SamplesPerPixel from exif=, tiffinfo=, or a source TIFF IFD to make libtiff consume a larger scanline than the buffer supplied by ImagingLibTiffEncode. This can read heap memory into the generated TIFF or crash the process. When TIFF Predictor 2 is enabled, libtiff can rewrite the oversized scanline in place and corrupt memory beyond the buffer. A carried-over PlanarConfiguration value of 2 instead makes libtiff use a shorter scanline and can produce an undecodable output file, but is not established to cause the out-of-bounds access. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Missing membership acceptance check permits group share-right deletion by invitees in Psono Server

descriptions.value: An authenticated user with a pending or declined group invitation carrying share_admin=True can delete the group's share-right records, revoking that group's access to the affected shares and their contained secrets for all accepted group members. The underlying shares and secrets are not deleted, and secret contents are not disclosed.

scenarios.value: Authenticated user with a pending or declined group invitation carrying share_admin=True and knowledge of a target group share-right UUID. Unauthorized deletion modifies access-control records and removes the group's access to affected shared data.

timeline.value: Vulnerability reported to esaqa GmbH by Nicholas Mullenski / K70n0s510 (2026-10-12 21:45 CEST, UTC+02:00)
Vendor fix implemented in commit 86e7ce7fdbb04fc4ae3430cc434179630948d48d, included in version 7.5.1 of both editions.

solutions.value: Upgrade Psono Server Community Edition and Psono Server Enterprise Edition to version 7.5.1 or later. Version 7.5.1 was released for both editions on 2026-10-13. The patch adds accepted=True to the User_Group_Membership authorization query in DeleteShareRightSerializer.validate, making group share-right deletion require both accepted membership and share_admin=True, matching the group authorization check in the create path.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade Psono Server Community Edition and Psono Server Enterprise Edition to version 7.5.1 or later. Version 7.5.1 was released for both editions on 2026-10-13. The patch adds accepted=True to the User_Group_Membership authorization query in DeleteShareRightSerializer.validate, making group share-right deletion require both accepted membership and share_admin=True, matching the group authorization check in the create path.

workarounds.value: Until the patch is deployed, use authorized group administration to remove pending and declined group memberships carrying share-admin privileges, or clear their share_admin flag. Avoid granting share-admin privileges to unaccepted invitees on affected versions.

supportingMedia.value: Until the patch is deployed, use authorized group administration to remove pending and declined group memberships carrying share-admin privileges, or clear their share_admin flag. Avoid granting share-admin privileges to unaccepted invitees on affected versions.

descriptions.value: Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition before 7.5.1 do not require accepted group membership when authorizing deletion of group share-rights. The DELETE /share/right/ endpoint checks for a membership matching the target group, the authenticated user, and share_admin=True, but omits accepted=True. An authenticated remote attacker who has been invited to a group with share-admin privileges, and who knows a group share-right UUID, can therefore delete that group's share-right record without accepting the invitation or after declining it. Pending invitations have accepted=None, while declined invitations retain accepted=False and the share_admin flag. Deletion revokes the group's access to the affected share and its contained secrets for all accepted group members, without deleting the underlying data or disclosing secret contents. The issue was fixed in version 7.5.1 of both editions, released on 2026-10-13.

supportingMedia.value: Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition before 7.5.1 do not require accepted group membership when authorizing deletion of group share-rights. The DELETE /share/right/ endpoint checks for a membership matching the target group, the authenticated user, and share_admin=True, but omits accepted=True. An authenticated remote attacker who has been invited to a group with share-admin privileges, and who knows a group share-right UUID, can therefore delete that group's share-right record without accepting the invitation or after declining it. Pending invitations have accepted=None, while declined invitations retain accepted=False and the share_admin flag. Deletion revokes the group's access to the affected share and its contained secrets for all accepted group members, without deleting the underlying data or disclosing secret contents. The issue was fixed in version 7.5.1 of both editions, released on 2026-10-13.

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

patches.subject: fix: [website] restrict post-login redirects to local paths

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [website] restrict post-login redirects to local paths
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The fix introduces a _safe_next_url() validation function that restricts post-login redirect destinations to local paths or same-host HTTP(S) URLs. Any target that is empty, contains backslashes, control characters, leading/trailing whitespace, an unrecognized scheme, a mismatched host, or a protocol-relative form is rejected and the user is redirected to the home page (/). Accepted same-host URLs are normalized to local paths (scheme and authority stripped) while preserving query strings and fragments, ensuring the Location header always contains a relative path. This eliminates the ability to redirect users to arbitrary external destinations after authentication.
assumptions: No specific affected or fixed version is identified in the patch metadata; the version range is recorded as unspecified.

The CVSS UI metric is set to Active (A) on the assumption that the victim must click a crafted link and submit login credentials; if the login page is auto-submitted in a phishing context, UI could be argued as Passive, but the evidence supports Active.
SC is set to Low based on the phishing/social-engineering risk of redirecting a user to an external site after login; no direct data exfiltration mechanism is present in the vulnerable code path.
The CAPEC-113 mapping is the closest available pattern for open redirect; no more specific CAPEC exists for post-login redirect manipulation.
The patch does not indicate whether this vulnerability was reported through a coordinated disclosure process; no finder or reporter credit is assigned beyond the remediation developer.
The website component is assumed to be a Flask-based web application served over HTTP(S); the patch does not specify deployment topology or additional authentication layers.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In website/app/account/account.py, the import of urlsplit and urlunsplit from urllib.parse is added. A new _safe_next_url() function is defined that validates the target string against a series of safety checks (whitespace, backslashes, control characters, scheme allowlist, host match, protocol-relative rejection, double-slash path rejection) and returns either a normalized local path or the fallback '/'. The login() handler's redirect call is changed from redirect(request.args.get('next') or '/') to redirect(_safe_next_url(request.args.get('next'))). A new test file website/tests/login_checks.py (172 lines) is added with comprehensive unit tests covering external rejection, malformed input rejection, local path preservation, same-host-with-port normalization, wrong-password non-redirect, CSRF enforcement, and remember-me cookie preservation. The website README is updated to document the new redirect validation behavior.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: exploitable over the network via a crafted URL. AC:L: no race conditions or special conditions; simply append a next parameter. AT:N: no attack requirements beyond delivering the URL. PR:N: the attacker needs no account; the victim performs the login. UI:A: the victim must actively visit the crafted URL and submit credentials. VC/VI/VA:N: the vulnerable system itself suffers no direct confidentiality, integrity, or availability loss. SC:L: subsequent confidentiality impact is low because the redirected user may be tricked into entering sensitive data on a phishing page, but the session cookie is domain-scoped and not directly exfiltrated. SI/SA:N: no subsequent integrity or availability impact is evidenced.

capecRationale.rationale: The patch directly addresses an open redirect: an attacker crafts a login URL with a malicious next parameter to redirect the victim to an external phishing site after authentication. CAPEC-113 describes exactly this attack pattern where a web application redirects to a user-controlled destination without proper validation. This is the closest and most precise CAPEC mapping available for this vulnerability class.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The login endpoint accepted an unvalidated user-supplied URL in the next query parameter and used it directly as the redirect destination, allowing an attacker to redirect authenticated users to arbitrary external sites. This is a textbook open redirect (CWE-601).

solutions.value: The fix introduces a _safe_next_url() validation function that restricts post-login redirect destinations to local paths or same-host HTTP(S) URLs. Any target that is empty, contains backslashes, control characters, leading/trailing whitespace, an unrecognized scheme, a mismatched host, or a protocol-relative form is rejected and the user is redirected to the home page (/). descriptions.value: The MISP Modules website component contains an open redirect vulnerability in its login endpoint. The /login route accepted a user-supplied next query parameter and passed it directly to Flask's redirect() function without validating the destination. An attacker could craft a URL such as https://victim-host/login?next=https://attacker.example/phish and deliver it to a user (e.g., via email or a lookalike page). After the user successfully authenticated, the application issued a 302 redirect to the attacker-controlled external URL. This enables phishing attacks where a user, believing they are still on the legitimate MISP Modules site, may enter additional credentials or sensitive information on the attacker's page. It can also be used to obscure the true destination of a link, bypassing user trust in the legitimate domain. The vulnerability requires the victim to interact with the crafted URL and complete a login, but no prior authentication or special configuration is needed on the attacker's side. The affected component is the website sub-project of misp-modules, specifically the account blueprint in website/app/account/account.py. No version boundaries are specified in the patch metadata.

cna.title: sqlite3-ruby: SQL Query Truncation

descriptions.value: sqlite3 provides Ruby bindings for the SQLite3 embedded database. Prior to 2.10.2, sqlite3-ruby casts Ruby string lengths to int before passing SQL through Database#prepare, bound String or Blob values through Statement#bind_param, and String or Blob results from Ruby-defined SQL functions and aggregates through Database#create_function and Database#create_aggregate. On 64-bit platforms, a string of 4 GiB (2^32 bytes) or larger can wrap the length so SQLite processes only a prefix. A truncated SQL string can drop trailing clauses such as a WHERE condition, while a truncated bound value matters only when the application validated the full value before binding it. Exploitation requires the application and server to accept and retain the unusually large attacker-controlled string. If a dropped SQL clause contained a bind placeholder, binding raises SQLite3::RangeException instead of running the query. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.2.

cna.title: PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade

descriptions.value: CAPEC-475 Signature Spoofing by Improper Validation

PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: OpenTelemetry-Go: Eager W3C baggage-property materialization causes bounded memory-allocation amplification

descriptions.value: OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From version 1.0.0-RC1 until version 1.47.0, baggage.Parse and propagation.Baggage.Extract eagerly materialize every W3C baggage property through parseMember, grow property slices, serialize members, and copy properties into internal/baggage.Item. A valid densely populated baggage header can therefore cause allocation traffic and retained memory disproportionate to its bounded input size. Remote impact requires baggage extraction to be enabled, attacker-controlled input to reach it, and extraction to run before authentication or on a public route; the evidence establishes increased allocation and garbage-collection pressure but not reliable process termination. This issue is fixed in version 1.47.0.

cna.title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: Hard-coded root password on the serial console

credits.value: Llorenç Romá Alvarez, Security Researcher, Cyber Defence Campus, Switzerland

scenarios.value: Scored on the only login channel that accepts the credential: the board's serial console, which requires physical access, so AV:P. No network login service (SSH/telnet) runs on the board by default. The credential is not an escalation on a host where code execution has already been achieved. BLAST RADIUS: the credential is image-wide, not per-device, so a single recovery applies to every affected unit and an operator cannot contain a leak. The vendor should also determine whether the same credential is reused in other DJI product lines; reuse was not verified in this engagement.

modules: 1300 DM810X communications board (uavmonitor_usbv1; root console credential in /etc/shadow)

timeline.value: DJI acknowledged the vulnerability and provided its assessment

solutions.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

supportingMedia.value: DJI AeroScope Mobile has been discontinued and is no longer supported by DJI. No fixed firmware is available. Operators should plan to replace affected units with a supported product and, until then, apply the workarounds.

references.name: DJI AeroScope Mobile research repository (technical details)

workarounds.value: Restrict physical access to deployed units and their serial console, and treat any unit that has left controlled custody as having a known root password. Network isolation does not mitigate this issue.

supportingMedia.value: Restrict physical access to deployed units and their serial console, and treat any unit that has left controlled custody as having a known root password. Network isolation does not mitigate this issue.

descriptions.value:
Use of hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) on the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an attacker with physical access to the board's serial console to log in as root. The same password hash is present on every unit and uses DES crypt, so the password can be recovered offline from the distributed firmware. No network login service accepts this password by default. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

cna.title: gittuf: Propagated controller policies not loaded during verification

solutions.value: Upgrade to gittuf 0.18.0 or later, then run gittuf verify-ref over the full history of each protected reference. Policy propagation has been moved back into gittuf's developer mode.

descriptions.value: In gittuf 0.10.0 through 0.17.0, the verification workflow does not load policy updates that are propagated from an upstream (controller) repository and recorded in the reference state log after the first entry being verified. Only the propagated policy in effect at the start of verification is applied, so later controller changes to global rules, such as threshold requirements and force-push blocks, are ignored and changes that these rules should block pass verification.

cna.title: gittuf: File protection rules bypassed for filenames with special characters

solutions.value: Upgrade to gittuf 0.18.0 or later, which asks Git for raw paths. Then re-run verification (gittuf verify-ref) for each protected reference: a reference that passed verification before the upgrade but fails after it contains a change that should have been blocked.

descriptions.value: In gittuf before 0.18.0, verification of file protection rules uses the quoted, escaped pathnames that Git prints by default for files with special characters (for example non-ASCII characters) instead of the raw paths. Such paths do not match patterns like file:internal/*, so the files are treated as unprotected, and a user who is not authorized by a file protection rule can change a protected file whose name contains special characters and still pass verification.

cna.title: opentelemetry-go: AttributeValueLengthLimit is fully bypassed by attribute values composed of valid U+FFFD runes

descriptions.value: OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From SDK version 1.33.0, SDK log version 0.9.0, and trace version 1.35.0 until version 1.47.0, the AttributeValueLengthLimit and WithAttributeValueLengthLimit truncation paths in sdk/internal/attrnorm, sdk/log/internal/attrnorm, and trace/auto.go do not count valid U+FFFD replacement characters. This is a distinct incomplete-fix defect in the replacement truncation code introduced by the remediation for CVE-2026-81869. Values composed of or dominated by those characters can therefore exceed the configured character and memory bound in span, log-record, and auto-instrumentation trace attributes. Attacker-controlled telemetry attributes can increase retained memory and pipeline pressure, while confidentiality and integrity are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.47.0.

cna.title: Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext

descriptions.value: CAPEC-158 Sniffing Network Traffic

Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: Nuxt dev server serves files from a parent directory that contains a lockfile

descriptions.value: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.5.0 until 4.6.4, Nuxt can choose a parent directory as the default workspaceDir in either of two cases: a stray parent lockfile when the project is outside a Git repository and has no workspace file above it, or a parent pnpm or Deno settings file that does not declare packages or a workspace, including when the project is inside a Git repository. When the development server is reachable from an untrusted network, Vite permits /_nuxt/@fs/ requests beneath that widened directory, allowing unauthenticated clients to read files such as credentials and SSH keys. The issue affects the development server only; production builds and projects whose parent directories contain no qualifying files are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

cna.title: Laravel: Task Output Injection - Concurrency Process

descriptions.value: Laravel is a web application framework. Prior to 12.71.0 and 13.40.0, Laravel's Concurrency::run process driver can treat a forged internal result message in child standard output as framework output. An application route must invoke Concurrency::run, and a task must write attacker-controlled bytes at the start of the child's standard output that form a complete JSON document followed by gzip magic bytes. Under those application-specific conditions, an attacker can forge the internal result message and achieve remote code execution. The affected behavior is not exposed by default and requires application code that routes untrusted input into task output. This issue is fixed in versions 12.71.0 and 13.40.0.

cna.title: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to multipart file/field type confusion via chunk-dependent header parsing

descriptions.value: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 3.2.1 through 3.2.5, the parser can interpret the same multipart bytes differently depending on how they are split across socket reads: when the sequence that terminates a part's header block arrives split exactly at the configured header size limit, an off by one error drops the final header line, so a part declared as a binary file attachment is emitted as an ordinary text field instead of a file. A remote client controls both the multipart body and the header padding needed to reach the boundary and can influence segmentation, so an application that applies upload validation such as malware scanning or extension checks only to file events while trusting plain field values may process the payload through the wrong path. The parser level type confusion is fully reproducible, while the downstream validation bypass depends on the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which tracks how many terminator bytes were actually buffered when the limit is reached so a split terminator no longer corrupts the final header, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, apply the same validation to field values as to file uploads rather than treating file events as a trust boundary.

cna.title: AIOHTTP: WebSocket max_msg_size bypass via integer overflow

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, the C WebSocket reader adds a declared frame length to the size of an already buffered partial message using signed 64-bit arithmetic. A length near two to the power of 63 can overflow, allowing the max_msg_size check to pass. A remote peer can send a small non-final fragment followed by an oversized message and cause unbounded memory consumption. The Python WebSocket reader is unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: Pillow: Memory DoS in TIFF and EXIF IFD parsing via overlapping tag data

descriptions.value: Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 1.0 through 12.3.0, ImageFileDirectory_v2.load() in src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py retains a separate bytes object for each out-of-line IFD tag value without limiting the total data read or preventing distinct tags from referencing the same file region. A small crafted TIFF or EXIF-bearing JPEG, PNG, WebP, or MPO can therefore cause memory use quadratic in the input size. TIFF and some JPEG paths trigger parsing during Image.open(), while other formats are exposed when EXIF is requested, including through getexif() or ImageOps.exif_transpose(). The declared pixel dimensions do not bound this metadata allocation, so decompression-bomb checks do not prevent process memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

cna.title: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-119200: a leading `//` in the request path bypasses `server/middleware` path checks and server route rules on page routes

descriptions.value: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, Nuxt parses a request path beginning with // as a URL host before rendering a page, while Nitro server/middleware and routeRules continue to evaluate the original path. An unauthenticated request such as //x/admin can therefore resolve to the /admin page without route-scoped serverHandlers, server/middleware path checks, redirects, or security headers configured for /admin. API handlers in server/api and server/routes, appMiddleware, page middleware are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

cna.title: AIOHTTP: Unbounded cookie storage in client CookieJar

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, Set-Cookie parsing treats unrecognized name=value attributes as additional cookies, while CookieJar does not limit the number of cookies stored or sent. A malicious server can make an aiohttp client accumulate a very large cookie set, consume memory and CPU repeatedly across redirects, and construct an excessively large Cookie header for later requests to the same domain. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: AES key schedule not cleared by the TinyCrypt AES-CTR backend in MCUboot bootutil

descriptions.value:
When MCUboot is built with the TinyCrypt crypto backend (MCUBOOT_USE_TINYCRYPT), bootutil_aes_ctr_drop() in boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/aes_ctr_tinycrypt.h was an empty stub. The AES-CTR context for this backend is the fully expanded AES-128 key schedule (struct tc_aes_key_sched_struct). Generic code relies on this hook to release and clear key state, so with TinyCrypt nothing was cleared. The mbedTLS and PSA backends do free or destroy their key state here.

As a result, boot_state_clear(), which boot_go() calls before handing off to the application, left the image's AES content-encryption key schedule in the static boot_data state. This is the case after an encrypted upgrade in single-image builds, where boot_enc_zeroize() is not called. boot_decrypt_key() likewise left the ECIES-derived key-encryption key schedule on the stack. The affected build uses MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES with TinyCrypt, which is the default ECDSA and Ed25519 backend in the Zephyr port.

The first AES-128 round key equals the cipher key, so anyone who can read the leftover bootloader RAM after boot can recover the image content key and decrypt that encrypted image. That includes a physical attacker with debug or RAM access, or code later running on the device. This weakens image-encryption key confidentiality (and so the confidentiality of the encrypted image's plaintext). The device's long-term private decryption key is not exposed, and image authenticity is not affected. The fix wipes the context with bootutil_wipe_memory().

cna.title: AIOHTTP: Event loop stall in add_domain() wildcard matching

descriptions.value: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, Application.add_domain() converts every asterisk wildcard in a domain mask into a greedy regular-expression fragment, so a mask containing two or more wildcards can take polynomial time to reject a long Host header that does not match. A remote attacker can repeatedly send such headers to a server configured with a multi-wildcard domain mask and stall the event loop. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

cna.title: OpenTelemetry JavaScript: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File and Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http

descriptions.value: OpenTelemetry JavaScript is the OpenTelemetry JavaScript client. From 0.204.0 until 0.222.0, @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http writes the raw query string from incoming HTTP requests to the url.query server-span attribute without applying the redactedQueryParams protection used for outgoing spans. Services receiving signed URLs or other credentials in query parameters can therefore export still-valid secrets to tracing backends, where observability infrastructure and users with span-read access may read them. The redactedQueryParams option does not protect incoming spans in affected versions. This issue is fixed in version 0.222.0.

The application fails to regenerate the session identifier (PHPSESSID) upon successful authentication. cna.title: russh try_sign: asynchronous confirmation can sign after agent lock

descriptions.value: russh is a Rust SSH client and server library that includes an SSH agent protocol implementation. Prior to version 0.65.1, try_sign() captures an Arc<PrivateKey> before awaiting Agent::confirm() and does not revalidate the shared lock state or key presence after the await. This is a distinct residual defect in the remediation for CVE-2026-116794. A peer, including a remote SSH server using agent forwarding, can begin a confirmation-constrained signature request while the agent is unlocked and receive the signature after another connection locks the agent if the stale confirmation returns true. New post-lock requests are rejected and private key material is not disclosed, but the pending operation bypasses the current lock state. This issue is fixed in version 0.65.1.
